chapters.title: Chapter 501: Going Back To Caprath City
paragraphs: "We managed to get everything from Tier 3 to Tier 6 herbs. However, Tier 7 is limited, so we couldn’t get the quantity you are after.
Also, not everything on the list was in stock," the lady said to Kent, handing him a storage ring.
"However, you can visit Lanky City in the Eldorath Kingdom. There is an herb store famous for selling high-tier herbs," she recommended, and Kent could only nod.
Not that he was disappointed. This was rather perfect for him, as he would have more places to visit with Vexthra.
"Here is the payment," Kent said, handing over the pouch containing the spirit stones, which had already reached hundreds of millions.
"It was Nice doing business with you. We look forward to seeing you again." The lady said, and Kent and Vexthra nodded and left the room.
The moment they appeared back inside the large space in the store, several eyes locked on them, bringing a smirk to Kent’s face.
’Looks like we have some hungry tigers on our trail. How should we handle them?’ Vexthra asked through their connection.

’In case you’re unaware, you’re basically a mortal here, so there’s not going to be a "we"—there’s only "I," my little demon.’ Kent chuckled, and Vexthra tightened her grip on his arm, causing the brat to smile through the pain.
’Let’s just go get dinner. That will help me determine how to deal with them’ Kent said, leading Vexthra out of the herb store.
The moment they stepped outside, both Kent and Vexthra felt several powerful presences begin to follow them.

Kent ignored them, let Vexthra into their carriage, and left the store. They were still being followed since the news of Vexthra taking out a pseudo-mystical technique book had already spread everywhere.

"These people just don’t learn," Kent sighed. "Initially, I thought perhaps they only tried to steal my stuff, knowing I was weak compared to them. But even after killing quite a few, they just switch targets.
"I wonder when they’ll learn their lesson and stop coveting things that don’t belong to them."
Vexthra shook her head, hearing Kent’s words.

"Greed is something everybody has. It isn’t just in this medium world—even the high, immortal, and god worlds are the same. Their greed usually compels them to go after things that don’t belong to them.
"The only way to stop them is by showing them you can keep the treasure you own. They won’t stop until they learn it the hard way. Naturally, that involves killing."
She chuckled and then continued, "Back when I first ascended to the stage of an immortal, I had a situation where a True Immortal—someone two realms above me—wanted to take something I owned.
Naturally, I was no match, so I peacefully gave it to him and avoided death. However, when I became capable enough, guess what happened?" she asked with an evil smile.
"You went and got beaten, huh?"
"You..." Vexthra smacked the back of Kent’s head. Kent is such a brat who can make everything funny, regardless of how serious the situation is.

"What I’m saying is, the world of cultivation is full of people who covet others’ treasures. If you’re too weak to hold on to your treasure, you can only give it away peacefully and pray they don’t kill you afterward.
And in case you manage to walk away, become strong and go for what is rightfully yours. You can’t always have it easy, but don’t fight unnecessary battles."
"Thanks for your wise words, my goddess. However, in this world, the person who can threaten me hasn’t arrived yet. Meaning, I will protect you from all harm regardless of how dangerous it is."
"As for my treasures, may the god of greed have mercy on their souls."
"You do know he exists, right?" Vexthra said
"Even better. And don’t worry, I will protect you while you are practically a god with no abilities," Kent laughed.
Vexthra smiled behind her veil. The fact that a mere mortal said he would protect her—while it sounded ridiculous—was oddly comforting. She indeed needed his protection.
Not that mortal weapons could kill her, even if she sat there and let them bombard her with attacks from all directions.
But that would be suspicious, so she was under Kent’s protection to preserve her secret and avoid using her god powers, which would be very bad for her and everyone.
After half an hour, Kent and Vexthra stopped at an inn to grab a bite before leaving for their next destination, which, in this case, was Lanky City for the rest of the herbs.
The book had a private table.
"It’s been a long time since I did something like this," Vexthra said, sitting behind their offered table.
"Enjoy it, for this is your life now. You eat mortal food and wear mortal clothes."

The experience was new to Vexthra, for it had indeed been a long time since she left the mortal realm. But this was all she wanted, so while she wasn’t really benefiting from it, the experience was indeed something many gods would ask for.
Of course, most gods create avatars to live through their mortal days again. But she was privileged to have this experience in her true body.
That is not something even a god can brag about.
A few minutes later, they were served, and they started digging in. Kent relaxed and waited to see if Vexthra could use the chopsticks.
However, he was taken aback when she used them flawlessly.
"What do you take me for?" she smirked.

"While you’ve been lazing around here, I’ve learned a lot of things. And since I did it before, it just came back to me. Plus, I am a god, so don’t expect me not to be able to do something as simple as using chopsticks."
Kent laughed, and for the next hour, they had their fair share of what they ordered. After dining, they relaxed for a few minutes before leaving.
However, when they were exiting the inn, Kent overheard a conversation that made his blood run cold.
"Have you heard? Somebody is killing all those who worked for that merchant family in Caprath City—the one that was wiped out overnight."
"Wait, so the strange killings... the victims were once workers from the Alderford Family?" someone asked.
"Yes. People are saying the brat that the four kingdoms are after is dating one of the daughters of the Alderford merchant family."
"Who would do something like this?"
Kent pulled Vexthra back into the private room they had just left when he heard what the people were talking about.
"Change of plans. We’re going to Caprath City."
They vanished into the tower and almost instantly appeared somewhere closer to Caprath City.

chapters.title: Chapter 502: The Most Incredibly Powerful Tower In the Universe
paragraphs: "Kent, what’s going on?" Vexthra asked the moment they appeared, about four miles away from Caprath City.
"Someone is killing people who used to work in Elsa’s family."
"What?" Vexthra’s gaze turned cold, hearing Kent’s response.
She had to hold herself back from releasing any of her aura, but she became very angry upon hearing something like this.
Elsa is her sister, and so the people who once worked for her are like family to her. Hearing that they are being killed made her furious.
But her fury couldn’t rival Kent’s. As angry as he was, he had to relax and analyse the situation well.
"Relax. We will better understand what is happening when we get to Caprath City." He retrieved the carriage that the tower had taken away when they left Vastport City.
Naturally, the people keeping an eye on them were taken aback when the carriage suddenly vanished. They are all scouring the city to find them while they are thousands of miles away.
Kent and Vexthra entered the carriage and left for Caprath City. A couple of minutes later, they came into view of the city gate, which at first sight made Kent’s eyes flash with killing intent.
At the city gate were two bodies, stripped of their clothes, cut in more than a hundred places, and hanging by the neck.
He immediately recognized one of them even from afar.
Back when he arrived in this world, some guards were sent to pick his master up when Lilian was poisoned. One of the people hanging was part of the guards who came to pick him up.
He was one of the people he interacted with when he first came to this world. So seeing his lifeless body hanging, his killing intent exploded.
’I am going to kill every last one of them,’ Kent vowed in his heart and turned to Vexthra.
"You have to go back to the tower. I will be using my original face from here onwards, so staying with me will make people notice you. Don’t worry, I will be careful."
Vexthra didn’t argue because she knew what he said was sound. His current appearance would allow him to enter any city without drawing trouble.
So if she was seen with his Kent form, people would suspect him when he turned back to Jest.
"Just be careful... There are many powerful people hidden in this world." Vexthra kissed him and vanished into the tower.
Kent took a deep sigh, then turned back to his real form. His gaze turned icy as lightning danced around his body.
At the city gate, both those entering and exiting stopped and turned toward the two bodies hanging at the entrance. On their chests, the mark of a claw could be seen.

"How unfortunate to die for someone else’s mistake," one of the travelers entering the city said, shaking his head. He knew what was happening because a rumor had already started spreading everywhere.
"It’s indeed unfortunate. However, what else can we do?" another replied, shaking their head as they went inside the city.

At the entrance, there were twelve guards, each clad in the same black armor as those at Vastport City. Clearly, the king’s guards were everywhere, and from the look of things, they were all working together.
Suddenly, a figure appeared in the air, bathed in lightning. With his arrival, two powerful sword arcs left his sword, cutting the ropes of the two dead bodies.
Kent appeared below and caught their bodies, preventing them from hitting the ground.
This sudden action drew countless eyes as people began gathering. Naturally, the guards who witnessed it surrounded Kent and drew their weapons.
"Identify yourself," one of the guards said, but before he could finish his sentence, a dark shard shot from the ground and pierced his neck, killing him instantly.
This act caused everyone to step back in panic; however, Kent didn’t even lift his head. Instead, he retrieved two pieces of cloth and gently covered the bodies before storing them in the tower.
Slowly, he stood up and turned toward the strongest among the King’s guards—a peak Sovereign.
"Speak," Kent said in a commanding tone. When the crowd recognized him, more powerful presences began appearing in the surroundings.
The one they are searching for has appeared...
"You’re Kent," the leader of the King’s guard said, pointing his weapon at Kent. He recognised him because his image is everywhere.
He is quite famous...
"Under the command of the King of the Althea Kingdom, I command you to surre—"
"Die."
Kent’s voice cut him off, freezing the leader of the King’s guards mid-sentence. Like a candle snuffed out, his face turned pale, and then he dropped dead.
Kent didn’t spare him a glance as he turned toward the next guard.
"Speak," he said again in the same commanding tone. But like the leader before him, the guard chose to raise his weapon and even attempted to charge at Kent.
Kent’s gaze turned icy. He raised his sword, and in the next instant, a powerful bolt of light shot out, blasting a hole through the man’s head.
Then he turned to the next. This time, instead of asking, he went straight for the kill, uttering a chilling line that made everyone present take several steps back.
"Why talk to the living when I can extract what I want from the dead?"
The nine remaining guards couldn’t even react as powerful, piercing shards shot up from the ground, killing all of them instantly.
Under everyone’s gaze, Kent walked over to the leader he had killed moments ago and used Soul Absorb on him, temporarily absorbing his memories.
The Soul Absorb skill allows him to temporary extract the memories of those he killed less than 5 minutes ago.
So he extracted their memories.
"Huh," he muttered as he sifted through them, finding exactly what he was looking for.
’Gaia, can the tower locate all those who worked for Elsa?’ Kent asked after finding what he was after.
⟪Yes, Master.⟫
’Locate all of them, Tower.’ Kent gave the command, and three million tower points were deducted. In that instant, the tower located every last one of them.
⟪Tracking complete. 134 located. Alive: 120, Dead: 14⟫
’Transport all of them to the Tower City,’ he ordered again. This time, ten million tower points were taken.
Across the four kingdoms, 120 people and 14 corpses suddenly vanished, leaving behind confusion and panic. Some were in the middle of conversations or daily routines, unaware that danger was looming.
Thankfully, their invisible guardian got to them before the hunters could.
⟪Transportation complete.⟫ the tower responded.
’Now, locate and tag everyone involved in these killings. I want their names, locations, ranks, ages, and hobbies.’
Within seconds, Kent was presented with a tall list of everyone he had to eliminate.
Turning to his right, he vanished and reappeared in front of an old man in the crowd, silently observing everything.
Before the man could make a sound, his head rolled to the ground.
Kent moved again, and dozens of heads followed before anyone could comprehend what was happening. They died not knowing how he had located them.
"What is going on?" someone asked, but Kent slashed his sword at the city gate instead of an answer, bringing the entire entrance down in a single stroke.
Suddenly, mocking laughter echoed through the area.
"How amusing... Looks like she didn’t call me out for no reason."
Up in the sky, a figure wielding a scythe, clad in dark, tattered robes, appeared, smiling at Kent.

chapters.title: Chapter 503: Giving Them Residence
paragraphs: "You are," Kent said, staring at the figure that appeared in the air with a calm expression. It’s a man who, although he isn’t that old, doesn’t look young either.
His looks are twisted, befitting someone who isn’t blessed with good looks. Hearing Kent’s question, the figure chose to entertain him.

"Very well. Since you’re the one who managed to make an entire organization that has existed for thousands of years go to such lengths and ask for my help, I don’t mind telling you my name—and just how screwed you are."
The laughter coming from the man was twisted, revealing how incredibly evil he was.

The people who were still processing Kent’s sudden appearance—and the fact that he had slaughtered nearly forty people in under a minute—felt their energy drain as they stood near Kent and the newcomer.
They began to back away, realizing that whatever was happening wasn’t something they could afford to stay close to.

Kent held his gaze on the man, who seemed to have found a new prey to toy with. Kent asked for his name only so he wouldn’t mind making his presence known once again to the people of Myrathis (Human Continent).
He was once a menace that went silent several years ago. Now, he is back to hunt Kent...
"I am—"
"You know what, I don’t care who you are." Before the figure could mention his name, Kent cut him off, and a chilling cold filled the air.
The man clearly didn’t like getting cut off mid-sentence. But Kent didn’t really care.
"I have a list, and your ugly self isn’t on it. So while I’d love to stay and admire that hideous face of yours, I don’t have the time.
So go back to the cave you crawled out of. You’re scaring everyone just by looking at them." Kent waved his hand at the man and turned to face everyone.
The air grew colder as the words left his lips. The figure in the air was taken aback, but before he could respond, Kent began to speak again.
"There’s a cowardly organization called the Hand that, for some reason, controls your kings and leaders.
They’re in charge of everything, so while you may think you have kings and queens, it’s actually this twisted organization running your affairs.
Normally, I wouldn’t care. But they came after me, and now the people I’ve interacted with from ever since I arrived in this kingdom.
That cannot be forgiven.
So while they try to cover their tracks by branding bodies with a claw, revealing just how pathetic they truly are, I will expose them. And that begins with what will happen from today onwards.
I’m telling you this now so you won’t be surprised if your king, queen, or even your entire royal family were to die overnight. And don’t worry—you’ll know I did it.

Because while I may be just one person, I’ve got more spine than that cowardly organization. I will kill every last one affiliated with them, so while I can say you all are safe, I cannot promise that.
So be ready to die if you have something to do with the Hand and their pathetic self. Spread the word."
Kent turned back to the man, whose face had twisted into an expression of sheer fury.
"They even hired an ugly bastard to come after me, thinking he has what it takes to kill me. How pathetic," Kent chuckled, feeling his surroundings get sealed by an invisible force.
The ugly-looking man wouldn’t let him slip off, no matter what. So he started sealing Kent’s surroundings.

"I would love to wipe that ugliness off your face, but I don’t have time for you now. Maybe use this chance to find a beauty product and fix that disaster. I mean, don’t you ever look at yourself in the mirror?
I am pretty sure you scared your mom to death right after giving birth to you..." Kent chuckled
"Until then, keep scaring people with your smile." Kent gave him the middle finger before vanishing into the tower.
A mere sealing spell from a Level 7 Core Formation expert wouldn’t be able to hold him. He had even canceled an attack from a Spirit Lord—what chance did a Core Formation expert have?
However, while Kent was running his mouth, he knew the ugly-looking man was someone who could threaten him.
He sensed his aura and understood that while the other Core Formation experts he had fought were strong, this one was different.
This one gave off a dangerous feeling that made him remember what Vexthra had said: there were indeed powerful beings hidden in this world.
Not that he was afraid, but like he said, the man wasn’t on his list—because he had checked and double-checked to make sure the Hunter wasn’t included.
The Hand had unleashed a group of killers known as the Shadows on Kent by ordering them to kill everyone connected to him.
In this case, the only people they could think of were those who worked for the Alderford Merchant Family.
Since Kent had taken their daughter—and even her mother—as his women, they assumed he would be hurt, or at least his wives would be, if they found out everyone connected to them had been killed.

They called themselves the Clawed Shadows.

It translated that they came after him but didn’t have the balls to show they were the ones. That was like a bad rap in the underworld.

Though that was a heavy loss, it could’ve been much worse. As far as he was concerned, Kent couldn’t have predicted the attack—no one knew of his involvement with the Alderfords.
The only ones who did were from the Ashlands, and they had all died when the Dark Devil Church visited them—the same night the Hand visited the Alderfords.
So this can only mean, while he wasn’t that known by many, the hand is quite aware of him and all those they can kill to make him tick.

But regardless of what had happened, Kent managed to save the remaining 120. Now, lost in thought and standing silently, the 120 he rescued found themselves inside an ample, unfamiliar space in the Tower City.
"Where are we?" one person asked, recognizing the person beside her. After all, they had once worked for the same family.
"I’m as lost as you are, Theo. I was in the middle of buying a skill book when I was teleported here," a lady replied, holding the skill book in her hand.
"Hope you didn’t pay for that skill book yet," someone else chimed in with a smile, clearly recognizing her.
"But of course. Too bad Old Jace is such a good guy," the lady shook her head. "But seriously, where are we?" she asked again, looking around at the stunning city surrounding them.
"I don’t know, but I think whoever pulled us here might’ve just saved my life," another man joined the conversation, making everyone turn toward him.
"What happened to you, Steve?" Theo asked, staring at the bleeding man. Steve had cuts on his left arm, chest, and leg.
"I was about to be executed when I was suddenly pulled here. And I think all of us would’ve been—if we weren’t teleported into this world."
"What?!" everyone exclaimed after hearing what he just said.
"He’s right. You all were at death’s door, had it not been for me," Kent suddenly appeared in the air, drawing everyone’s attention.

The laughter coming from the man was twisted, revealing how incredibly evil he was.

I will kill every last one affiliated with them, so while I can say you all are safe, I cannot promise that.
So be ready to die if you have something to do with the Hand and their pathetic self.
Spread the word."

chapters.title: Chapter 504: You Are Kent Madson
paragraphs: "You are Kent Madson." The moment Kent spoke, almost everyone recognized him.
But why wouldn’t they? He was basically the most wanted fugitive in all four kingdoms, so everyone recognized him.
"Yes, I am Kent Madson," Kent said to the lady who recognized him.
"Please, why are we here?" Steve, the man who was at death’s door before the tower pulled him away, asked. He walked forward, taking on the role of the leader of the ragtag group.

"You don’t recognize me, huh?" Kent smiled, watching the face of one of the five guards who had come to pick him up in place of his master to examine Lilian’s health when he arrived in the world of Sonox.
Steve narrowed his gaze at Kent, as if trying to recall something. A few seconds later, realization struck him, making him widen his eyes.
"Pill Master Kent," Steve said, making Kent smile. They knew him as an alchemist, so calling him using such a title was only right.
"I am actually a Grandmaster now, but yeah, I am Kent—the same Kent you remember," Kent said, causing the former guard to go on his knees.
"Thank you for saving me, Pill Grandmaster Kent," Steve said, shocking everyone.
Though they knew Kent as someone popular across the four kingdoms, they only saw him as a fugitive thanks to his painting on every mission board.
However, as Steve went down on his knees, three more joined him—the other guards who came to pick Kent up.
"What is going on... Why are you bowing to a fugitive of the four kingdoms?" someone asked, causing Steve to turn and glare at her despite still bleeding.
"You better show your respect, Janet. In case you’re not aware, this is the husband of young Miss Lilian."

Hearing Steve’s words, everyone’s expression changed. Even Kent, who was feeling some tension from the 120 assembled just a second ago, raised his brow when all their looks turned to ones of shock and reverence.
It was like the idea of him being a fugitive was wiped out instantly.
Kent didn’t know that when he gave Lilian and her mom the large sum of spirit stones to use as a farewell gift to the workers, Lilian had made everyone aware it was from her fiancé.
And while a billion was nothing to him back then, when shared among 136 people, it was enough to secure their futures for thousands of years.
So, while they were mere workers back then, earning only a couple of spirit stones every month, they became rich men and women when they were sent away from the Alderford Mansion.
This made them forever thankful to the Alderfords and Kent.
So, hearing he was the one who changed their lives, they couldn’t help but feel grateful.
"No need for any of this. You are all here because a danger that was aimed at me was redirected toward you. I am sorry for that.
To prevent further danger to your lives, I brought you here to stay for now. I will handle the threat on the outside, and when I deem everything safe, you can leave and live your lives freely again."
Kent didn’t lie to them. This was indeed his doing for the reason they were in danger was because the Hand want to make him tick.
So he told them the truth. However, he was surprised to see them not show any sign of hostility when they found out he was the cause of their predicament.
"Pill Grandmaster Kent, if you don’t mind me asking a question," Steve asked, looking up at Kent.
"Go ahead—and you can just call me Kent."

"I don’t think I can. You are my young miss’s husband. Calling you by your first name feels disrespectful, so allow me to call you Young Master Kent if you insist," Steve said, and almost everyone there nodded in agreement.
"Whatever makes you happy. In any case, ask your question," Kent said, maintaining his calm expression.
"Is the young miss with you? And how is she faring?" Steve asked.
"She is fine. She is here with her mother, but they are both in seclusion, cultivating," Kent responded. Steve and the others sighed in relief upon hearing that Lilian and her mother were safe.
Though they no longer worked for them, they were happy knowing their benefactors were living well, despite their entire family having been razed to the ground.
"Since the young miss is here, I’ve decided not to live here again. I will resume my service to the young miss," Steve declared with unwavering determination.
"You really don’t have to. Your young miss is in no danger, and while you’d be showing your loyalty by choosing to serve her again, you should live your life to the fullest.
That was what she wanted for all of you when she let you go after the attack," Kent said—but he could tell the man wouldn’t listen to him.

"I don’t have any life on the outside anyway. I spent my entire life serving in the Alderford Mansion, and now that I can again, I won’t hesitate. Please allow me to have this," Steve said, almost pleading.
Kent stared at him for a few seconds before a sigh escaped his lips.

"Fine. However, you cannot leave after you choose to stay. So, all those who want to stay and continue serving your young miss, step to the left." Every last one of them was on the left in under a second.
Kent was taken aback. However, what he wasn’t aware of was that all these people had spent almost their entire lives serving Lilian’s family.
So, when they were sent away, making a living for themselves became something they struggled with.
Now, given a second chance, they would rather stay in this lush city than go back out there. Who wouldn’t want to live in such a place anyway?
"I will be leaving now. My assistants will come to help you settle in. If you need anything or have anyone you’d like to bring here, let them know, and they’ll make it happen.
Basically, listen to what they say, and you’ll be fine. I’ll return when I’m done with my business."
Kent vanished before any of them could thank him and appeared in the mountain garden, where Vexthra and the three lolis stood, gazing at the 120 new residents in the tower city.
⟪I scanned their memories, Master. None of them holds any animosity toward you. They truly want to serve⟫, Dori said to Kent the moment he appeared in the garden.
"Thank you, Dori," he said, walking toward Vexthra.

chapters.title: Chapter 505: Qi’lan Crystal
paragraphs: "Sorry for cutting our outing short," Kent said, holding Vexthra’s waist as he pulled her closer to him. He leaned in and kissed her lips.
"It’s nothing. You have something important to deal with, and like I said, I don’t want to stand in the way of your business. So finish it quickly and get back here.
I still have two days to spend on the outside, and I won’t allow some pest to get in the way of that." Vexthra wrapped her arm around Kent’s neck as she kissed him.
⟪Ahem... Some of us are underage, so you might want to cut the public display of affection short⟫, Gaia said, causing Vexthra to break the kiss with red cheeks.
Though she was a goddess, getting embarrassed wasn’t beyond her, especially when it came to matters of the heart.
Kent turned and looked at Gaia, who was grinning at him.
"You sly demon loli."
Kent kissed Vexthra one last time before looking toward the city.

"Gaia, ensure they have everything they want. They are now residents here, and since they are willing to serve, let them. Also, add them to the servant tower." Kent gave Gaia her assignment and then turned to Akira.
Since they will be living there forever, they must contribute to Kent’s strength. Since he is making them stay for free, the stats they offer him will go a long way.

"They don’t really have much use here, so help them with their spirit roots and cultivation techniques. If possible, give them good classes. Once I bind the dungeons to the tower, they will have a way to train more effectively.
Of course, I’ll pay for your service when I get money, so put it on my tab."
⟪Okay, master. But don’t hold your tab for too long, or I’ll be pissed—and you won’t like me when I’m pissed off⟫
"I can already picture a small face like that of a monkey in a painting," Kent laughed, causing Akira to shrug and take out a paintbrush and a scroll.
She set it down and started painting. Kent looked at all this with a puzzled expression.
"What are you doing?" he asked.

"She is creating a cultivation realm where people can enter and cultivate. It’s like one of those secret domains where you can fight over ancient cultivation techniques and rare treasures or pass trials to obtain.
Only this time, she is creating them uniquely for the residents in the tower."
Vexthra explained, staring at Akira’s painting, which was actually her weaving. It was one of the many ways she weaves.
"Okay, I guess," Kent said, then turned to Dori.
"Help them come to terms with their new world and life." Dori nodded.

"Then I will be leaving for now." He waved goodbye and vanished, appearing in the Legion Tower where Zareth, alongside Kaizo, Sylara, Vaelros, Veydris, Saden, and the three Soul Sentinels, were waiting for him.
"How was your mission?" Kent asked.
"We have done eight dungeons before you called," Zareth responded.
"Then, how about unlocking the skill? Have you made some progress?"
"Yes. I awakened one skill after clearing six dungeons. However, just that one is enough, considering it’s already too much to fathom," Zareth replied, looking rather enthusiastic.

The main reason Kent gave them the mission to clear the dungeons was so he could gather enough material to conduct a ritual that would unlock some of the skills that once belonged to the World Serpent.
"I also managed to strengthen the Coil Dragon Spirit and the Alabaster Poison Serpent Spirit, so from now on, I can summon the two for one hour every day.
Their strengths have also reached a level I can’t estimate yet.
But I am confident that the time will be extended further when we are done with all twelve dungeons," Zareth added, and Kent nodded.
"Looks like you gained a lot." Kent turned to the rest of his undead and asked,
"How about you guys? Did you gain something?"
"It’s about the battle experience for me, so while I didn’t earn anything, I most certainly had fun punching some bastards," Kaizo said, as usual, beating his chest.
Kent could tell Kaizo had indeed had fun. This made him realize he shouldn’t let them laze around in the tower if he had pending missions. They seem to enjoy doing missions.
"I also had fun, and I managed to get the hearts of some powerful creatures. I just want to keep going since the dungeons aren’t as simple as we thought.
By the time we are done, I am sure I will be a step closer to having a breakthrough through" Vaelros, the chain brute fighter, said.
Sylara was next to speak, "Though I managed to get gallons of blood, I realized fighting inside the dungeon is much more entertaining and dangerous.
However, it wasn’t the kind of danger you run from. I had fun, and I would love to keep going." Sylara wasn’t far behind with her own experience.
Though Kent didn’t know if she was being serious about enjoying the danger, not that he expected anything less from an undead like Sylara, who enjoys torture more than a game of chess.
Saden and the three Soul Sentinels clearly appeared to want to join them, but Kent would not give them an answer for now. They had a new mission, and that must be handled first.
"Well, I don’t plan on keeping you for long. It seems your mission is going quite well, so I’ll make this short." Kent retrieved six token tablets from his space ring and handed them out.
Zareth, Kaizo, Sylara, and Vaelros each got one, while Saden and Nyxira got one, and the other two Soul Sentinels, Kael and Kaelion, also received one.
"Inside each crystal is a list of names and images bearing their real-time locations. Your mission is simple: locate them and eliminate every last name on the list."
The command was simple, yet the impact would be felt by everyone.
Kaizo and the rest of his teammates nodded at Kent’s words. They knew he wouldn’t give them this mission if it wasn’t of the utmost importance.
"Also, read their thoughts whenever you kill them. I want to connect the dots from them. We will eradicate them from the root this time, not just kill the branches."
"Okay, Master."
"Before we leave, there is something we have for you." Kaizo retrieved a head-sized black crystal that immediately filled the space with thick spiritual qi.
"We found it when we defeated a certain floor boss." Kent received the crystal and appraised it. What he saw made his eyes widen.
⟪Name: Qi’lan Crystal⟫
→ A crystal created from the core of a powerful spirit beast.
→ Its use is to absorb the spiritual qi in the air and purify it to its highest concentration.
→ Every last strand of energy absorbed from it is the purest form it can be.
[Current Capacity: 12,000,000/670,000,000 Spiritual Qi]
"Damn..."

"We have done eight dungeons before you called," Zareth responded.
"Then, how about unlocking the skill?
Have you made some progress?"
"Yes.
I awakened one skill after clearing six dungeons.
However, just that one is enough, considering it’s already too much to fathom," Zareth replied, looking rather enthusiastic.

The main reason Kent gave them the mission to clear the dungeons was so he could gather enough material to conduct a ritual that would unlock some of the skills that once belonged to the World Serpent.
"I also managed to strengthen the Coil Dragon Spirit and the Alabaster Poison Serpent Spirit, so from now on, I can summon the two for one hour every day.
Their strengths have also reached a level I can’t estimate yet.
But I am confident that the time will be extended further when we are done with all twelve dungeons," Zareth added, and Kent nodded.
"Looks like you gained a lot." Kent turned to the rest of his undead and asked,
"How about you guys?
Did you gain something?"
"It’s about the battle experience for me, so while I didn’t earn anything, I most certainly had fun punching some bastards," Kaizo said, as usual, beating his chest.
Kent could tell Kaizo had indeed had fun.
This made him realize he shouldn’t let them laze around in the tower if he had pending missions.
They seem to enjoy doing missions.
"I also had fun, and I managed to get the hearts of some powerful creatures.
I just want to keep going since the dungeons aren’t as simple as we thought.
By the time we are done, I am sure I will be a step closer to having a breakthrough through" Vaelros, the chain brute fighter, said.
Sylara was next to speak, "Though I managed to get gallons of blood, I realized fighting inside the dungeon is much more entertaining and dangerous.
However, it wasn’t the kind of danger you run from.
I had fun, and I would love to keep going." Sylara wasn’t far behind with her own experience.
Though Kent didn’t know if she was being serious about enjoying the danger, not that he expected anything less from an undead like Sylara, who enjoys torture more than a game of chess.
Saden and the three Soul Sentinels clearly appeared to want to join them, but Kent would not give them an answer for now.
They had a new mission, and that must be handled first.
"Well, I don’t plan on keeping you for long.
It seems your mission is going quite well, so I’ll make this short." Kent retrieved six token tablets from his space ring and handed them out.
Zareth, Kaizo, Sylara, and Vaelros each got one, while Saden and Nyxira got one, and the other two Soul Sentinels, Kael and Kaelion, also received one.
"Inside each crystal is a list of names and images bearing their real-time locations.
Your mission is simple: locate them and eliminate every last name on the list."
The command was simple, yet the impact would be felt by everyone.
Kaizo and the rest of his teammates nodded at Kent’s words.
They knew he wouldn’t give them this mission if it wasn’t of the utmost importance.
"Also, read their thoughts whenever you kill them.
I want to connect the dots from them.
We will eradicate them from the root this time, not just kill the branches."
"Okay, Master."
"Before we leave, there is something we have for you." Kaizo retrieved a head-sized black crystal that immediately filled the space with thick spiritual qi.
"We found it when we defeated a certain floor boss." Kent received the crystal and appraised it.
What he saw made his eyes widen.
⟪Name: Qi’lan Crystal⟫
→ A crystal created from the core of a powerful spirit beast.
→ Its use is to absorb the spiritual qi in the air and purify it to its highest concentration.
→ Every last strand of energy absorbed from it is the purest form it can be.
[Current Capacity: 12,000,000/670,000,000 Spiritual Qi]
"Damn..."

chapters.title: Chapter 506: Solo Leveling
paragraphs: "We found it in the Orc Dungeon when we defeated the Orc Chieftain, the last floor boss.
It was a rather interesting battle, considering the orc was quite powerful for a Peak Sovereign," Kaizo said, noticing Kent’s intrigue with the crystal he gave him.
In contrast to Kent’s expression, the crystal in his hand was much more powerful than he let on. The crystal could store spiritual qi and purify it, allowing one to absorb it.
The fact that it purifies the stored energy is enough to show how invaluable it is. Then there’s the part where he can absorb the stored energy.
The capacity is enough to make it valuable even when he becomes immortal.
Naturally, Gaia has already started sniffing it, knowing she could upgrade it. But even without upgrades, it’s incredibly valuable.

The energy in the Tower is very pure; however, even with Kent’s robust cultivation technique and cultivation speed, he still wouldn’t be able to absorb the spirit qi in the air as fast as he could from the crystal.
This means the crystal is perfect for someone looking to level up faster. Kent needed one, considering his strength was still at the 8th level of the Root Great Sage stage.
Though his current form after breaking his first limitation has moved past the sovereign stage, he still needs to raise his cultivation base.
This means the Qu’lan crystal came at the right time.
"How powerful was this Orc Chieftain?" Kent asked. He didn’t really understand these things about dungeons, especially since he hadn’t even bound them to the tower after receiving the eight prompts.
He had been too busy to get into that. But now, he seemed to have found a fascination for it, considering such a powerful treasure was found in one.
It wasn’t just about knowing more about the orc; it was more about learning the nature of the dungeon, starting with the Orc Chieftain.

"That bastard was a seriously powerful master. He wielded a Great Axe, and while I could beat my chest and say I could solo him even if I were sitting at the peak of the Ascension stage, that would be a lie.
Even Zareth had to go all out just so he and Veydris could take him down. In fact, all eight last-floor bosses we faced weren’t easy." Kaizo smiles, looking at Kent’s expression.
"And yes, the Orc wasn’t the strongest of the eight we’ve faced. Makes me wonder what’s waiting for us in the remaining four."
Kent raised his brow, and from the expression on Zareth’s face, he could tell Kaizo was exaggerating.
Zareth is one incredibly powerful undead, so for someone like him to need Veydris’s help and still have to go all out to face one person, he could on wonder what this Orc was made of.
"Even Zareth had to go all out. Then I’d better bind the dungeons and summon the last floor bosses. Who knows what will become of my legion once they join?"

"You should do that, Master. We need the dungeons for training. Though we are awesome, we aren’t that strong, if you ask me." Kaizo shot straight, making his master aware that they needed training spaces.
"I will do that," Kent said with a sigh. "Now, take these branding tools. Brand any of the names on the list whenever you kill them."
Kent handed a branding tool to his undead.
"Veydris, your mission is to keep this ugly bastard in sight for the next two days. Feel free to sever at least a hand if he does anything stupid, and you can go ahead and carve on his face."
After everything was done, the team left. They each had their own way of traveling, so going to the four kingdoms wasn’t a headache.
However, the moment they left, Kent appeared inside the Soul Tower and sat down on the soul stone, taking out the crystal.
"Time to level up." A smile appeared on his face as he activated his cultivation technique. Though he had so far relied on his ladies to level up, that didn’t mean he couldn’t cultivate on his own.
His cultivation technique was rather robust. So while he enjoyed having sex with his women to level up, he could indeed cultivate on his own.
The technique was activated, and the spiritual qi in the Qi’lan crystal started entering his body. Kent sat quietly, his eyes closed, as the energy flowed into him.
Just six minutes into cultivation, a message appeared in his view showing he had leveled up.
⟪You’ve Leveled Up: Level 9 Root Great Sage⟫
Kent didn’t stop there. Instead, he continued, and before long, a new message appeared.
⟪You’ve Leveled Up: Level 1 Root Transcendent⟫
Kent felt a powerful energy enter his body, showing he was no longer a Root Great Sage but had moved to a different stage, several times stronger than the previous.
This meant his strength had already reached levels he couldn’t measure yet. But that wasn’t enough, so Kent continued cultivating the stored spiritual energy in the Qi’lan Crystal.
⟪You’ve Leveled Up: Level 1 Root Transcendent⟫
⟪You’ve Leveled Up: Level 2 Root Transcendent⟫
⟪You’ve Leveled Up: Level 3 Root Transcendent⟫
⟪You’ve Leveled Up: Level 4 Root Transcendent⟫
⟪You’ve Leveled Up: Level 9 Root Transcendent⟫
Five hours later, he had progressed to the peak of the Transcendent stage, making him grin from ear to ear.
He knew he wasn’t in danger, considering his physique, cultivation technique, and the tower were all working to keep him in shape.
But even if those weren’t enough to stabilize and strengthen his foundation, his body cultivation was there.
As a body cultivator, the chances of rapid leveling affecting him were slim. And since he was absorbing the purest form of spiritual qi, his foundation was as firm as possible.
He is also a dragon with a Celestial Grade Spirit Root. These factors alone make him the perfect person to use the Qu’lan Crystal. And he wasn’t being polite about that.
Thus, Kent didn’t stop and continued to absorb until the message he had been waiting for appeared.
⟪You’ve Leveled Up: Level 1 Root Ascension⟫
"It’s almost drained." Kent scanned the crystal and knew it was nearing depletion, so he drained it completely. Since he broke a limit, the spiritual Qi needed to level up was also on a new level.
⟪You’ve Leveled Up: Level 1 Root Ascension⟫
⟪You’ve Leveled Up: Level 2 Root Ascension⟫
⟪You’ve Leveled Up: Level 3 Root Ascension⟫
Thankfully, that brought him to the third level, enough to tell him he had become a monster from this rapid level-up.
"It’s time to complete these missions. I wouldn’t want them running with their tails between their legs." Kent stood up, leaving the crystal on the ground.
For his next breakthrough, he needed to absorb more spiritual qi, and since the tower had a much denser spiritual qi, he left it there.

"Then again, hiding won’t save them—not when I have the strongest tracking system in the universe inside my soul." An evil smile appeared on his face as his clothing transformed, taking on a new look.
He was clad in black from head to toe.
"May the stars have mercy on their souls." Saying that, he vanished from the Tower and appeared somewhere in Vastport City.

chapters.title: Chapter 507: The Grim Massacre
paragraphs: Kent appeared atop a particular five-star hotel.
It was one of the hotels he had stayed in during the annual auction, so he left a marker there, allowing him to stand at its peak and overlook the vast expanse of buildings below him.
It was around 6 p.m., and the sun was almost set.
The moment he emerged, he pulled up his status window and looked at his stats...
Name: Kent
Age: 18
Bloodline: Primordial Chaos Dragon
Class: Alchemist (Grandmaster)
SubClass:
⟪ Swordsman [Grandmaster] ⟫
⟪ Soul Cultivation [Tier 10] ⟫
⟪ Body Cultivator [Gold] ⟫
Cultivation: Root Ascension - Lvl 3/9
⟦ STATs ⟧
Physical Strength: 137,650
Physical Agility: 138,260
Physical Stamina: 137,625
Spiritual Strength: 442,275
Mental Strength: 154,665
[Attribute Points: 543,000]
[Tower Points: 41, 100,000]
[Skill Upgrade Points: 211,100]
"At this rate, I can already tell even a Level 8 Core Formation expert can’t handle a slap from me," Kent laughed, exaggerating his strength.
But while it was indeed on a level even he couldn’t measure, he knew Core Formation experts—or at least the ones he had met—wouldn’t be able to do anything to him.
His stats had shot up to this stage due to two factors. The first was that his body had entered the Gold Rank, making him several times more powerful.
This affected the stats he earned after every level-up.
The second was the limit he had broken. It was like opening a whole different window for him. And while he could tell he was close to breaking the second limit, he wasn’t confident yet.
However, he had indeed become a monster worth fearing, and now, this tiger wasn’t even done.
"Gaia, kindly add 100,000 points to Strength, Agility, Stamina, Mental, and 143,000 to Soul Strength," Kent gave the order, and Gaia did as she was told.

The moment the points were added, Kent took the soul bead from his space ring and decided to use it, considering Vexthra was now inside the Tower, and he no longer needed the bead to power the compass since he could easily do it with his soul essence.

He shattered the bead and let the essence flow into him. It contained about 500,000 soul essence, and since he was nearing the Tier 11 stage, the moment all 500,000 entered, the message he had longed to see appeared.
"Finally, I’ve entered the 11th Tier," Kent smirked, feeling his soul strength grow several times monstrous.
He then spread his superior soul over the city, scanning every hidden spot worth searching.
After a few minutes, he retracted his soul energy and decided to greet those destined to die soon. He blinked away, heading to his first location.
Several individuals could be seen dining and talking inside a particular inn as they spent their evening. The air inside the inn was very lively, making almost everyone laugh now and then.
It was the Dawn Dinner Inn, one of the hotspots in Vastport City.
Many went there to eat, but when Kent stepped through the gate, it became a place where many would witness the chilling side of an angry dragon who was a step away from unleashing chaos everywhere.
When Kent stepped through the gates, bringing his presence with him, everyone quieted down and instinctively turned in his direction.
"Salutations," Kent said, waving at everyone.

"I am Kent Madson. Yes, that Kent Madson. However, I didn’t come to introduce myself or dine with you all. I am merely here to kill this guy, that guy, that one, and this one," Kent pointed at four figures who immediately went for their weapons.
However, before they could draw them, Kent spoke:
"Stop breathing."
Under the agonizing gaze of everyone, the four figures tried their best to resist, but they could only hold on for a few seconds before their eyes rolled backward and they fell down, dead.
Kent waved his hand and collected their bodies, bringing them outside. Then his sword came out of the sheath, swinging a few times in the air.
Three words were left on the four bodies when it went back inside the sheath:
"Fuck the Hand"
Kent retrieved a pouch and threw it to the innkeeper. "Sorry for the inconvenience." With that, he vanished and appeared several kilometers away. He came and went like the wind, silent and deadly.
The same thing happened in the next place we went. He walked into a restaurant and told five people to stop breathing.
After they dropped dead, he branded them and moved to the next. Within 25 minutes, Kent killed close to 30 people in Vastport City alone, and then he left.
In under an hour, news of Kent appearing at random places and killing people spread in Vastport City and started spreading to the nearby cities.
However, it didn’t take long for news to start coming from other cities saying similar things.
Of course, this was all Kaizo and company doing. Kaizo went to Eldorath Kingdom, and within two hours, he visited three cities, killing about 35 people.
Their master was resourceful, so he ensured they had everything they needed. This gave them the means to travel several miles within minutes.
Thankfully, he was long gone before the King’s Guards could close in on him. The last person to kill was dead 15 minutes before the King’s guard made their move.
This was the same in the other three kingdoms. They all wanted the perpetrators dead, but they were one before they could get their hands on them.
Somewhere in Kyrrith, fifteen people could be seen embedded on several sharpened trees. Their limbs are broken in several spots, showing just how chilling the killer was.
Naturally, this was Sylara’s doing, as she made sure whoever saw this and held any animosity toward her master would have second thoughts.
The chilling nature of how she left the dead bodies was plain as day. This made all those who saw it break into cold sweats.
Then in the Athena Kingdom, Saden and Nyxira also made their way through three cities, killing to their fill.
Vaelros and Zareth also had their fill, and while the news kept traveling back and forth, their unholy mission was almost complete.
At 6 a.m. the next day, every last member of the Clawed Shadows was killed, sending the four kingdoms into a great spiral that left them wondering just what was happening.
But while they continued to handle that, news of Kent Madson started to spread yet again—only this time, he made everyone aware of what would happen next.
People from other kingdoms started wondering if what he said was true.
But since they had yet to receive concrete evidence that their kings and queens were under the thumb of a secret organization, they could only wait and see what would happen.
Of course, the next phase of Kent’s plan was already in motion long before the last person was killed.

chapters.title: Chapter 508: The Oracles
paragraphs: The cave is one of the secluded places on the human continent.
Well, it’s secluded simply because it’s a secret domain located in a pocket dimension. It’s technically not in the world of Sonox.
This place is where one of the most powerful organisations in the world of Sonox is located. It is an organisation of women who call themselves the Oracles.
Their base of operation is called the Cave, and aside from their top-ranking members, nobody, even if part of the Oracle, gets there. Only privilege ones can enter.
For nearly ten months now, the Oracles have been facing a rather grim situation when it come to using the fate strings and power of Karma.
This was due to something incredibly powerful that had messed with their senses.
Oracles are beings who have some connection to the universe and can manipulate fate and weave the fate of others. They use Karma to their advantage, which is rather dangerous.
However, since they are experts, they don’t get any backlash until Kent suddenly appears, and the Karma they take advantage of starts retaliating against them.
This caused them to start looking for why or what had caused that, but no matter how hard they looked, they couldn’t find anything—until Kent started causing waves everywhere.
That was when they noticed something.
No matter how hard they tried, they couldn’t figure out anything about Kent, and as such, they were at a roadblock. They didn’t know what to do.
One thing about the Oracles: they don’t kill randomly, so knowing that perhaps Kent might be the reason for their recent headaches, they started keeping tabs on him.
However, all this changed when they received word from a powerful organisation, one they see as rivals in the game of shadows and deceit.
The Hand.
They received word that Kent was the cause of their troubles, and as such, they could do whatever they wanted to stop him.
This, of course, made them start paying more attention to him. So when he appeared again, they took action.

A dark-clothed lady could be seen flying through the shades of trees in what looked like a dense forest. Nobody was chasing her, but the speed she was moving could not be perceived with just the naked eye.
She was a peak Sovereign with a powerful aura that could not be ignored.
The way she moved also contained hidden patterns that could not be read unless one paid close attention or was taught with vivid detail.

After flying deeper into the thick forest, she stopped when she arrived at a section that looked like the entrance to a cave. She didn’t even bother to look around, confident that no one could have followed her.
Just a slight turn, and they would lose track of her. Trusting in her flight path, she knew she hadn’t been followed.
She stopped and walked closer to the cave entrance, forming a hand seal before pointing her finger at the opening.
A sudden burst of energy formed a portal at the cave’s entrance—nearly invisible to the eye. Trusting herself once more, she flew in, vanishing from sight in the next second.
When she appeared again, she was flying over a bustling forest that housed a small island, in the centre of which stood a rather extravagant castle.
Looking at it from above was simply breathtaking, considering the entire structure was built using jade—white jade crystals. It looked stunning.
However, it was home to some of the most ruthless women in the world of Sonox. The lady flew toward the building and only stopped when she was a few meters from the entrance.
The moment she alighted, she dropped to her knees and spoke.
"I have information about Kent Madson."

Those were the only words she needed to say to be taken seriously, as the gates opened for her to enter. She moved in and soon found herself in a grand hall featuring sixteen chairs and one large throne.
Seated in the sixteen chairs were masked ladies, each exuding a potent Core Formation expert aura—one that Kent had never felt before.
Each possessed a distinct feel, indicating they were from different races. That was especially true for one of them, whose ear was noticeably longer than the average human’s.

However, it was the figure sitting on the throne who commanded the most attention. Her mere presence was enough to crush one’s hopes and dreams. She exuded a pressure similar to the leader of the Hand—an overwhelming force.
"Speak," she said, her voice alone compelling the lady to drop to her knees. The sheer weight of her presence forced her mouth open.
"Kent Madson is out and has already killed every last member of the Clawed Shadow in all four kingdoms," the words flowed from her lips.
"So, how is that going to help us? We already tried to get him, but he slipped away before we could reach him," one of the figures in the chairs replied.
"That’s because this time, he won’t be slipping away—if we hurry," the lady answered, directing her gaze toward the leader, despite being questioned by one of the sixteen.
"How confident are you that your intel is valid?" yet another figure asked.
"Because he’s about to clash with the Hunter."
At the mention of the Hunter, the atmosphere in the room shifted.
"Are you sure?" The lady suddenly felt her body seized by one of the sixteen. She couldn’t resist—the pressure was too overwhelming.
"I’m sure. One of the Hunter’s lackeys made contact with him, and when I left, Kent Madson had just encountered that figure. Which means... the Hunter is already around—and waiting to hunt."
The sixteen figures turned to look toward their leader, who, despite the dark veil covering her face, still radiated a beauty that could be felt.
They knew this was a great opportunity to kill the one who had made their lives miserable for the past several months.
The fact that the Hand went out of their way to inform them of Kent’s true presence was enough to confirm that he was indeed the key to ending their suffering.
"It seems our suspicions are valid. The Hand is clearly up to something big, so much so that they’ve unleashed the Hunter against Kent Madson.
Looks like this is our chance to kill two birds with one stone," the leader of the Oracles said, smiling as she pulled a triangular-shaped item from her space ring.

"I will hand this mission to you, 16th Oracle. Ensure that Kent Madson and the Hunter do not see the light of day after today." The item flew through the air and landed in the hands of one of the figures.
"I will handle it, Leader."

chapters.title: Chapter 509: The hunter
paragraphs: Who is the Hunter?
One hundred fifty years ago, out of nowhere, a certain cultivator appeared on the Ancient Battlefield of Parting and, within seven days, killed thousands of people regardless of their race.
It was said that during this massacre, every race in the world of Sonox sent their best and brightest to apprehend this rogue cultivator.

However, what met them was a bloodbath that left a bitter taste in everyone’s mouth to this day. The Hunter only went quiet and hasn’t been heard from again since the Dragon King and the Shadow Demon Lord went after it.
Nobody knew whether this Hunter was a he or a she. But one thing was known—killing the Hunter wouldn’t be as simple as they might want to think.
The Hunter killed a lot, and every background in the world of Sonox lost someone to this massacre.
Even the Oracles weren’t spared in the unholy massacre, so hearing the Hunter was on the loose again made them plan for both Kent and definitely wouldn’t let this mysterious Hunter off easily.

Currently, inside the Winding Valley, located somewhere in Kyrrith Kingdom, the ugly man who tried to challenge Kent back in Caprath City could be seen face to face with Veydris, who was holding his longsword firmly and gazing sharply at the ugly man’s neck.
Well, Veydris doesn’t have emotions, but the look in his eyes was enough to show the man that if he made any sudden moves, his life would be in danger.
Kent only told Veydris to keep an eye on the ugly man; however, Veydris took that literally and had been staring daggers at the ugly man for the past 14 hours.
Suddenly, mocking laughter filled the space, causing the ugly man to turn to his left and meet Kent’s gaze.
Kent hovered in the air with Zareth, Sylara, Vaelros, and Kaizo behind him. The line-up was terrifying, and the ugly man who came to kill Kent started to sense that perhaps he had made a mistake.
"I know what you’re thinking—why does it have to be this way? You came to kill me, yet here you are, surrounded with no chance of escape in sight," Kent said, smiling at the ugly man.
This caused him to frown, bringing out his features, which only made him uglier.

"You probably have regrets and would love to correct them before dying. However, I don’t have much time to entertain you, so tell me this—where is your master? And don’t ask me how I knew. I can see a slave from a mile away."
The mention of "slave" made the man frown deeper. His hands moved, and before Kent could say or act, he drove a dagger through his chest, ending his own life.
"Looks like you hit the nail too hard, Master," Kaizo said, and Kent nodded with a smile.
"He was dead anyway. I didn’t see it earlier when we met in Caprath City because of my weak cultivation base.
But now that I have become a Root Ascension stage expert, I can tell he was long dead without him even knowing it," Kent said.
"Looks like your necromancy abilities are surfacing, Master," Sylara said. "I saw the death aura around him, too, and from the look of things, his master can’t be underestimated."
"This begs the question—who is his master?" Zareth wasn’t even done speaking when the body on the ground burst, filling the entire space with a pungent smell.
The mist also created a translucent air that made seeing and sensing difficult. However, Zareth just waved his hand, and within seconds, the mist cleared.
However, the moment it cleared, a scene that terrified all of them, including Kent, greeted them.
Before them stood a lineup of 14 Core Formation experts, each sitting at the peak. They all held swords, and their eyes were covered with strips of dark cloth.
Their aura wasn’t just suffocating; it also contained poison. The moment Kent breathed it in, a message appeared in his vision:
⟪You’ve been poisoned. All stats dropped by 20%⟫
"This is rather disappointing. To think they would use their one chance at summoning me on a mere Root Ascension stage brat. How disappointing."
A voice echoed from everywhere, as if the speaker were all around them at once. The voice wasn’t that of a lady or a man. It was a blend of both, with a touch of evil.
However, Kent didn’t bother looking around like Kaizo and the others were doing.
He merely turned slightly to his left and spoke.
"I wonder why they would call out a coward to come after me. I mean, using poison from the get-go. How disappointing." Kent didn’t bother polishing his words, knowing the person wouldn’t let him go.
"Hahahaha..." the person laughed, then asked a question that would have sent chills down the spine of anyone, except Kent.
"Have you ever heard of the Hunter?"
"Can’t say I have. But even if I did, what about it?" Kent asked.

"You are arrogant." Clearly, the voice didn’t appreciate Kent’s tone. His attitude wasn’t encouraging at all. The monologue the voice wanted to have was falling flat thanks to Kent’s indifferent replies.
Kent knew this and planned not to allow the voice to have that chance to monologue. Only he get to monologue as it should be.

"You don’t have to tell me who you are. I know you are the Hunter, once famous for killing 7,200 beings within seven days. Using their souls, blood, spirit roots, and hearts, you created these 14 abominations.
You went into hiding after the leader of The Hand saved you from the Dragon King and the Shadow Demon Lord.
Since you owe The Hand a debt, they summoned you to come after me.
I didn’t expect anything less from people running the entire world. However, I have one question: What happens now that you’re here? You’re a pawn here, so tell me...
Are you confident you’ll be leaving here alive?"

"You, a mere Root Ascension stage brat, and your wannabe subordinates think you can kill me and my Hunter army?" A figure clad in dark, tattered cloth appeared above the 14 abominations with a smirk on her lips.
It didn’t take Kent a second to know she was some form of Necromancer.
The moment she appeared, a powerful aura exploded from her body, revealing that she sat at the peak of the Core Formation stage. But unlike the 14 abominations, her aura is much deeper and dangerous.
Her presence was so overbearing that Kent and his undead were forced down, landing on the ground.
The lady smirked, then used Kent’s own words against him.
"Are you confident you’ll be leaving here alive?"
In response, Kent raised his right hand, extending the middle finger first, before snapping his fingers. "But of course."
The dense pressure falling on him evaporated the moment he snapped his fingers.
The Hunter frowned, sensing her control over Kent vanish just like that. This wasn’t something she expected, but she shrugged and pointed forward.
"Kill him."
Upon receiving the order, the 14 abominations charged forward. However, before they could move a meter, a portal appeared in the air, and a giant axe shot out, blocking their path.
A three-meter-tall, green-skinned, colossal Orc emerged from the portal, gazing coldly at the 14 abominations...

chapters.title: Chapter 510: The Legion of Eternal Wrath (1)
paragraphs: We’ve already met the Undead Legion, the Soul Sentinels, and the Lost Knights. So I guess it’s time to meet the next legion—known as the Eternal Wrath.)
On Kent’s side, there are two Transcendents, three Ascendants, and one Sovereign.

He himself is part of the three Ascendants, so asking him to face an onslaught of 14 Peak Core Formation experts isn’t logical, especially when they have a master whose presence is even more suffocating than all 14 of them combined.
This means Kent needed backup.

Of course, he could call forth the 13 Battle Dolls and let them fight for him, but that would just be them sacrificing their metallic bodies, because there was no way they would be able to do anything.
Their opponents are beings created from an unholy ritual, granting them overwhelming powers.
The 14 abominations are powerful and can easily dominate the Battle Dolls. So he knew that option was out of bounds.
Thankfully, he made his move at the right time. The reason being, Zareth and the rest of the undead had already cleared eight dungeons and claimed them.
Meaning he could now bind the dungeons to the tower, and per the function of the Dungeon Master Cards, he could summon them.
So the moment the hunter showed her true colours, he knew he had to make his own move. Though his team still wouldn’t have a Core Formation expert, he knew they wouldn’t be helpless either.
He just needed them to hold back the 14 while he handled their master. Per the rules of necromancy, the moment the master is dead, all the undead will follow.
So he bound the dungeons to the tower, which took less than a minute. Right when that was done, he decided to show the hunter he wouldn’t be easily killed.

Inside the Legion Tower, eight dungeons, each with 12 floors, appeared. At the top floor of each dungeon, eight beings, each sitting at the Sovereign’s stage, and an appearance bearing a different shape and size, appeared, with a look of shock on their faces.
Well, not all had expressions that could be read, but the way they were turning around said it all—they were shocked by something.
However, before they could wonder what was going on, Kent’s voice spoke to them.
"No need to look shocked. You are alive, and I need you to fight for me." Right when his voice dropped, a portal appeared in front of each and every last one of them.
At the same time, the hunter ordered the fourteen abominations to kill Kent. Naturally, the eight beings on the last floor of the dungeons saw this, so they made their move without any hesitation.
The Orc chieftain swung his axe, sending it flying through the portal. Right when it appeared on the other side, it grew into a colossal axe, slamming into the ground with a thunderous boom.
The shockwave pushed the 14 back several meters.
"It’s that guy, Kaizo, who was ready to charge into battle, halted and turned toward the portal from which the axe came. There, the Orc chieftain appeared, looking coldly at the 14 abominations.
He is one massive orc, standing over 8 feet tall and with a hulking body covered in battle scars. Like any Orc, he has a scarred face with sharp tusks jutting out from his lower jaw.
He is clad in rough, patchwork leather armour with bits of iron and bone stitched in. His chest and shoulders are adorned with tribal markings.
He turned and looked at Kaizo briefly before turning back to the 14 abominations.

"Master, he calls himself Skoggr, and while I dislike his face, he is a very powerful fighter. However, I think he is mad because we took the Qi’lan crystal from him." The look on Skoggr’s face showed he was mad about something.
This, of course, calls for many questions. But that can wait, considering the second figure appeared.
A powerful presence emerged from another portal, bringing a wave of lightning into the space. This one is a wyvern in humanoid form, wielding a large spear bathed in lightning.
"That one is Kha’azal. Though he appears quiet, don’t underestimate him," Kaizo whispered to Kent, watching the draconic, muscular beast point his spear at the hunter and her army.
The look of surprise could be seen on her face as these two powerful beings appeared. However, her shock didn’t end there.
From the third portal, a skull-faced man appeared. His head was devoid of flesh, and his glowing red eyes revealed the horrors hidden within.
Where there should be hair, he has shadows swirling across his white, tattooed skull. He wears ancient, faded royal robes that flow with an eerie, ethereal light.
His hands are long and claw-like, with ethereal chains hanging from his wrists. A glowing, spectral scythe is also in his grip...
"That is Nykali. He is creepy and doesn’t fight himself. He summons some ghostly spectrals to fight for him," Kaizo whispered again to Kent.
As if Nykali heard him, he waved his scythe, summoning hundreds of ghostly figures that hovered behind him.
"Like I said, he is creepy." Kent smiled, watching how spoiled Kaizo was being. Clearly, the experience he had from the dungeon was still giving him nightmares.
Then the fourth appeared.
"It had to be that guy." This time, it was Zareth who spoke as the towering titan appeared.
"He is the strongest of the eight we faced," he muttered, looking at the titan brute, who was literally made of fire. His entire form blazed, and the hammer he wielded was forged from flame itself.
Kent narrowed his eyes when he saw this monstrosity standing over 12 feet tall with a giant hammer in his hand.
"When we faced him, had it not been for the Coil Dragon and the Alabaster Poison Serpent aiding us, we would have lost.
This bastard is powerful," Zareth, who was always looking for a worthy opponent, knew he had found one in the form of an elemental titan.
’Damn, that is one large brute,’ Kent thought. Looking at the towering figure, he knew he would get his chance to handle the hunter, who now wore a serious expression.
The rate at which the figures appeared on the battlefield was overwhelming.
Of course, the look on her face didn’t stop the fifth figure from coming out, too.
