So I guess it’s time to meet the next legion—known as the Eternal Wrath.)
On Kent’s side, there are two Transcendents, three Ascendants, and one Sovereign.

He himself is part of the three Ascendants, so asking him to face an onslaught of 14 Peak Core Formation experts isn’t logical, especially when they have a master whose presence is even more suffocating than all 14 of them combined.
This means Kent needed backup.

Of course, he could call forth the 13 Battle Dolls and let them fight for him, but that would just be them sacrificing their metallic bodies, because there was no way they would be able to do anything.
Their opponents are beings created from an unholy ritual, granting them overwhelming powers.
The 14 abominations are powerful and can easily dominate the Battle Dolls.
So he knew that option was out of bounds.
Thankfully, he made his move at the right time.
The reason being, Zareth and the rest of the undead had already cleared eight dungeons and claimed them.
Meaning he could now bind the dungeons to the tower, and per the function of the Dungeon Master Cards, he could summon them.
So the moment the hunter showed her true colours, he knew he had to make his own move.
Though his team still wouldn’t have a Core Formation expert, he knew they wouldn’t be helpless either.
He just needed them to hold back the 14 while he handled their master.
Per the rules of necromancy, the moment the master is dead, all the undead will follow.
So he bound the dungeons to the tower, which took less than a minute.
Right when that was done, he decided to show the hunter he wouldn’t be easily killed.
Inside the Legion Tower, eight dungeons, each with 12 floors, appeared.
At the top floor of each dungeon, eight beings, each sitting at the Sovereign’s stage, and an appearance bearing a different shape and size, appeared, with a look of shock on their faces.
Well, not all had expressions that could be read, but the way they were turning around said it all—they were shocked by something.
However, before they could wonder what was going on, Kent’s voice spoke to them.
"No need to look shocked.
You are alive, and I need you to fight for me." Right when his voice dropped, a portal appeared in front of each and every last one of them.
At the same time, the hunter ordered the fourteen abominations to kill Kent.
Naturally, the eight beings on the last floor of the dungeons saw this, so they made their move without any hesitation.
The Orc chieftain swung his axe, sending it flying through the portal.
Right when it appeared on the other side, it grew into a colossal axe, slamming into the ground with a thunderous boom.
The shockwave pushed the 14 back several meters.
"It’s that guy, Kaizo, who was ready to charge into battle, halted and turned toward the portal from which the axe came.
There, the Orc chieftain appeared, looking coldly at the 14 abominations.
He is one massive orc, standing over 8 feet tall and with a hulking body covered in battle scars.
Like any Orc, he has a scarred face with sharp tusks jutting out from his lower jaw.
He is clad in rough, patchwork leather armour with bits of iron and bone stitched in.
His chest and shoulders are adorned with tribal markings.
He turned and looked at Kaizo briefly before turning back to the 14 abominations.
"Master, he calls himself Skoggr, and while I dislike his face, he is a very powerful fighter.
However, I think he is mad because we took the Qi’lan crystal from him." The look on Skoggr’s face showed he was mad about something.
This, of course, calls for many questions.
But that can wait, considering the second figure appeared.
A powerful presence emerged from another portal, bringing a wave of lightning into the space.
This one is a wyvern in humanoid form, wielding a large spear bathed in lightning.
"That one is Kha’azal.
Though he appears quiet, don’t underestimate him," Kaizo whispered to Kent, watching the draconic, muscular beast point his spear at the hunter and her army.
The look of surprise could be seen on her face as these two powerful beings appeared.
However, her shock didn’t end there.
From the third portal, a skull-faced man appeared.
His head was devoid of flesh, and his glowing red eyes revealed the horrors hidden within.
Where there should be hair, he has shadows swirling across his white, tattooed skull.
He wears ancient, faded royal robes that flow with an eerie, ethereal light.
His hands are long and claw-like, with ethereal chains hanging from his wrists.
A glowing, spectral scythe is also in his grip...
"That is Nykali.
He is creepy and doesn’t fight himself.
He summons some ghostly spectrals to fight for him," Kaizo whispered again to Kent.
As if Nykali heard him, he waved his scythe, summoning hundreds of ghostly figures that hovered behind him.
"Like I said, he is creepy." Kent smiled, watching how spoiled Kaizo was being.
Clearly, the experience he had from the dungeon was still giving him nightmares.
Then the fourth appeared.
"It had to be that guy." This time, it was Zareth who spoke as the towering titan appeared.
"He is the strongest of the eight we faced," he muttered, looking at the titan brute, who was literally made of fire.
His entire form blazed, and the hammer he wielded was forged from flame itself.
Kent narrowed his eyes when he saw this monstrosity standing over 12 feet tall with a giant hammer in his hand.
"When we faced him, had it not been for the Coil Dragon and the Alabaster Poison Serpent aiding us, we would have lost.
This bastard is powerful," Zareth, who was always looking for a worthy opponent, knew he had found one in the form of an elemental titan.
’Damn, that is one large brute,’ Kent thought.
Looking at the towering figure, he knew he would get his chance to handle the hunter, who now wore a serious expression.
The rate at which the figures appeared on the battlefield was overwhelming.
Of course, the look on her face didn’t stop the fifth figure from coming out, too.

chapters.title: Chapter 511: The Legion of Eternal Wrath (2)
paragraphs: "Personally, I think he is cooler than the rest," Kaizo said, looking toward the fifth portal. From within, a man with a lion-like head appeared. He had a broad, intimidating face with eyes filled with primal intensity.
His face was covered in thick fur, giving him a fierce and rugged look, with a wide mouth filled with razor-sharp teeth.
His mane was a dark, tangled mess of black fur that ran down his back and across his chest. Standing at 7 feet tall, his body was large and muscular, with broad shoulders and thick limbs.
He wore minimal armour—a few leather straps across his chest and waist, and fur pelts draped over his shoulders.
His claws were long and sharp, his arms covered in tribal tattoos, each marking having a distinct meaning. His weapon was his clawed fists, powerful enough to tear through stone.

"Just watch him," Kaizo gestured forward as the lion-headed man raised his hand, and a gate opened. From within, five Peak Ascension Stage Hellhounds, each towering over 3 meters, appeared standing behind him.
"For some reason, he can summon the creatures from the floors below his own. I think he is some kind of summoner that can only summon beasts from the dungeon he rules."

Kent nodded, staring at the lion’s head with a complicated look. So far, he didn’t know where the feeling was coming from, but a sense of familiarity could be felt between him and the beings coming from the portals.
He couldn’t say he felt the same for the rest of his undead, but he did with Gaia, Dori, and Akira.
Of course, this brought many questions, but he didn’t have much time, considering the only reason he wasn’t in a fight yet was that the hunter was still in shock.
He pocketed all questions and could only wait until after the battle...
Then the sixth appeared.
This time, it was a lady.
A tall, slender woman walked out through the portal, holding a staff that needed no description to know she was a necromancer.
The hunter who saw her appear through the portal narrowed her gaze, considering their energies were in sync. The same necrotic energy every necromancer has was reeking from her like perfume.
She wore a dark, flowing robe made of shifting shadows and ethereal fabric that seemed to ripple with dark energy. Her long black hair cascaded like a waterfall.
Naturally, a lady was supposed to have sharp features, and she did. Her facial features were pronounced and perfectly sculpted.
However, she had a tattoo on her face, giving her a skull look. This was the only thing about her that made her look like Nykali, the third to appear from the portal.
Still, judging by her demeanour, it was plain to see she had some firepower in her. Instead of summoning undead, her staff morphed into a sword, which she pointed at the fourteen abominations.
"She’s also creepy. Might want to avoid her at all costs," Kaizo said. He clearly needed therapy for whatever he went through inside the dungeon.
Naturally, Zareth was the cause of all this. Thanks to Kaizo’s unyielding personality, he went into every battle first, which, at every turn, ended badly for the lightning brute fighter.
So while he still had bad memories from his time inside the dungeon, the others were just standing there calmly. Of course, Kent didn’t know that so that he couldn’t get justice for Kaizo.
Turning from the creepy necromancer lady, they focused on the seventh to come through the portal.
The seventh being was massive and bulky, with a body made of dense muscle and rock-like skin that gave him an almost stone-like appearance.
His body was partially armoured with large, jagged rocks and iron plates fastened with leather straps.
He had short, thick black hair with some strands of grey, and a broad orcish face with deep-set eyes and a heavily scarred, stone-like brow.
"This is the second orc we’ve faced, and just like the chieftain, he’s also very powerful. However, I’ll be more awesome than he is once I become an Ascension Stage expert.
The only thing cool about him is that he is a Barbarian Orc"
"Sure," Kent said with a smile. Kaizo clearly needed therapy.
The eighth to appear was, surprisingly, a human—or more accurately, his humanoid form was perfect, giving him a flawless human appearance.ree
He had short, dark hair with the same hue as his eyes. His form was slender, with lean yet sculpted muscle. However, while he looked human, his eyes betrayed him.
His eyes were those of a beast—a panther, to be precise.
He was a panther in perfect human form, and judging by the number of daggers hoisted on his belt strap and other parts of his body, he was clearly an assassin of some kind.
Many years ago, these eight were part of the Eternal Wrath Legion who heeded the call of the Chaos Dragon and travelled through time, appearing when the universe was on the brink of destruction.
Painfully, none of them knew that—including Kent, who could only sense the familiarity but not the reason behind it.
However, while they had no idea what they once did, or perhaps would do, considering the concept of time was a complicated subject, they once again heeded the call of their master.
Standing now, facing the fourteen abominations, the look of determination was the only thing in their eyes.
Kent, who now knew his chance to see how much he had grown had arrived, looked at the hunter and smiled.
"It’s between you and me now." Without even giving her a chance to reply, he blinked and appeared before her, landing a powerful punch.
The hunter blocked by crossing her arms over her chest. The force from the punch vibrated through her arms, sending her flying back.
Kent turned to his lineup of twelve warriors. "Have fun."

With that, he jumped back into the battle as he and the hunter clashed more fiercely. Now that he had become several times stronger, he wanted to see how well he would fare against a Core Formation expert.
His sword had not appeared yet—Kent was testing his strength, so his fists were the weapon for now.
From how he was devastating the hunter, it was safe to say his strength had already reached a level he couldn’t fully comprehend yet.

chapters.title: Chapter 512: Clash With The Hunter (1)
paragraphs: Kent clashed with the Hunter, distancing her from the rest of the battles.
The moment he left, his team went into battle too. Kaizo was the first to lunge forward, taking on one of the fourteen abominations.
The rest also picked their opponents, with Zareth alone taking on two. The enemy outnumbered them, so he had to take on two in order to prevent them from going back to their master.
Kent was already going against odds that heavy, so adding more was simply too much.

Kazarak, the lion-headed man-beast who summoned the five Hellhounds, also took on two Core Formation enemies. He and one Hellhound were on one, while the other four Hellhounds were on the other beast.
The rest was up to Kent’s ability to handle the Hunter before they could no longer hold them back.
But asking that was just underestimating Kent. So far, he had pushed the Hunter back with his punches, showing her he wasn’t a mere Root Ascension expert.
He had seriously underestimated his own strength. The punches he was landing on the Hunter weren’t something any of the Core Formation experts he had fought would have been able to handle.

Whenever he punched using his full strength, the space seemed to crack, threatening to open the void. However, Kent wasn’t thinking about that, considering every single punch was him testing how much he had grown.
"Is it just me, or are you just weak and can’t handle my punches?" Kent paused, looking at the Hunter, who had been punched back for the umpteenth time.
"Shut up."
Instead of answering, the Hunter waved her staff, and a powerful beam of dark energy shot from it, speeding toward Kent.

Kent was on the move, evading the dark beam. He appeared behind the Hunter and kicked forward, trying to land a powerful kick on her neck. However, the Hunter blocked with her arm and swung her staff.
Kent blinked away, avoiding the swing before landing a punch on her face, only to be blocked again. He distanced himself once more, appearing several meters from her.
"I don’t know why you think you can kill me or make a big deal out of your presence, but tell me this: how did you manage to kill thousands without getting caught?
You are weak, which is normal considering you’re a necromancer. But just where is your strength coming from?"
Kent asked, not understanding something. The Hunter he was facing now wasn’t much. He was pushing her back, and to be frank with himself, he was starting to think that perhaps something was wrong.
However, while it would have been great to get the answer the simple way, which means by hearing it from the Hunter, she wasn’t about to speak.
Instead, she waved her staff, conjuring thousands of dark shards to appear in the air and shoot at Kent, who started moving between the attacks.

The more he moved, the more and faster the shards appeared and rained down on him. However, regardless of how fast the shards were coming, Kent was weaving his way through them like it was the easiest thing to do.
His speed and strength had already become monstrous, so there was no way he would struggle against such an attack.
Being a necromancer, the Hunter didn’t pose much of a threat. But that didn’t mean Kent underestimated her.
Eventually, he had had enough and retrieved his sword.
The moment the sword entered his grip, his energy exploded, pushing the Hunter back. This caused her to narrow her gaze at the sword in Kent’s hand.
"No need to look shocked; I’m richer than you," Kent said, taking a swing.
The Hunter, who recognized the sword’s value in Kent’s hand, distanced herself from him and raised a defense to block the sword’s attack.
The sword arc landed on her defense, creating a crack in it.
However, Kent didn’t waste time as he unleashed the Lunar Eclipse Slash, sending a powerful crescent-shaped sword arc at the Hunter.
The moment the attack landed on her defense, it shattered, causing her to cough blood as a powerful shockwave blew her back.

Kent didn’t let her rest as he unleashed another powerful sword slash, sending her flying back even farther. Noticing she wasn’t putting up much resistance against the attacks, he continued bombarding her without pause.
Meanwhile, his team was also engaged in fierce combat with the fourteen abominations.
All sides of the battle were chaotic—perhaps even more chaotic than the clash between Kent and the Hunter.
Not that it was unexpected. The Hunter was a necromancer, meaning combat was the last thing she specialized in. So the fact that she had managed to hold Kent back this long was a miracle in itself.
The fourteen abominations, however, were made for combat, and that was evident in how they were facing Kent’s team. Still, they didn’t have the upper hand in the fight.

Kent’s side was also monstrous, and as such, they were handling themselves quite well. Even Kaizo, who was by far the weakest, managed to hold back the Core Formation expert he was engaged in combat with.
Kaizo gritted his teeth as he blocked another strike. The Core Formation abomination towered over him, but Kaizo didn’t back down.
His movements were slower, but he stayed in the fight, dodging when he could and countering when he must.
The sounds of battle rang out everywhere—swords clashing, spells crackling, roars shaking the air. The ground was scarred, and the air was thick with smoke and blood.
Meanwhile, Kent remained focused.
He swung his sword again, the arc of energy smashing into the Hunter’s defenses. Her body was thrown back, crashing into a jagged rock. She staggered to her feet, blood dripping from her lips.
Kent didn’t know why, but despite pushing the hunter back, he wasn’t happy about that. It was like something else was at play, and he needed to be extra careful.
The Hunter dropped to her knee, blood dripping from the corner of his lips...
"You can’t win, so you might as well tell me your deal with the Hand and perhaps their location," Kent said flatly, walking toward her.
The Hunter didn’t answer. Her eyes narrowed. Her grip tightened on her staff.
She raised it slowly, dark energy swirling around her. She locked her gaze on Kent as if looking into his soul.
Suddenly, the sky turned pale. The ground trembled. Kent came to a stop, sensing the swift in the air. A sense of dread washed over him, causing him to look back.
Somewhere atop where his team and the abominations were fighting, A loud crack appeared in the air, echoing across the battlefield.
Then came the roar—deep, hollow, and chilling.
Bones clawed their way through the crack.
A massive skeletal form appeared, its wings wide and empty of flesh. Its eyes glowed with sickly green fire, and its jaw opened in a silent growl.
Kent felt something lock onto his body when the bone head appeared.
He turned his gaze from the Bone Dragon back to the Hunter, who was now forming a seal with both hands. A glowing spell diagram appeared beneath her feet, pulsing with eerie light.
"Soul Sacrifice," Kent muttered at first, but then his eyes widened as realization struck him.
"No... Soul Swap. You’re not the necromancer, are you? You’re also an undead."
Kent spread his senses outward, searching. But he found nothing-no presence, no heartbeat, no soul.
He took in a sharp, cold breath.
"So what if you’re a Bone Dragon... You’re just a cheap copy anyway."
With that, Kent lunged toward the Bone Dragon. He knew he had to be extra careful now.
The Hunter was becoming more mysterious by the second. Even Kent’s Enchanted Eyes couldn’t read her anymore.

But he found nothing-no presence, no heartbeat, no soul.
He took in a sharp, cold breath.
"So what if you’re a Bone Dragon...
You’re just a cheap copy anyway."
With that, Kent lunged toward the Bone Dragon.
He knew he had to be extra careful now.
The Hunter was becoming more mysterious by the second.
Even Kent’s Enchanted Eyes couldn’t read her anymore.

chapters.title: Chapter 513: Clash With The Hunter (1)
paragraphs: One good thing about having superior-grade skills and techniques is that the attack power they unleash when used is several times stronger than that of inferior ones.
Kent’s skills are several times stronger than the limit of the world he is in, and as such, he has stronger attack power than one could imagine.

His soul strength is currently at Tier 11, allowing him to harness more of his cultivation. One good thing about having a stronger soul is that he can harness more of his cultivation’s spiritual essence.
This allows him to use more attack power without injuring his soul.
All skills require some soul essence to unleash, and as such, if his soul strength isn’t strong enough, he wouldn’t be able to unleash the attack.
But even if he forces himself and uses it, the chances of injuring his soul are very high. Thankfully, he is at the 11th Tier now and still growing.

Then there is the fact that he had broken a limit on himself, which in this case has led to more modifications to his body. His meridians widened, allowing him to harness more of his energy into the attacks.
The fact that he had broken a limit is already enough to allow him to harness more of his strength. As for his body cultivation, that one is a bonus.
So when the bone dragon appeared, he didn’t falter in his attacks.
He first used the Rapid Slash to overwhelm it, and then from there, he started Lunar Eclipse Slash to bombard it with powerful sword attacks.
The lady Kent, initially believed to be the hunter, has now merged with the dragon, making it even stronger than the lady was before merging with the dragon.
However, in under five minutes, Kent had managed to break some bones and lower its defense significantly.
’At this rate, I wonder where the real deal is or when they will arrive.’ Knowing the hunter was merely using minions made him become alert.
His senses were spreading through the space for any signs of the real hunter, but nothing clicked. He even exerted his soul strength, but nothing seemed to click.
"What if?" Kent paused and turned to his left, watching his team clashing with the 14 abominations.
’I am no genius, but I know there is a range within which a person must be to release and maintain control of their undead, especially if they are not like mine.
This means they should be close by, but they are hidden from sight. In that case, why not look for them closely this time, considering the dragon isn’t on the level that must be feared?’

Kent sighed, not minding the bone dragon. He had already established that his strength was at the peak of the Core Formation stage, so worrying about the wannabe bone dragon was just him worrying himself.
His Gaze techniques were already enough.
The Lunar Eclipse Slash was unleashing sword arcs, while the Thousand Blade Reflections was multiplying the attacks, creating hundreds of copies.
The dragon couldn’t get closer.
’Since Akira said I should train my senses, I’d better figure this one out before turning to the tower if I can’t.’ Kent focused his soul strength, spreading it hundreds of miles.
He focused on the smallest detail, exploring every tiny aspect.
This time, he took his time, so when he saw something odd, he knew he had found something.
Twelve miles from where the battle was raging, a small dark orb, about the size of an egg, was sitting quietly on the ground, exuding little to no aura.
Kent had missed this at first, but this time, he found it odd.
However, he didn’t take any action. If his suspicion was right and this orb had something to do with the real hunter, then he had to be careful.
He quickly made a plan on how to approach it and put it into action almost immediately. He didn’t even bother with the dragon, which was nearly reduced to broken bones.
"A true Bone Dragon of a necromancer shouldn’t be this weak. I guess this hunter is just a basic one." His comment ended with a sudden swing of his sword.
"Void Cleave."
Kent was 1 km away, knowing that the second form of the Annihilation Sword Techniques required a certain distance to unleash its full power.
So he unleashed it, and as the sword arc closed in on the dragon, it started getting more powerful until it slammed into its bony head, cracking it completely.
The moment the dragon’s head exploded, a powerful soul force erupted from Kent, moving in a single direction.
The orb, sitting 12 miles away, cracked when the soul energy surrounded it. The crack widened, and then it exploded into a dark mist.
The mist formed into a person who immediately coughed up blood. She was clad in black clothes from head to toe, with a dark hood covering her head.
"You do know only cowards hide, right?" Kent said, unleashing a powerful swing again, sending a Void Cleave toward the hunter, whose actual body had now appeared and was injured in the soul.
The attack slammed into her, sending her flying. She slammed into the ground but quickly got back on her feet.
"How? My soul concealment was perfect," she said.
Kent sneered and replied, "I guess it wasn’t perfect enough."
"Bullshit! I know my control is perfect. There was no way you could have found me." The hunter was still in disbelief, refusing to accept that she had been discovered.
"Tell that to the next Tier 10 you’ll fight." The hunter narrowed her eyes at Kent when she heard his reply.
Then they widened as she sensed something unbelievable.
"Impossible." She sensed Kent’s Tier 11 soul strength only because he allowed her to. Watching the shocked look on her face, Kent smirk
"Nothing is impossible, lady. Now you can die in peace," Kent said, channeling lightning into his sword.
However, just as he was about to unleash the attack, a figure appeared above, looking down on both him and the hunter. She retrieved an item from her space ring.
They both sensed something grim when a triangular-shaped item appeared in the newcomer’s hand.
"The Oracles send their greetings. Now die." The lady in the air spoke, channeling her energy into the triangular-shaped item.

"No, stop!" the hunter shouted. But the lady in the air ignored her panic. The hunter seemed to recognize the item the lady was holding, which made her want to escape. However, Kent attacked, halting her steps..
In that instant, the lady in the air activated the item.
"Dead Region Teleporter, activate." The lady threw the item at Kent and the hunter, whose bodies were immediately locked in place.
There was panic on the hunter’s face. However, on Kent’s face, no panic could be seen. He turned and looked at the lady as he felt his body being pulled into the teleporter.
"The Dead Region, huh? I didn’t know I’d be going back this soon... Guess there’s no place like home."
His body vanished into the teleporter along with the hunter who was crying her heart out...
The lady who activated the teleporter frowned when she heard what Kent just said. "Did he just say, ’There’s no place like home’?" Clearly, she had heard him right.
To make matters worse, Kaizo and the rest of Kent’s team appeared at the spot where he had vanished. The lady in the air distanced herself. However, her frown deepened when she heard Kaizo speak.
"Looks like the master has gone back home. This means our job is done here."
Kaizo turned toward the lady’s direction and smiled. "Thank you for making the trip short for my master. We will be sure to pay you and your organization a proper visit to offer our thanks."
With that, they vanished back into the tower.
Since the hunter was gone, her undead also vanished.
"I need to report this," the lady, who was the 16th Oracle, said with a panicked voice as she began speeding away. The outcome she expected didn’t happen.

chapters.title: Chapter 514: The Dead Region
paragraphs: Kent didn’t know he would be pulled into the Dead Region, which is one of the many dangerous places in the Ancient Battlefield of Parting.
Nobody knew what was inside that space, simply because all who entered never returned. So he never expected there to be a teleporter that could send someone there.
However, since there was, he most certainly wasn’t going to allow the user to get the satisfaction they wanted. He was more shameless than that.
Hearing the smugness in the voice of the 16th Oracle pissed him off so he knew he had to mess with her head and wipe the smugness from her face under the mask.
So, knowing nobody truly knew his background, when he was getting pulled in, he made sure the person who wanted to send him to his death was made aware he was from the Dead Region.
There was no way the lady from the Oracles could know whether he was lying or not.
Nobody knew anything about the Dead Region, so for someone with abnormally strong willpower and strength like Kent’s to say he was from there, there was some substance in it.

One could say he was speaking the truth, considering the type of people he had on his side. They clearly weren’t human, so there was that—and the fact that Kent appeared out of nowhere and started causing trouble everywhere.
His messing with the Oracle was just his way of getting them riled up for when he returns. He could have escaped, but he didn’t—simply because he wanted to go to the Dead Region.
This was because, while he initially planned just to escape into the tower, a quest appeared that made him change his mind.
He couldn’t ignore the quest despite knowing that where he was going wasn’t friendly at all.
Naturally, this quest wasn’t one he could breeze through, considering it came with a rather serious condition:
He could not summon his undead or the new additions to his team. This time, he had to get everything done by himself.
So he allowed himself to be pulled into the teleporter that sent him and the hunter to two different places inside the Dead Region.
Kent appeared atop a tall mountain, immediately feeling the change around him.
The first thing he noticed was the change in the air. It was much more chaotic and stronger than the one outside. Though it was not as pure as the outside, it wasn’t impure either.
"This feeling." Surprisingly, Kent was resonating with the new air he was breathing, which shouldn’t have been possible, considering this air should limit anyone who stepped in.

However, he wasn’t being limited; instead, the moment he appeared there, it seemed right for him. Then again, he did tell the lady she was going back to him, which, in this situation, he felt right at home.
He couldn’t contact his undead, the ladies, or his assistants, but he could contact the tower, which immediately gave him the answer to his sudden rise in strength.
"Tower, what am I dealing with here?" He knew he was in the Dead Region, so he had to get his questions sorted out faster before things escalated.
⟪Though faint, there are traces of chaos energy in the air, and since your bloodline is basically made of chaos energy, the air inside the region is resonating with your bloodline.⟫
"In this case, cultivating here means my bloodline will be strengthened, right?" Kent asked.
⟪Yes. However, before you can use it to strengthen your bloodline or even harness it while here, you must first understand chaos energy and how it behaves. This means you must cultivate it⟫
"How do I do that?"

⟪Just tap into your bloodline, and it will come to you naturally. You have the chaos energy in your bloodline, but because it hasn’t made any significant increase in awakening, you don’t yet have that understanding.
However, with these strands of chaos energy in the air, you can easily start to comprehend it, and with some effort, you will begin to gain understanding.⟫
Kent didn’t immediately respond. Instead, he looked around, gazing at the red sky and the thick air filled with chaotic energy.
"This is your doing, isn’t it?" Kent asked the tower after looking around him for a few moments.
There was no danger within a 16-mile radius. He sensed that, instead of appearing deep within the Dead Region, he had appeared at the outskirts.
There was no danger there, and considering the hunter wasn’t with him, it wouldn’t take a genius to know what had happened.
⟪Though the master is unaware of this, beings inside this region have some understanding of chaos energy. Though weak, they can use it.
This means you are out of your league here, and since you are alone, I figured you must at least gain some understanding before embarking on the quest.
My job is to ensure the master benefits from every small resource, so I made this decision after putting all variables into consideration.⟫
"Great decision, Tower. I truly cannot face this quest with my current strength," Kent sighed and then sat down in a lotus posture.
"In that case, I will start early since I only have three weeks to complete the quest." He tapped into his bloodline and started circulating his blood.
He could sense the air around him getting pulled into his body the moment he began.
⟪You have started comprehending Chaos Qi⟫
This message appeared, making Kent smile as he sat there, comprehending more of the Chaos Qi.
Meanwhile, deep in the Dead Region, in a valley, a river made of blood flowed freely. A figure was kneeling down, blood seeping from the corner of her mouth, with a gaping hole through her chest.
This person was the hunter, who was unfortunate enough to find herself trapped inside the inner section of the Dead Region.
Standing before her was a figure clad in purple armor with a dark mask covering his face. He had the same height as a human.
The air around him revealed he was a Peak Sovereign; however, his strength was enough to overpower the hunter and her fourteen abominations.
This was because he had some understanding of the CHAOS QI and could use it.
A spear was in his grip, pointing toward the hunter, who kept coughing up blood.
"Where is your other companion? I sensed two people enter this region," the figure said, making the hunter shudder as she waited for her death.
"Like I said before, I don’t know, and he is not my companion. He is actually my enemy," she answered, but the figure didn’t believe her, so he stabbed his spear forward.
"Stop," a new voice spoke, halting the masked man.
He turned to his right and bowed down. "Tribe Master, I sensed two people entered our region, but only found one. I tried to find out about the other from her, but she wouldn’t give me an answer."
The man with the spear spoke, showing great respect to the new arrival. The newcomer was a man wearing a dark cloak but with no hood or mask.
This revealed his crime skin and three eyes.
"I will take it from here. You can leave."
The spearman nodded and left without much protest.

chapters.title: Chapter 515: Learning Chaos Qi
paragraphs: [Inside the Tower]
Vexthra, who was seated inside the Mountain Garden enjoying her tea, suddenly felt an unknown force block her connection to Kent.
This caused her to panic; however, before things could escalate, Gaia appeared inside the garden.
"Where is Kent?" Vexthra asked.
"He is on a mission that came with a special condition. We can’t contact him, and he can’t contact us. However, he is fine.
"I only came to inform you because he will be away for a while," Gaia responded, and Vexthra let out a deep sigh.
Her worried expression softened upon hearing what Gaia said.
"How long will he be away for?" Vexthra asked.
"Close to two years," Gaia answered. Since time runs differently inside the tower, the three weeks for Kent are over 500 days for them. So, close to two years will pass before they see Kent again.
"Thank you." Gaia nodded and left.
"Two years. That is enough time to make sure the ladies are at their prime." A smile tugged at her lips as she looked over the bustling city.
With 120 new people added, it started to look more like a proper city and less like just a place with majestic structures.
After spending a few seconds there, she left for the Body Tower, where her sister would be waking up soon. She needed time to make sure they came out of their training looking their best.

Inside the Legion Tower, the undead and the Eternal Wrath, the new addition to Kent’s team who had come from the dungeon, also started to look at each other’s faces the moment they teleported back into the tower.
Kent had only told Kaizo to mess with the 16th Oracle, but he said nothing about them not being able to contact him after he was teleported away.
Thankfully, after Gaia, who could communicate with the tower, learned of what was going on, she made sure all concerned bodies were made aware of the situation.
She appeared inside the Legion Tower at the same time she went to see Vexthra.
"Master will be away for two years, so do whatever you want for the time being. I will inform you if he has something for you." After saying that, she left.
"In that case, why don’t we handle the last four dungeons and be done with the mission once and for all?" Kaizo proposed, and the rest of his teammates nodded.

Kaizo then turned to the eight Eternal Wrath, who held calm looks on their faces. Well, they appeared calm, but they were some of the most dangerous beings in the universe, so they weren’t exactly calm, per se.
"Do you guys want to join us?" Kaizo asked, but all eight shook their heads, and without even a peep, they vanished into their respective dungeons.
They would rather wait for Kent to return so they could see what the hell was going on and why they felt like they had become someone’s subordinate.

Naturally, becoming Kent’s subordinate was the least of their worries. They were more concerned about the fact that they had died and come back to life—and now, they felt like they didn’t belong in the dungeons in the first place.
But they must wait for Kent to come back before all their questions are answered.
Kaizo looked at where the eight Eternal Wrath had stood and smirked. "What an uptight bunch." He shrugged and turned back to his teammates.
"I guess it’s just us now." They nodded, and before long, vanished into the next dungeon they would be clearing. Zareth needed the bodies from their kills to unlock another skill or technique.
Meanwhile, inside the Dead Region, Kent was still seated, circulating his blood as the Chaos energy entered his body, improving his comprehension.
After the Tower made him aware that he had started learning Chaos Qi, he sat there doing nothing aside from comprehending it.
Ten minutes later, a message appeared, bringing a smile to his face:
⟪Your comprehension of Chaos Qi has improved slightly⟫

⟪You have unlocked 9% of your Bloodline.⟫

The moment he attained Weak comprehension of Chaos Qi, he could tell how pitifully low the chaos energy in the air had become.

"He is on a mission that came with a special condition.
We can’t contact him, and he can’t contact us.
However, he is fine.
"I only came to inform you because he will be away for a while," Gaia responded, and Vexthra let out a deep sigh.
Her worried expression softened upon hearing what Gaia said.
"How long will he be away for?" Vexthra asked.
"Close to two years," Gaia answered.
Since time runs differently inside the tower, the three weeks for Kent are over 500 days for them.
So, close to two years will pass before they see Kent again.
"Thank you." Gaia nodded and left.
"Two years.

She needed time to make sure they came out of their training looking their best.

chapters.title: Chapter 516: The Rescue Quest
paragraphs: "Are you sure?" the 13th Oracle asked, staring toward the 16th Oracle.
"Yes. I heard him say he was going back home," the 16th Oracle said. "When he was teleported away, even his subordinate didn’t look shocked or angry. It was like a normal thing to them.
I waited six whole days just to see if he would appear again, but he didn’t. However, I have this feeling he wasn’t bluffing."

The 16th Oracle, who was sent to kill Kent and the Hunter, returned after almost a week simply because she was still disturbed by what Kent said when she teleported him and the Hunter to the Dead Region.
This made her wait for a while before returning to report. Though Kent didn’t return even after six days, she was still skeptical about whether or not he was indeed telling the truth.
"This is indeed concerning," the 10th Oracle said, making the others nod. They then turned to their leader.
"This is indeed not ideal, and considering we still don’t have enough access to the Karma of this world, it means he is still alive.
Or perhaps we were wrong about him—in which case, if he died, we would only incur a small portion of the Karmic backlash.
That said, if he comes back alive, then we will know he is indeed the one we are after, which means we can only try again until we succeed.
For now, we can only continue to steal the fate of fertile men and hope this doesn’t last forever." All sixteen oracles in the hall nodded.
They most certainly didn’t know the only reason Kent hadn’t yet escaped the Dead Region was that he received a quest that could not be ignored.
Back inside the Dead Region, after learning Chaos Qi, Kent spent some time checking his strength and how to wield the small amount of Chaos Qi he could muster at the moment.
Strangely, even the small amount was enough to prove he had become incredibly powerful.
After getting acquainted with using Chaos Qi, he tested his bloodline, considering it had finally reached 9%.
He could still only summon his dragon scales, horns, claws, and wings. There was no new aspect at his time. However, that doesn’t mean he hadn’t gained anything.
Thanks to reaching 9%, the scales felt sturdier, and the claws were much sharper and stronger.
Flexing them, he felt like he could claw through metal, tearing it with his bare hands. He then checked his wings, which were now much sharper and better suited for flight.
His speed had also increased, and as for his strength, he would need to punch a few things to measure it accurately.
Basically, he had become very powerful, and regardless of who he faced—even in his human form—they would struggle to keep up with him.
"I can’t wait to gain more features and perhaps turn into a full dragon. I would look cooler and badass that way," he said, his smile contagious as he felt his strength.

"I guess it’s off to the quest then. I must end this fast, since I have alchemy to do and other continents to explore—not forgetting the Ancient Battlefield of Parting is still there, waiting for me, my wives, and my legion."
He turned to the quest and started reading it.
⟪You have received a new Quest from the Universe.⟫
⟪Quest Name: Rescue the Bloodvein Tribe⟫
⟪Quest Difficulty: Very Hard⟫
→ The Bloodvein Tribe in the Dead Region will soon face an extinction event that will end their existence.
→ This cannot be allowed to happen, considering they are staunch followers of Shara, the Mother of Killers.
→ Your mission is to contact them and help them overcome this event.
→ You are prohibited from killing anyone from this tribe, and you cannot allow them to face this event on their own, whether they accept your help or not.
⟪Rewards:⟫
→ 30 Million Tower Points
→ Memory Fragment (Shara)
→ Reward from Bloodvein Tribe
[Note: You cannot summon or communicate with anyone inside the Tower. This mission must be handled by you alone.]
"Hmm, looks like this is something Neomi should be doing, considering these are her followers," Kent smirked as he read the quest’s details.
The fact that he was pulled into this quest proves its great importance. It concerns the existence of an entire race and one of his wives.
Thanks to her true name, Neomi went by many names.
One such name was Shara, the Mother of Killers.
Eons ago, when she emerged from the Slaughter Trial, she earned many names and titles, but for years now, the name Shara has been associated with killing.
Naturally, that sounded disturbing.
However, while it unsettled some, others worshipped her. This meant she was a symbol—and when the time came, she would gain even more fate simply because of her name: Shara.
That was wild, and now, Kent, being the good husband, was meant to protect this fate. But he still has many questions, like whether Shara had lived in this world before.
Another being, who was Shara, and how does she connect to his wife?
Then it dawned on him: "If these people are followers of Shara, then does it mean Neomi would one day become this Shara?" He paused and looked at the rewards.
"Don’t tell me she would recover her memories like I do with the Memory Key." Kent hadn’t caught that earlier, but now that he did, he immediately focused on the mission.
He had already seen what memories could do, so if his wives had a chance to recover theirs, he wouldn’t waste time.
"Does this mean they were also like me? Does it mean they once lived and died like I did?" This question, however, wasn’t something he could answer now.
He also didn’t know why, but thinking about their past wasn’t something he was overly concerned about. He had this nagging feeling that things would come together one way or another.
"I must get her this fragment and see what she can do with it." Kent didn’t waste any more time.
His wings appeared, and like a shooting star, he shot toward the western side of the Dead Region, where the Bloodvein Tribe was located.

chapters.title: Chapter 517: The Bloodvein Tribe
paragraphs: The Bloodvein Tribe is one of the three major tribes in the Dark Region. There are seven tribes in total, but three rule over the rest. The Bloodvein rule over two minor tribes, while the other two have one each.

They are located in the western part of the Dead Region, and while they have lived there for thousands of years, nobody from the outside world knows who they are, simply because no one ever makes it out of there alive.

The Dead Region is one of the many places in the universe that just doesn’t make any sense. The people in the Bloodvein Tribe are red-skinned and have red eyes, making them resonate with their affinity for blood.
In the Bloodvein Tribe, there are thousands of inhabitants with only one tribe chief and three elders who see to it that matters of the tribe are handled.
However, while they may be more limited than the world outside, their strength cannot be ignored. Regardless of age, every last one has the means to protect themselves when outside their tribe.
They were the strongest tribe in the Dead Region until a month ago, when something happened. Their hunters, who went out to hunt in a neutral region, never returned.
After conducting an investigation, it was discovered that the Dreadclaw Tribe and Soulshroud Tribe were responsible.
Naturally, if only one tribe had been involved, the Bloodvein Tribe would have retaliated. However, this time, it was both of the other major tribes that came together to commit such a crime.
But it didn’t stop there. Over the past week, this new alliance went ahead and destroyed businesses owned by the Bloodvein Tribe.

They tried to retaliate, but the odds they were up against weren’t something they could easily face. So they held back, trying their best to negotiate, even going as far as offering a portion of their domain to appease the wrath of the two tribes.
However, in response to their offer, the alliance of the two tribes went ahead and used nefarious means to pull the minor tribes that were under the Bloodvein Tribe.
The Bloodvein Tribe became powerless against all this simply because, while they were the strongest, they couldn’t go against the combined force of the two major tribes and now four tribes.
Naturally, the Bloodveins suspected their strength wasn’t coming only from their combined force.
Something else made them bold, which in this case made the Bloodveins hesitate from retaliating despite their odds stacked too large against them.
Then, two weeks ago, they received a declaration of war from the alliance of the two major and four minor tribes.
They demand two things: the most valuable and beautiful item of the Bloodvein Tribe.
The Blood Heart Stone and the daughter of the tribe chief.
Their terms were clear and precise. Failure to meet these demands means they choose death, and as such, they will invade in a week.
This caused them to close their borders, and for the past two weeks, they have been waiting for the tribe chief to decide.
Their demands wasnt something the Bloodveins would give freely. They would die first before even considering it.
The Blood Heart Stone holds the fate of the entire tribe. Handing it over to the alliance would be akin to letting them brand the tribe with slave marks.
Then there’s the matter of them asking for the daughter of the tribe chief. That demand was nothing more than a humiliation tactic—they simply wanted to turn her into a plaything.

Naturally, the alliance had no intention of letting them live in peace, even after getting what they wanted. So, the plan for the past two weeks had been to prepare for war, which they had been doing all along.
Kent, of course, knew nothing of this. His mission was to help handle the extinction event about to befall the Bloodvein Tribe.
Now flying at top speed toward the Bloodvein Tribe’s domain was Kent.
"I’m almost there. I’d better walk from here before they think I’m an intruder," he said, coming to a stop in a valley filled with plants that had red leaves and bark.
"This place is beautiful." Looking at the overwhelming redness everywhere, he couldn’t help but admire its unique beauty.
One would expect red only to convey danger, but this was far from that. The red this time was portraying beauty.
He started moving forward, keeping his senses sharp and spread out.
After learning Chaos Qi, his senses could now stretch as far as 50 miles in all directions—and when focused in one direction, he could see up to 100 miles ahead.
He didn’t know if this was due to the Chaos Qi in the air, but at that moment, he was at the peak of his power and loving it.
After moving about ten miles, he stopped when he sensed five figures two miles ahead.
"Judging by their auras and the way they’re standing, I would say they are on the lookout for something," Kent concluded.
All five were Peak Root Sovereigns, with auras that surpassed even kingdom protectors by several degrees.
"The moment I enter the one-mile radius, they’ll sense me—and since I can’t kill them, I must make this as peaceful as possible. Of course, if they try anything stupid, I can just shut them up."
He started walking forward again, but this time with an air of calm. He didn’t want to rile them up.
Like he predicted, when he stepped within a one-mile radius, the five figures noticed him. As if they already wanted him dead, all five locked onto him with their auras before flying toward him.
"An intruder. Inform the Chief!" one of them shouted. And before Kent could even respond or introduce himself, four powerful attacks were already hurtling toward him.
"Oh, come on," he muttered as he jumped back, pushed away by the explosion caused by the attacks.
"Wait! I am—" Kent tried to approach things the easy way, but the four attackers didn’t allow it. They lunged forward. Three were swordsmen, and the other two wielded staffs—clearly mages.
The three swordsmen unleashed their skills. One swung his sword, summoning a large snake made of sword qi, tinged with a touch of chaos energy that Kent immediately sensed.
The second conjured dozens of energy swords with a single swing, and the last unleashed a flurry of sword arcs—each as sharp and deadly as the next.
"These idiots..."
Kent dodged two of the attacks, but the snake landed on him, knocking him back. Thankfully, his clothes were made from a divine item, so the attack didn’t harm him physically.
Inwardly, however, something profound happened.
⟪Your comprehension of Chaos Qi has improved slightly⟫
’Well, fuck me sideways,’ a smile crept onto his face as he watched this unfold...

I am—" Kent tried to approach things the easy way, but the four attackers didn’t allow it.
They lunged forward.
Three were swordsmen, and the other two wielded staffs—clearly mages.
The three swordsmen unleashed their skills.
One swung his sword, summoning a large snake made of sword qi, tinged with a touch of chaos energy that Kent immediately sensed.
The second conjured dozens of energy swords with a single swing, and the last unleashed a flurry of sword arcs—each as sharp and deadly as the next.
"These idiots..."
Kent dodged two of the attacks, but the snake landed on him, knocking him back.
Thankfully, his clothes were made from a divine item, so the attack didn’t harm him physically.
Inwardly, however, something profound happened.
⟪Your comprehension of Chaos Qi has improved slightly⟫
’Well, fuck me sideways,’ a smile crept onto his face as he watched this unfold...

chapters.title: Chapter 518: Malthar Bloodseer
paragraphs: ⟪Your comprehension of Chaos Qi has improved slightly⟫
A second attack landed on Kent’s body, pushing him back, but the message he had been wanting to see a second time appeared, making him smile again.
’Looks like my understanding of Chaos Qi grows as more attacks land on my body," Kent thought to himself as he took on another attack.
⟪Your comprehension of Chaos Qi has improved slightly⟫

That was when he decided to take on all the attacks. He made sure his vitals were protected but coating them with thick spiritual qi, and then, like an idiot, he started letting every last attack land on his body.

For the first few attacks, the five individuals didn’t say anything and kept doing their best to kill him. However, after a few more hits, they paused and stared at Kent in shock when they realized he wasn’t even getting hurt.
"Why did you guys stop? I was enjoying the tickle," Kent said, taunting the five to attack. He was getting stronger from getting attacked, so he wanted more.
Of course, this wasn’t an option for the five, who became afraid of Kent instead of getting angry and continuing to attack.
All their attacks did nothing to him, and worse, it seemed their target wanted to sleep and let them bombard him.
That was not something normal to witness. It was clear to them that they were not going to kill him anytime soon.
Worst, they began to wonder what would become of them when Kent attacked them.
"Who are you?" one of the guards asked.
"Oh, now you want to know who I am? What if I were to say I am your father—would you believe me?" Kent said with a mocking smile.
"You—" The guard who asked the question pointed his sword at Kent. "State your name or prepare to die."

"I prefer death." Kent didn’t even let him finish before giving his answer. His clothing was more durable than most armor, considering Vexthra personally made it, so it wasn’t like they could break it.
The least they could do was hurt him using soul attacks, but thankfully, he was immune to those. And even if he wasn’t, his soul cultivation was at the 11th Tier, so he wasn’t afraid of them.
However, his neck and head were his only concerns. Thankfully, he had all the energy in the world to protect those. So, when the five guards attacked, he wasn’t afraid of them hitting his vitals.
Basically, he had become so powerful that attacks from Peak Sovereigns who wielded both spiritual qi and Chaos qi couldn’t penetrate his defenses.
"Let’s keep him occupied until the chief arrives. I’ve already informed him," one of the guards said before they resumed attacking him.
Kent just let them bombard him with attacks for close to five minutes until the guards came to a stop again.
"What should we do?" one of them asked.
"If he is from the alliance of the two tribes, we cannot let him leave here alive."
"But our attacks aren’t working, and the chief is also not here yet. What should we do?"
Unbeknownst to the five guards, the chief they were waiting for was standing 30 miles away, watching the battle with a calm expression on his face.
Behind him stood three individuals, all sitting at the peak of the Core Formation Stage. They were the three elders of the Bloodvein Tribe.
One was an old woman. She had deep red skin and long, dark hair. Naturally, because of her age, her features were slightly weathered.
The second elder was a hulking figure with features that screamed brute fighter. His muscular body was covered in chaotic tattoos, and his arms were thick and perfect for punching.
The last was also a man, with a slender figure—his form perfect for a swordsman. He carried a sword sheathed in black leather, a clear sign of his commitment to the sword path.
The tribe’s Chief stood 7 feet tall and had a muscular body, graceful like that of a warrior wielding an axe in battle. All four were of an age that showed they had been around for a long time.
The experience and strength in their gaze said it all...they are powerful beings.
"What do you three think?" he asked.
"I think he’s looking down on our guards. Just look at how smug he looks," the brute answered, revealing his blunt personality.
"I think so too," the old lady seconded.
"I think he didn’t want to kill them. And while he looks smug, I don’t think he’s mocking them—I believe it’s just a taunt to keep them attacking him.
This can only mean one thing..."
"He is a body cultivator, and their attacks are tempering his body," the Tribe Chief said, looking in Kent’s direction.
"Then what should we do?" the old lady asked. "If he isn’t here to kill our people, then what is he here for?"
"Why don’t we find out? But be ready. While he poses no threat, we don’t know his true objective yet, so we can only be prepared for anything."
The four vanished from where they stood.
Back at the border, Kent stood there, taking on the attacks from the five guards. After a while, he stopped feeling anything. Their attacks weren’t doing anything to him anymore.
However, since he had been warned not to kill the Bloodveins, he could only stand there and let them bombard him with attacks that could easily kill a Core Formation expert.
"Enough."
Suddenly, a voice filled the battleground, halting the steps of the five guards. They turned around and bowed.
"Tribe Chief. Elders."

The Tribe Chief stared at them with all three of his eyes and then turned to Kent, who stood there dusting his clothes like four beings who could bring the Althea Kingdom to its knees weren’t staring at him.
"I am Malthar Bloodseer, the Tribe Chief of the Bloodvein Tribe," the Tribe Chief introduced himself, then turned to the three elders.
"These are the three elders of the Bloodvein Tribe: Farra, Ureth, and Zarka. May we know who you are and what you are doing in our domain?" Tribe Chief Malthar asked after introducing the elders.
Kent looked at the four powerful beings and then smiled.
"I am Kent Madson, Envoy of the Mother of Killers, Shara."
The expressions of Malthar and the three elders changed when they heard what Kent said.

chapters.title: Chapter 519: Envoy of the Mother of Killers [Bonus]
paragraphs: Sitting at the core of the Universe, the beautiful lady smirked, which soon turned into a cute little laughter.
"This brat, how can he always find ways to make a joke where he is required to be serious?" she said to herself, watching Kent smile at the four figures.
"They should kick his ass to teach him a lesson." She could only wish, but her wish could not change anything unless she intervened, which, in that case, would cause more harm than good.
So, since that was the case, she could only watch the amusement Kent was giving her and laugh to her heart’s content.
Back in the Dead Region, Tribe Chief Malthar extended his finger, causing a blood-type energy to appear on it, locking onto Kent’s body.
"Are you mocking our god?" he asked, looking coldly at Kent.
The three elders weren’t taking the sudden comment from Kent too simply. Farra retrieved a whip made of metallic rope, while Zarka pulled his sword from its sheath.
As for Ureth, his fists were coated in the same red energy as Tribe Chief Malthar’s finger.
"Who said I was mocking your god? Do you think I am that stupid?" Kent wasn’t showing any sign of panic, knowing that he could easily escape when it came to it.
The quest clearly stated that the end justifies the means. He could save the Bloodvein Tribe regardless of whether they let him into their domain.
"You clearly stated you are the envoy of our god. Do you think anyone would believe that? Our tribe has followed and upheld the teachings of our god and mother for thousands of years.
In those thousands of years, a male envoy of our god has never been mentioned. So, do you also think we are stupid?"
’Well, I totally forgot the 13 Guards of Rakshasa are all women.’ Kent smiled in his head.

Shara, the mother of killers, later became Rakshasa, the Scarlet Fang—the Daughter of Battle. It was then that she picked the 13 guards who ensured her name and teachings never died, even to this day.
So naturally, her followers would know of the 13 guards, meaning he had made a blunder choosing to enter the tribe as an envoy.

’I should have taken on the appearance of a lady. That would have solved everything.’ Kent smiled, knowing his next words would determine whether he would escape or enter the domain of the Bloodvein Tribe.
"I don’t care whether you believe me or not. But I am the envoy of the Mother of Killers, and she sent me here to save you from a calamity that will soon befall you.
Whether you believe me or not, I am here at her command, and as such, I will do just that. I have no beef with any of you, so be sure to take that to heart before you make your next move."
He ended his sentence with a smile while waiting for the attacks. However, after five minutes, none of the four Bloodveins attacked.
This gave him their answer.
"I know you still don’t believe me, but I am not lying. I was sent here to help your tribe.
Now, as to whether we can sit down and talk peacefully, you have to know that I wasn’t lying when I said I am an envoy from the Mother of Killers.

She sensed your fate and felt your pain, so she sent me here to help. I want no trouble with your kind, so even if you don’t want me in your domain, I only ask that you don’t come against me when I start making my moves.
It would be great if we fought on the same side. But if you don’t want that, I can complete my mission without your intervention."
The three elders turned to the Tribe Leader, waiting for his judgment.
"You are right. We don’t trust you. However, that doesn’t mean we will become hostile and turn you away."
"Even if there is the slightest chance you are telling the truth, we wouldn’t want to invoke the wrath of our god by killing you.
So we will take you to our tribe, where you will be questioned. If the outcome is satisfactory, we will listen to you again."
Kent smiled, hearing the Tribe Leader say that. "That’s the spirit. Now, why don’t you lead the way?"
"Not so fast," Elder Farra said, appearing before Kent. Her whip moved, and before he could react, his hands were bound by the metallic rope.
A powerful Chaos energy entered the whip, creating a rather intense binding force around Kent.
"If you don’t resist, you won’t feel any pain," Elder Farra said, staring coldly at him.
Kent just smiled. "Oh, trust me, I have no plans of resisting."
His smile wasn’t because anything was funny—no, it was more due to the message that appeared before him.
⟪Your comprehension of Chaos Qi has improved moderately⟫
’Her Chaos Qi is much more potent than the five guards,’ Kent said inwardly as he was lifted off the ground and began flying toward the tribe.
He was circulating his blood, absorbing the constant stream of Chaos Qi running through the whip. Sadly, the flight was so fast that it took them just five minutes to arrive.
For a region famous for being one of the most dangerous places in the world, they sure were living in a rather luxurious setting.
Though not as majestic as the outside world, they had solid buildings, and the design wasn’t bad. The tribe was located in a valley with a river of blood running through both sides.

Kent didn’t want to offend anyone, so he refrained from using his senses. When they arrived at the tribe, every single gaze turned in their direction. They were all staring at Kent, who was bound by Elder Farra’s whip.
"Who is that?" many began to ask, but the elders and the Tribe Chief flew straight toward a larger, castle-like building.
Kent, now the center of attention, could only watch the thousands of Bloodveins, all of whom had red skin and, most notably, red hair.
Of course, some had deeper shades of red skin than others, but they all shared that crimson tone.
Kent and the elders arrived at the Bloodvein Tribe’s palace, which they entered through a tall door. The moment they stepped in, Elder Farra freed Kent, making him sit on a chair.
"Summon the Priestess," Tribe Chief Malthar commanded, and a guard went running.

chapters.title: Chapter 520: Velyra, Priestess of the Bloodvein Tribe [Bonus]
paragraphs: The design of the throne room wasn’t too lavish, but it wasn’t too ugly. One could say they used what they had and made something grand out of it.
Kent was seated in a stone chair that looked and felt more comfortable than one could expect. His seat was on the left side of the Tribe Chief.
The elders were on the right, showing the hierarchy and power disparity.
A few minutes after they arrived, the large door opened again, allowing a lady to enter.
From where Kent was seated, he saw the lady with red skin—just like the rest of the Bloodveins—enter the throne room with careful steps.
She was clad in a white gown that, considering its bagginess, ensured none of her features were on display.
Per her dressing, it was no coincidence she was called Priestess.
She had long, dark silver hair that fell down her back, red pupils that highlighted her Bloodvein heritage, and sharp facial features that made her rather cute for someone dressed in baggy clothes.
This time, Kent used his Enchanted Eyes to see her status page and perhaps glean a few hidden details about her.
Unfortunately for him, what he wanted to see and what he was given weren’t really much.
⟦Name: Velyra Bloodseer⟧
⟦Cultivation: Peak Core Formation (3/7)⟧
⟦Class: Priestess⟧
⟦Sub-class: Blood Swordsman⟧
→ Velyra is the only daughter of the Tribe Chief of the Bloodveins. She is also the most cherished princess of the Bloodveins.
→ They hold her in high esteem, so while using your eye to spy on her may seem harmless, you might want to ask her permission first.
’What in the world?’ Kent was taken aback, but he acted composedly, considering this was the first time this had happened. He didn’t know how it happened, but he didn’t panic.
’Tower. What just happened?’
⟪Not sure, but there is one possibility. The lady you are spying on is someone loved by the universe. If that is the case, then it’s clear the universe doesn’t want you peeking into her business.⟫

’I see. I only hope she wasn’t made aware.’ Kent sighed in his heart, then returned his gaze to the lady who, for a moment there, smiled—or perhaps smirked—at Kent, making the Chaos Dragon wonder if she knew.
’So what if she knew? I doubt she will out me to her pops.’ Thankfully, nothing like that happened as the lady walked to the right side of her father and sat down.
"This is the Priestess of the Bloodvein Tribe and also my daughter, Velyra," Tribe Chief Malthar said, causing Kent to nod.
"Nice meeting you, Priestess Velyra." He had to act his part, considering this was the only chance he would have to convince the Bloodvein Tribe they shouldn’t be hostile toward him.
His mission ends in 15 days, so he needed all the cooperation he could get to see it through.
"I am Kent Madson." Kent introduced himself...
"I know," Velyra said, looking strangely at Kent. This, of course, made the dragon narrow his eyes at the lady.
’Why does it feel like she can see right through me?’ Kent wondered, a sudden unease creeping into his spine.
"You are Kent Madson, a man with many identities. Perhaps you would like me to call you Jest. Or do you prefer Chaos instead?"
This time, Kent moved in his chair, and instead of smiling, a frown appeared on his face.
"Who are you?" he asked, not liking where any of this was going at all.
"I am a nobody. Just a lone Priestess of the Bloodvein Tribe, staunch followers of the Mother of Killers, Shara." She smiled as she said that.
"Then how did you know all this stuff about me?" Kent asked.
"You told me," Velyra answered, still maintaining her smile.

"I did no such thing. Today is my first time meeting you, and I don’t forget faces—especially the faces of beautiful women." Kent cut his words short, knowing he wasn’t supposed to extend his sentence that far.
Unfortunately for him, he said the major words already...
Velyra smiled upon hearing that.
"To you, this is our first time meeting. But to me, it’s our second," she sighed. "Don’t worry, I and all who heard what I said will forget it in the next 30 minutes.
However, before that, I would like you to tell me more about the Mother of Killers."
Kent didn’t want to show it, but hearing that she and the elders would forget his other identities calmed his heart. Hearing his identity from a stranger wasn’t pleasant at all.
Now, he could get back to his mission, but he became more careful around the Priestess, who was still giving him the creeps.
"You want to hear more about the Mother of Killers? Does that mean you believe I am her envoy?" Kent asked.
"I do."
The elders and the Tribe Chief, who heard what she said, turned and looked at Kent, this time with calm expressions. The hostile looks were wiped away, replaced with more considerate ones.
They even showed signs of panic, considering they didn’t exactly handle him like the egg he is when they first met.
"Don’t worry, guys. I don’t hold grudges," Kent said with a smile. His groove returned, though the Priestess was still giving him the creeps.
"As for the Mother of Killers, she is indeed reborn and currently in seclusion, training. Of course, she doesn’t know her true identity yet, but she bears the names Shara and Rakshasa.
She doesn’t know I’m here, for I came under someone else’s order. I can’t talk about the person, but they want me to save your kind simply because you truly believe in the Mother of Killers.
That is why I am here. I am here to help save the followers of Shara from a great calamity."
Kent knew he couldn’t lie in front of the lady for unknown reasons, and he was right.
She had a unique ability that allowed her to know if someone was lying. This made Kent choose to tell the truth—but with limited information.
He wouldn’t want what happened to Vexthra to happen here. Their knowing too much about forbidden things isn’t something he wants to entertain.
He already had enough on his plate to worry about the karmic backlash of an entire race.
"I believe you," Velyra said. "But I want to ask—what makes you think you have what it takes to save us from our enemies?"
"Let’s just say wherever I go, chaos follows," Kent said with a wink.
