From where Kent was seated, he saw the lady with red skin—just like the rest of the Bloodveins—enter the throne room with careful steps.
She was clad in a white gown that, considering its bagginess, ensured none of her features were on display.
Per her dressing, it was no coincidence she was called Priestess.
She had long, dark silver hair that fell down her back, red pupils that highlighted her Bloodvein heritage, and sharp facial features that made her rather cute for someone dressed in baggy clothes.
This time, Kent used his Enchanted Eyes to see her status page and perhaps glean a few hidden details about her.
Unfortunately for him, what he wanted to see and what he was given weren’t really much.
⟦Name: Velyra Bloodseer⟧
⟦Cultivation: Peak Core Formation (3/7)⟧
⟦Class: Priestess⟧
⟦Sub-class: Blood Swordsman⟧
→ Velyra is the only daughter of the Tribe Chief of the Bloodveins.
She is also the most cherished princess of the Bloodveins.
→ They hold her in high esteem, so while using your eye to spy on her may seem harmless, you might want to ask her permission first.
’What in the world?’ Kent was taken aback, but he acted composedly, considering this was the first time this had happened.
He didn’t know how it happened, but he didn’t panic.
’Tower.
What just happened?’
⟪Not sure, but there is one possibility.
The lady you are spying on is someone loved by the universe.
If that is the case, then it’s clear the universe doesn’t want you peeking into her business.⟫
’I see.

I only hope she wasn’t made aware.’ Kent sighed in his heart, then returned his gaze to the lady who, for a moment there, smiled—or perhaps smirked—at Kent, making the Chaos Dragon wonder if she knew.
’So what if she knew?
I doubt she will out me to her pops.’ Thankfully, nothing like that happened as the lady walked to the right side of her father and sat down.
"This is the Priestess of the Bloodvein Tribe and also my daughter, Velyra," Tribe Chief Malthar said, causing Kent to nod.
"Nice meeting you, Priestess Velyra." He had to act his part, considering this was the only chance he would have to convince the Bloodvein Tribe they shouldn’t be hostile toward him.
His mission ends in 15 days, so he needed all the cooperation he could get to see it through.
"I am Kent Madson." Kent introduced himself...
"I know," Velyra said, looking strangely at Kent.
This, of course, made the dragon narrow his eyes at the lady.
’Why does it feel like she can see right through me?’ Kent wondered, a sudden unease creeping into his spine.
"You are Kent Madson, a man with many identities.
Perhaps you would like me to call you Jest.
Or do you prefer Chaos instead?"
This time, Kent moved in his chair, and instead of smiling, a frown appeared on his face.
"Who are you?" he asked, not liking where any of this was going at all.
"I am a nobody.
Just a lone Priestess of the Bloodvein Tribe, staunch followers of the Mother of Killers, Shara." She smiled as she said that.
"Then how did you know all this stuff about me?" Kent asked.
"You told me," Velyra answered, still maintaining her smile.
"I did no such thing.
Today is my first time meeting you, and I don’t forget faces—especially the faces of beautiful women." Kent cut his words short, knowing he wasn’t supposed to extend his sentence that far.
Unfortunately for him, he said the major words already...
Velyra smiled upon hearing that.
"To you, this is our first time meeting.
But to me, it’s our second," she sighed.
"Don’t worry, I and all who heard what I said will forget it in the next 30 minutes.
However, before that, I would like you to tell me more about the Mother of Killers."
Kent didn’t want to show it, but hearing that she and the elders would forget his other identities calmed his heart.
Hearing his identity from a stranger wasn’t pleasant at all.
Now, he could get back to his mission, but he became more careful around the Priestess, who was still giving him the creeps.
"You want to hear more about the Mother of Killers?
Does that mean you believe I am her envoy?" Kent asked.
"I do."
The elders and the Tribe Chief, who heard what she said, turned and looked at Kent, this time with calm expressions.
The hostile looks were wiped away, replaced with more considerate ones.
They even showed signs of panic, considering they didn’t exactly handle him like the egg he is when they first met.
"Don’t worry, guys.
I don’t hold grudges," Kent said with a smile.
His groove returned, though the Priestess was still giving him the creeps.
"As for the Mother of Killers, she is indeed reborn and currently in seclusion, training.
Of course, she doesn’t know her true identity yet, but she bears the names Shara and Rakshasa.
She doesn’t know I’m here, for I came under someone else’s order.
I can’t talk about the person, but they want me to save your kind simply because you truly believe in the Mother of Killers.
That is why I am here.
I am here to help save the followers of Shara from a great calamity."
Kent knew he couldn’t lie in front of the lady for unknown reasons, and he was right.
She had a unique ability that allowed her to know if someone was lying.
This made Kent choose to tell the truth—but with limited information.
He wouldn’t want what happened to Vexthra to happen here.
Their knowing too much about forbidden things isn’t something he wants to entertain.
He already had enough on his plate to worry about the karmic backlash of an entire race.
"I believe you," Velyra said.
"But I want to ask—what makes you think you have what it takes to save us from our enemies?"
"Let’s just say wherever I go, chaos follows," Kent said with a wink.

chapters.title: Chapter 521: Situation Of the Bloodvein Tribe
paragraphs: There was one thing to believe what Kent said, and another for the elders and the tribe chief to trust him with the lives of their tribe.
They just can’t do that despite their priestess saying Kent is indeed the envoy of their god.
However, Kent didn’t really care about that. His mission ends in 15 days, and because of that, he knew he must get his groove on before it was too late.
"I can’t beat my chest and say my being here will solve all your problems. That would just be me being stupid. However, I can say I will do my best to help you.

I can also say that with me here, your tribe won’t fall, not without putting up a good fight. So instead of looking down on me, let’s say for a moment you all see me as someone worthy to help your tribe.
Wouldn’t you want to take me then seriously?"
Kent was only thankful they didn’t become hostile toward him. He knew this was good progress and could be used to his advantage.
The tribe elders and chief were all stronger than him, but he knew he could help them face their enemies if and when it came down to it.
"Father, I think we should believe him," Velyra said after hearing what Kent said. "I mean, what do we have to lose anyway? The alliance surpasses us in both numbers and strength.
Though you are the strongest in this region, I doubt they care too much about that. This can only mean they are confident in stopping you and have even put in measures for the rest of us.
So, from the way I see it, why don’t we have a secret weapon of our own? Kent could be that secret weapon.
You saw something in him, which was why you brought him back instead of killing him like you always do. So why not put some trust in him?"
Both the elders and the tribe chief couldn’t deny Velyra’s words. The enemy clearly didn’t place them in their sights anymore, so they wouldn’t lose anything by making Kent their secret weapon.
As for Kent, being referred to as a secret weapon only made him smile. But he knew the mission took priority here, so he had to take his chance and get the job done.
"Tell us what you want," Tribe Chief Malthar said, staring at Kent.

"Before I say what I want, what can you tell me about this alliance? I want to know the odds I’ve signed up to go against and, if possible, include all the people that are on the same level as you and the three elders."
Kent wanted nothing more than to know the enemy, which, according to the art of warfare, knowing one’s enemy is half the battle won.
"In this region, there are three major tribes: the Bloodvein, which is us; the Dreadclaw, located in the East; and the Soulshroud tribe, which is in the North.

A month ago, we were three major clans ruling over four minor clans, and we had good relationships with each other. However, everything changed when we started losing contact with our men on the outside.
It turns out the two tribes had secretly formed an alliance and had been plotting against us for years. They only bared their fangs a month ago.

Things escalated quickly when they started attacking our businesses and everything owned by our tribe. They weren’t this hostile all these years, and while we were the strongest, we never tried to suppress them.

Now, they are openly hostile toward us, and because of that, we have to seal our borders and stay alert. In a week, they will attack our domain, and while I would love to say we have what it takes to take them on, I don’t have much confidence this time.
The reason being, just like we have me and three tribe elders, they also have their own peak powerhouses.

And I don’t know if you’re aware, but once someone forms their Core at the core formation stage, which shows they are at the peak of their cultivation, there are another seven stages inside the core formation stage alone.
The core that was forming has seven stages. So, even at the core formation stage, this core must undergo seven evolutions, each bigger than the last.
Every evolution makes one’s strength grow by leaps and bounds.
So, two people at the same stage but with different evolution stages cannot be measured using the same strength scale. It is just not possible.
"I am at the 5th evolution, with the elders currently at the 4th. This also applies to the other tribes. They all have the same setup as us."
"Then what makes your tribe the strongest? If what you just said is true, then this means that your strengths were equally matched even before the alliance, right?" Kent asked.

Though he didn’t truly understand the power dynamics in the Dead Region, he had picked up on some details. It appeared the tribes all have the same strength level, so just how is one stronger than the other two?
"It’s true we have the same power level. However, that is just in terms of cultivation. The only reason we are the strongest is because of our understanding of the Chaos Qi.
I know you are already aware of this region’s unique energy, and I’m sure you understand it.
We, the Bloodveins, have a natural affinity for Chaos Qi, and because of that, we are naturally stronger. I have already reached the peak of comprehension in this world, which is the Very High level.

The other tribe chiefs are at the High stage, which is why we are the strongest. However, the fact that they declared war on us shows that they are confident and don’t care about me or my strength at all.
We also suspect they may have some secret weapon that gave them the confidence to match us."
Tribe Chief Malthar sighed. He didn’t want to admit it, but he was afraid, like the rest of his tribe. They all knew that in a week, they would have to fight a great battle.

"This is indeed a unique situation. However, I don’t think you should worry too much. I have some unique skill sets that will allow me to gather more information on them and perhaps make a plan to stop them." Kent said with a smile
"What do you need?" Velyra asked, hearing what Kent said.

chapters.title: Chapter 522: Where Their Fate Came From
paragraphs: "I need somewhere quiet with a high concentration of Chaos Qi. I will stay there for four days to train and prepare," Kent requested, and the Elders turned to Velyra.

"I will take him there." She didn’t need the approval of the tribe chief or the elders. She was the priestess, and they could only hope she was making the right decision if she wanted to take him to her dwelling.
"Before you go, I would like to know if you came with someone else," Tribe Chief Malthar asked.
"Actually, yes. I was in the middle of a battle when I was brought here. My opponent was also transported here with me," Kent answered.
"I guess she wasn’t lying when she said you are her enemy," the tribe chief muttered. "She is currently locked up in our prison cell. If you want, we can take you to her and finish what you started."
"She can wait. I have a much more important mission to handle." Kent didn’t want to look nonchalant, but the fact that he hadn’t even thought of the hunter that much proved he didn’t really hate her.
She was just a pawn in a much bigger game. That was all. So while he would love to kill an enemy, he could also just let her wait a minute while he got his job done first.

"Then, in that case, you should go with my daughter. And Kent, I look forward to seeing how you can help us overcome our predicament." The tribe chief and the elders held a hopeful gaze as Velyra took Kent away.
After leaving the throne room, the elders turned to their chief.
"What should we do now?" Farra, the lady elder with the whip as her go-to weapon, asked.
"There is nothing we can do but wait for the time to come. If we are destined to die, then we can only take as many as we can with us.
Remember, the first rule is killing..."
"Only in death can we stop killing," the elders said.
"This means before we die, we have thousands of means to kill to our heart’s content." The aura of killing radiated from their bodies as they prepared for their upcoming battle against the alliance.
Meanwhile, after leaving the throne room, Velyra led Kent up a certain mountain under the watchful eyes of every person they met or passed by.
"Do you not get enough visitors?" Kent asked.
"We usually kill every human we encounter. You are the second we let in—and the first we allow to move within the tribe."
The first to enter was the hunter, who was taken straight to prison. Kent was the only one without chains.
"Lucky me, I guess," Kent smiled and asked, "If you don’t mind me asking, where did your belief in the Mother of Killers come from?"

"Don’t get me wrong, I am not questioning your belief in the Mother of Killers, but I know for a fact the Mother of Killers isn’t from this world. So if that’s the case, where did this belief come from?"
The Mother of Killers was an entity who went by many names.
Before she was Shara, she was Zhara, who lived in the city of the strong, Vashrakar. She was born in battle and lived for battle.
Vashrakar wasn’t a place in these lands. The world she is from is a high world—and a very dangerous one. So, having people in a world she perhaps hadn’t even heard of was a rather unique situation.
This caught Kent’s curiosity, so he wanted to understand.
"Before our god died, she picked thirteen guards who later became her envoys. They move through thousands of worlds, saving people in the name of Shara.
Our race was one of such.
I don’t know if you know, but the Bloodvein tribe isn’t from this world. We are from a different world, but had to relocate here due to the war.
One tribe is just one of many in the millions of worlds in the universe."
"Let me guess—you were saved by a follower of the Mother of Killers, and as such, your tribe adopted the believed and started walking the path of killers," Kent said, and Velyra nodded.
"We were indeed saved by one of her envoys, and for thousands of years, we lived in harmony with our neighbours. However, it turns out peace can only last for so long."
Velyra took a deep sigh, saying that.
Kent didn’t immediately say anything. Instead, he decided to let her have her moment before asking the second major question.
After a while, he asked,
"Nobody declares a war without making a demand. So, if you don’t mind me asking, what are they asking for?" Kent asked, and Velyra suddenly stopped, the air around her changing from calm to fury.
"Those bastards." For someone who was supposed to be a priestess, her aura was rather sinister. She felt nothing more than a trained killer who had killed a lot of men.
"No offence, but I just wanted to know," Kent reiterated, not wanting to be the recipient of her fury. Velyra, of course, knew that, so she calmed down and decided to answer.

"They want our most prized possession—something we cannot give to anyone. I can’t tell you what it is, but know that if we hand this item to them, we might as well hand our lives to them on a silver platter.
That is something we cannot do. So if it’s war they want, then they should come. We have nothing to fear here."
Kent didn’t say anything anymore and just followed her up the mountain.
Inwardly, though, Kent was having a nice chat with the tower.
’What is this item she is talking about?’ Kent asked the tower.
⟪It’s called the Blood Heart Stone. It’s a fist-sized crystal containing high-level blood energy and the essence of a mighty beast called Valthoroth, the Bloodthirsty Serpent.
Absorbing it would not only elevate your bloodline, but it would also grant you unique innate abilities like Regeneration, Blood Manipulation, and more.⟫
’I guess they have a reason to keep it locked up. I wonder if they’ll be willing to let me have it.’
Kent smiled, thinking about that. A short while later, they arrived at a house sitting at the peak of the mountain. The moment they entered, Kent felt a shift in the air.
Without even doing anything, but only breathing, a message appeared...
⟪Your comprehension of Chaos Qi has improved moderately⟫

chapters.title: Chapter 523: Comprehending Chaos Qi
paragraphs: Kent’s understanding of Chaos Qi started to rise just by breathing, shocking him. Velyra noticed his surprised look, so she addressed it.
"This house is right atop a major source of Chaos energy underground. This is why the Chaos energy here is very potent," she explained, and Kent nodded.
"Lucky me, I guess." His smile said it all; he was happy, and Velyra could see that.
"You can head down as your comprehension progresses. However, with only the few days you requested, I doubt you’ll be able to do much.
Also, know that you can’t force it, since cultivating in a highly concentrated space with a low comprehension level can cause your body to explode."
Kent smiled and then responded, "I know, and don’t worry. I have no plans to kill myself by jumping into the dense chaos energy."
Of course, he knew he wouldn’t die even if the concentration were much more potent. His bloodline is much more potent...
But he can’t reveal that, so he can only use the baby steps formula to get what he wants.
Velyra didn’t say anything. She just turned to her left and formed an orb that flew and touched the walls of the room, creating a protection barrier around the room.
"I have sealed the room, so don’t worry about getting disturbed. In that case, I will be heading down," Velyra said before walking away.
Kent didn’t want to use his Enchanted eyes on her after what happened the first time, so he just let her go. But he could tell by a glance that she was at a high comprehension stage.
This made her much more dangerous than she appeared.
Unlike her father, who had already attained five evolutions and a very high level of Chaos Qi comprehension, she had only achieved three evolutions.
It’s not that Kent underestimated her, but he knew she couldn’t kill him, at least not as easily as he might want it to happen.
Kent sat down and started cultivating. He had four days to spare before he started making his moves, which meant he had just four days to take his comprehension to the next level or higher.
⟪Your comprehension of Chaos Qi has improved moderately⟫
Seven hours later, Kent stopped receiving the messages, meaning the Chaos Qi in his space wasn’t affecting him anymore, so he moved to a new spot.
The path leading to the ground level was large and cozy enough for him to cultivate, so he moved a couple of steps down, sat, and resumed his cultivation.

chapters.title: Chapter 524: Medium Level Comprehension, Helping Velyra [Bonus]
paragraphs: Three days passed in the blink of an eye.
All over the Bloodvein Tribe, thousands of warriors were on high alert, ready for the battle that was about to come.
They knew it would be hard, but they weren’t backing down or bowing to their enemies, even if they all
would die from this battle.
Not even their dead bodies would do that. They are prepared to die.
So they were preparing.
There were about 10,000 inhabitants in the Bloodvein Tribe. However, only 7,000 were fit to go to war.
They were protectors meant to shield the weak, so these 7,000 warriors would decide the battle yet to come.
Out of the 7000 warriors, 5000 were below the Root Transcendent stage.
1,500 were in the Root Transcendent stage, ranging from level 1 to 9, which was the peak. Naturally, they would do more than the 5,000.
However, they also didn’t have much standing in the army, considering a capable enough Root Ascension stage expert could handle dozens of them.

Among the remaining 500, 300 were Root Ascension, and 194 were Root Sovereigns. The ones left were the Tribe Chief, three elders, Velyra, and the commander of their army, who was also a Core Formation expert.
He was almost on the same level as the three elders, making him stronger than Velyra. However, even with six of them, the chances of facing double or triple those odds were just too much.
However, they were the Bloodveins. They wouldn’t hold the title of the strongest if they weren’t brave enough to go into battle against such a force.
The only upside was that the battle would happen in their domain, where they were the strongest. So, they could only wait for their enemies to come.
Meanwhile, Kent had already progressed in the pool and was now in the same spot as Velyra. His comprehension had also shown tremendous growth.
Thankfully, after three days since he started, he had finally achieved the second stage in his comprehension.
⟪Your comprehension of Chaos Qi has improved dramatically. You have reached the Medium stage.⟫
⟪You have unlocked 10% of your Bloodline.⟫
The moment these messages appeared, Kent felt his control of the chaos qi grow much stronger. His bloodline had also strengthened, taking his speed and strength to the next level.
’I am nearing my next limit. I wonder what the tower will suggest next,’ Kent smiled, feeling his strength soar to new heights.
The first limit was broke using the golden titan stairway. Now, he started to wonder what the next thing would be required of him to break the next limit.
Velyra, who was a few steps away from Kent, sensed that something had changed about him. This caused her to pay more attention, and to her shock, Kent had made a breakthrough.
’He has only achieved a Medium level in Chaos Qi cultivation, yet he was able to get this far into the pool. Just who is this young man?’ Velyra wondered, staring at Kent.
Kent noticed her gaze, so he turned toward her.
"You don’t mind if I go deeper?" Kent asked with a guilty smile. He knew he was asking for too much, considering he hadn’t even done anything for them yet.
However, he planned on helping them, so this was just him taking his payment in advance. Velyra nodded and focused back on her training. However, this time she started paying more attention to Kent.
To her shock, Kent moved deeper into the pool and for four hours, he continued to cultivate. He cultivated until he couldn’t go any deeper, simply because he was at the end of the pool.
He sighed and then moved back.
"This pool can’t help me anymore, unfortunately." While Kent was looking down because his training ended abruptly, Velyra was staring at him with a shocked expression.
’Only Father managed to get to the end, but it took him forty years. Just how monstrous is his talent? And he only reached the Medium level.’
’Father must know about this.’
Velyra was contemplating whether to inform her father. However, before she could move, Kent spoke.
"If you don’t mind, I can help speed up your cultivation if you allow me." Kent’s request caught her off guard.
"What do you mean by you can help me?" she asked.
"I meant it like it sounds. You’re at the ’High level,’ even sitting at the peak. I want to help you advance to the Very High level.
This way, your strength will reach the level of the elders, despite your cultivation being below theirs."
"Are you being serious?" she asked, half-trusting him, waiting for Kent to say he was just messing with her.
Unbeknownst to her, Kent wasn’t offering simply because he suddenly had the inspiration to do so. He offered because he had received a minor quest with a rather generous reward.
This time, he was even allowed to accept or reject the quest. He accepted it, since it was just a minor task for him. He still had a few hours left in his four-day window anyway.
"It will take just a few hours, so we’d better get started," Kent said, moving and stopping behind her.
"Relax your body and feel my energy flow through you. Tap into that flow, and then circulate the Chaos Qi along," he instructed.
Before she could ask a question, Kent placed both palms on her back and began channelling his energy into her body.
Velyra tried to resist at first; however, when she tried, she realised she couldn’t, so she began following the flow of energy circulating through her body.
Then, just as Kent had told her, she began circulating the Chaos Qi along the channels of Kent’s energy.

’This is...’ To her shock, her comprehension started improving rapidly by following Kent’s flow. It took just a few minutes, but something that would have taken her months was being accomplished in mere moments.
’Just who is this young man?’
She could only wonder. Five hours later, a wave of Chaos Qi exploded out of her body, signalling that she had finally stepped into the Very High level.
"Congratulations on your breakthrough," Kent said with a smile, watching her examine her body as he moved back.
After a few minutes, she walked toward Kent and bowed.
"Thanks for your help. I will never forget it," she said, but Kent just smiled and replied,
"Trust me, I will also never forget, too."
Naturally, when Velyra bowed, the twin melons greeted Kent. As a man of culture, moments like this can never be forgotten—not even amnesia could take that memory from him.

chapters.title: Chapter 525: Learning about the Alliance [Bonus]
paragraphs: After helping Velyra break through in her Chaos Qi comprehension, Kent left the pool and used his alchemy flames to dry himself, then climbed back to the house.
He had already achieved his objective, so the next thing left for him to do was to start his mission, which, if his calculations were right, would end in under two weeks.
Velyra joined him a few minutes later, wearing a thankful gaze.
"Once again, thank you for helping me," she said, but Kent just smiled. It wasn’t much of a big deal anyway, so he could only let her have her moment.
He had already received his reward, which he planned to use right after the discussion he was about to have with her.
"If you don’t mind me asking, how strong are the two major tribes coming after your tribe?" Kent asked.
Velyra sat down and took a deep sigh.
"The Dreadclaw Tribe are a tribe of demihumans. They have a bloodline of beasts, so despite their human nature, the majority of their bodies are made of beastly features.
Their most notable and perhaps strongest feature is their claws. They have an affinity for the lightning element, just like how we do with the blood element.
However, some have the ability to transform into a full beast mode. That is especially true for the tribe chief and his bloodline.
They are more like royalty, and thanks to the chaos energy in the air, they are much more powerful than one might think.
However, they still pale in comparison to the Soulshroud Tribe.
The Soulshroud Tribe are descended from the Soulbinders, an ancient race that made pacts with the spirits of the dead to gain control over the power of souls.
Their bloodline allows them to see, hear, and interact with spirits, as well as control them and even draw on their power for strength.
I don’t know if you have soul refiners in your world, but the Soulshroud Tribe is famous for its refinement. It can refine souls into weapons and even craft them into useful skills.
They are the most feared when it comes to soul arts. They even have someone in the tribe who has refined a powerful weapon for the tribe’s chief, allowing him to be just a step below Father.
I don’t know how we’re going to face them, but from their strength alone, I don’t see a path beyond our doom." She sighed again, looking into the distance, watching the activities going on below.
"Sounds like these two are my target this time. With the big fishes these two tribes taken care of, can your tribe finish the job?" Kent asked.
"Even if one of them is taken care of, we can handle the others. As for the minor clans, we don’t pay much attention to them, considering they are much weaker than the major ones.
"In that case, I will head to the Dreadclaw Tribe. Something tells me they will be more of a threat than the Soulshrouds," Kent smiled.
He was confident in his ability to render the Soulshroud army useless, especially since he had just received the means to do so.
"Are you sure about that? The Dreadclaw Tribe is full of powerful demihumans. I know this because, while the Soulshroud Tribe is scary, their physical form is not that strong.
So if you want to do something to weaken them, you might want to start there."
Kent laughed, knowing she was right in that aspect. If he needed to weaken them, he could just visit the race that didn’t have much resistance to physical attacks.
She knew Kent was powerful after spending time training with him inside the pool, so despite his weaker cultivation base, she knew she could trust him.
But going to a tribe full of brutes didn’t look too good for him, especially when the tribe chief of the Dreadclaw Tribe was more monstrous than one could compare.
"Call it a gut feeling, but I sense the Soulshroud Tribe won’t pose much of a threat in future battles.
I have plans to handle them, so I will first go to the Dreadclaw Tribe. They are the priority here."
Kent didn’t even bother explaining further, knowing he would show what he had planned later.
"When are you leaving, then?" Velyra asked.

In response, Kent stood up and began walking toward the entrance. "I plan on ending the mission faster so I can relax. This means I must leave now. But before that, I must first see your father and elders."
"Do you need help?" Velyra asked, but Kent shook his head. His plan didn’t need much interference from anyone, regardless of their strength. He had to work on his own if he wanted to finish faster.
"Thanks for the offer, but I must do this alone." Velyra expected that answer, so she didn’t hold it against him.
"Then let’s go see Father. I have a feeling they are expecting you." Kent and Velyra left and soon entered the throne room, where the tribe chief and the three elders were waiting for him.
"How was your training?" Tribe Chief Malthar asked.
"It went better than I expected. Thank you for letting me train here," Kent responded, and the tribe chief nodded. He had nothing to lose either way.
They would battle in the coming days, with or without Kent’s presence. This meant they were prepared for all outcomes.
Although Kent was regarded as their god’s envoy, the tribe did not place much hope in him.
This did not reflect a lack of faith in their god, but rather an acknowledgment that their god had not personally sent Kent, prompting them to rely on their own strength and teachings.
"So, what is your plan now that you are done training?" Elder Farra asked.

"I plan on going to the Dreadclaw Tribe to handle a few issues there. I was told they are one of the major tribes here, and since they are in cohort with the Soulshroud Tribe, I will visit them first."
The elders and the tribe chief exchanged glances but made no further comments. Shortly afterwards, Kent departed from the Bloodvein Tribe and headed east toward the territory of the Dreadclaw Clan.

"Do you need help?" Velyra asked, but Kent shook his head.
His plan didn’t need much interference from anyone, regardless of their strength.
He had to work on his own if he wanted to finish faster.
"Thanks for the offer, but I must do this alone." Velyra expected that answer, so she didn’t hold it against him.
"Then let’s go see Father.
I have a feeling they are expecting you." Kent and Velyra left and soon entered the throne room, where the tribe chief and the three elders were waiting for him.
"How was your training?" Tribe Chief Malthar asked.
"It went better than I expected.
Thank you for letting me train here," Kent responded, and the tribe chief nodded.
He had nothing to lose either way.
They would battle in the coming days, with or without Kent’s presence.
This meant they were prepared for all outcomes.
Although Kent was regarded as their god’s envoy, the tribe did not place much hope in him.
This did not reflect a lack of faith in their god, but rather an acknowledgment that their god had not personally sent Kent, prompting them to rely on their own strength and teachings.
"So, what is your plan now that you are done training?" Elder Farra asked.
"I plan on going to the Dreadclaw Tribe to handle a few issues there.
I was told they are one of the major tribes here, and since they are in cohort with the Soulshroud Tribe, I will visit them first."
The elders and the tribe chief exchanged glances but made no further comments.
Shortly afterwards, Kent departed from the Bloodvein Tribe and headed east toward the territory of the Dreadclaw Clan.

chapters.title: Chapter 526: Skill Modification Token
paragraphs: When Kent left, the tribe elders turned to Velyra.
"What do you think? Does he have the means to help us?" Elder Ureth, the brute among the elders, asked.
"I don’t know if he can, but I know he will try," Velyra answered with a strange expression. This caused the elders to stare at each other.
"You sound like you’ve known him for years. Don’t tell me spending a few days with him has softened your heart," Tribe Chief Malthar said with a smile.

"Be serious, Father," Velyra smiled. "I don’t know who he is or what he is, but this young man has proven to me that there are those beyond talented. Can you believe he touched the wall in the Chaos Pool?"
"WHAT?"
Both the tribe chief and the elders exclaimed upon hearing what Velyra said. "Did you just say he touched the wall?" Elder Zarka asked, looking visibly shocked.
"Yes. I saw him move through to the end of the pool, and it happened in less than a day after he stepped inside the pool."
"Does that mean he is on the same level as the Tribe Chief?" Elder Farra asked. In the entire Bloodvein Tribe, only the tribe chief had managed to get to the other end of the Chaos Pool.
Nobody else had managed to do that, so hearing Kent had done the impossible made them question if he had indeed reached the level of the tribe chief.
"No. He is still at the Medium Level. However, the same cannot be said for me." Velyra unleashed her Chaos Qi, causing the elders and the tribe chief to jump to their feet.
"How?" they all asked.

They considered Velyra a genius among geniuses; however, even with her talent, they knew she wouldn’t be able to reach the ’Very High’ level for at least another ten years. So the sudden jump to that stage took them aback.
"Kent helped me. I don’t know how, but he used his energy to open channels in my body, allowing me to channel the Chaos Qi through those pathways.
It was like a unique cultivation method made for Chaos Qi cultivation. It took him just a few hours to help me step into the ’Very High’ stage."

The elders could only look at Velyra with expressions of both happiness and shock. They were happy for her, knowing that with her breakthrough, they had gained yet another powerhouse who could do more than her previous self.
Velyra saw their expressions and smiled.
"This is why we don’t know much about him, but I believe we can trust him. Now, we can only prepare and hope for good news from him," she added.
The elders and her father nodded. They trusted the priestesses of their race, so they must trust her words and hope for the best.
Meanwhile, Kent, who had caused the elders and the tribe chief great shock, was now speeding toward the eastern part of the Dead Region.
His wings were now much more sturdy and robust, allowing him to move at great speed through the air. His focus now was to infiltrate the Dreadclaw Tribe and work his magic there.
He planned to find out what they were hiding and whether they possessed something that gave them the confidence to challenge the Bloodvein Tribe.
Kent knew he could not wage war on them alone, so he had to plan well and hope the execution worked.
"Now would be the best time to check how useful my reward from the quest is," he said, accessing the tower interface and opening the reward panel.
Inside, he saw the reward:
⟪Name: Skill Modification Token⟫
→ You can modify any skill of your choice and either edit already given abilities or add new ones.
→ The usefulness of the new ability will depend on how broad your imagination is.
"This is a good item. The question now is, which of my skills should I modify?" he thought deeply as he glided through the clouds, hiding behind the misty gases.

"Both the Blink and 72 String Sovereign Strike are at the Heaven grade, and it’s not like I readily need them, considering my speed now can rival the 5,000 meters I can Blink, and my sword techniques are also robust.

Meaning I have to choose between Elemental Lord, which is also a Heaven grade skill, and the Soul Mapping Arts. Right now, I have the highest chance of gaining more from soul skills, so I’ll go with the Soul Mapping Arts."
Kent decided, already knowing what to add to the Soul Mapping Arts. At the moment, it had three abilities.
[Soul Brand] allows him to brand any soul and keep them within a 10-mile radius of himself.
Then there’s [Soul Lock], a skill that lets him lock a 100-meter radius around him. Those caught within this confinement cannot leave.
Of course, those with higher soul cultivation can escape. But those below Kent’s soul cultivation would have their souls extinguished if they tried to leave.
Then there’s the last one, [Soul Bomb]. This allows him to go further with the Soul Brand. Those he imprints on can have their brand transformed into a bomb that he can detonate at will.
This only works on souls below Kent’s cultivation stage. This means those below the Tier 11 stage are at risk of having their souls destroyed with a snap of his fingers.
He had already used it multiple times, but this time, he wanted to take it a step further.
If possible, he wanted to see if he could make the skill so powerful that even those at the same level as him—but weaker in soul essence—could be affected.
Kent knew the only way to keep up with his enemies was to have abilities that transcended common sense. If possible, he would love to ensure his enemies cried blood when facing him.
"If I add one more ability to it, wouldn’t that be wonderful?" Kent muttered.
"Since I don’t have a soul cultivation path yet, I can only use this skill to the best of my abilities." Kent decided to go ahead and use the Skill Modification Token on the Soul Mapping Arts skill.
The moment he chose the skill, a prompt appeared that made him smile.

chapters.title: Chapter 527: Upgrading Soul Mapping Arts Skill
paragraphs: ⟪You have selected the skill: Soul Mapping Art to be modified⟫
⟪Requirement met. You have three options to choose from⟫
→ Modify any two of the three abilities (Soul Brand, Soul Lock, and Soul Bomb)
→ Upgrade to Mythic Grade
→ Add two new abilities to the skill
"Hmm. I will go for the third option." Kent chose to add two new abilities to the skill. He most certainly didn’t know if the second option would add new abilities after the upgrade.
However, he knew what he wanted, and that was to add two new abilities to his skill. He also knows that if his newly added abilities are robust enough, the skill will upgrade on its own.
⟪You have two slots to add two new abilities. Just give the name of the skill and how it works. The tower will handle the rest⟫
Kent sighed deeply and relaxed his nerves before speaking the name and description of the first ability he would be adding.
"Skill name: Soul Execution Blade," Kent said, then went ahead to give the description.
"It should allow me to summon a spectral blade forged from condensed soul energy. The stronger my soul, the sturdier the sword summoned is.
Depending on how strong my soul is, I should be able to summon more than a dozen swords at a time. Also, when just one is summoned, it should be more powerful.
It should be robust enough to target any branded soul across space (up to 10 km). The longer my soul sensing range expands, the longer this limit is extended too.
Lastly, the skill should directly ignore physical defense and attack the soul core."
Kent finished the description, knowing all loopholes were covered and plans for future evolutions were added.
Now, he could summon more than one sword and even extend the attacking range as his soul grew stronger. Basically, this ability grows as his soul or the grade of the skill advances.
⟪First ability recorded. You can give the information about the second ability⟫
"Name of the ability is Netherstorm Howl."
"The skill should allow me to release a wide-ranging psychic scream that shatters weaker souls within a 10-mile radius.
The closer the person is to me, the stronger the effect on them.
Those who survive become disoriented, hallucinate, or go mad.
To end it, add a special effect called Soul Corruption. This should make the infected targets lose control of soul-based skills for a few seconds."
Kent again described his skill, and the expected result included everything he wanted. He also made sure no loophole was left here.
A second later, the tower was done, and Kent felt two new abilities added to his skill, which had changed from Soul Mapping Art to Soul Dominion Arts.
⟪Modifications complete. Your skill has evolved⟫
⟪Soul Mapping Arts → Soul Dominion Arts⟫
⟪Grade: Mystical → Mythic⟫
You have unlocked new potential within your soul-based combat path.
⟪Updated Ability Set:⟫
1. Soul Brand
→ Implants a hidden mark on the soul of any target within a 14-mile range and below the user’s tier.
→ Now resists most stealth or soul-concealing treasures.
→ Tracking Radius: Scales with soul tier.
2. Soul Lock
→ Locks a 100-meter space with soul energy.
→ Unauthorized exit or entry causes searing soul-burn every second.
→ Effect: Soul Paralysis - chance to freeze weaker soul techniques.
3. Soul Bomb
→ Implants a soul-core detonator into branded souls.
→ Snap of fingers = detonation.
→ Can now detonate souls within a 14-mile radius.
⟪New Abilities:⟫
4. Soul Execution Blade
→ Summons one or multiple blades of soul-forged energy.
→ Can strike any branded soul within 14 miles (scales with soul sense).
→ Pierces space, bypasses armor, and attacks the soul core directly.
→ Special Effect: Soul Severance - limits soul recovery for 1 hour.
5. Netherstorm Howl
→ Emits a massive psychic scream in a 10-mile radius.
→ Kills weaker targets, drives stronger ones insane.
→ Effect: Soul Corruption - disables soul-based skills for 10 seconds.
"Perfect. With this, only a few can withstand my wrath." Kent smiled as he continued moving toward the east of the Dead Region. He didn’t know if the Soulshroud Tribe had souls stronger than Tier 11.
However, even if they did, it wasn’t like they could hurt him. This meant he could easily kill those at Tier 10 and below, and find ways to handle those at Tier 11 and perhaps even Tier 12.
Not that he cared about them much.
His plan now was to get to the Dreadclaw Tribe as fast as he could.
On his way, he started thinking of his ladies, so he asked the tower:
"Tower, how are my wives doing?"

⟪They are out of seclusion and now climbing the stairway. It seems the herbs used in tempering their bodies have helped them greatly, considering they’re only a few steps away from reaching the Gold Body stage.⟫
Kent smiled, hearing that.
"Is any of them closer to the 300th step?" he had to know, considering he had reached that stage and gotten the Body Transcendence Pill.
If they got one—perhaps, if they hadn’t yet—they would be drawing close to reaching their first limit, which, when broken, would make them much more powerful.
But aside from wanting to know where they were, he also wanted to see if any of his ladies could surpass him.

⟪Lady Vari is three steps away from the 300th step. Lady Lani, Nara, Elsa, and Neomi are on the 269th step, while Selene, Mara, Camilla, and Ingrid are on the 256th step. Unity, Lilian, Val, Elaine and Alina are on the 235th step.⟫
"Wait, when did Elaine join the training?" Kent asked. She wasn’t part when he left, so when did she join?
⟪It happened a few days after you left. The goddess brought her to join the training⟫
"I see. It seems Vexthra is doing a good job with them," Kent said with a big smile.
While it had only been two weeks for him, months had already passed inside the tower, and it was clearly reflected in their training.
⟪Also, Zaila will be out of the Nightmare Chamber three days from now,⟫ the tower added, and Kent came to a stop abruptly.
"Looks like I won’t be there to welcome her. I guess I’ll make it up to her when I return." He resumed his flight the next second.
It will take three days for him and 72 days for his ladies. This means he won’t be able to be there when Zaila comes out.
After five hours, he was nearing the borders of the Dreadclaw Tribe, so he landed and decided to walk the next couple of miles.
He planned to get inside the tribe without revealing his identity, so he started moving in slowly, with plans forming in his mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 528: Infiltrating the Dreadclaw Tribe
paragraphs: "Velyra wasn’t exaggerating when she said the Dreadclaw Tribe is full of demihumans with lightning affinity."
Kent said as he stood atop a tall mountain overlooking the large expanse of forest and jagged mountain ranges.

The entire environment was filled with lightning, and the pressure from the storm could be felt from miles away. He was exactly 10 miles out, but he was already scanning the forest, looking for a path to take.
Two hours later, something caught Kent’s attention.
Nine miles away, five individuals appeared at the border, seemingly acting as guards. Kent knew his chance had come.
"Though I could use my demi-dragon form to enter, it’s a good thing I didn’t. These people are more beastly than I would have looked."
The five who appeared were more beast than human.
Three were tigerkins. They had the head of a tiger and the body of a man, with claws sharper than one could imagine.
However, even though their bodies were humanoid, they were covered in fur, clearly showing they were more beast than man.
The only difference between them and actual beasts was their inability to fully assume a human appearance and the fact that not all of them could transform into a full beast form.
One was a rabbitkin, with ears as long as a rabbit’s. His face was human-like but had rabbit whiskers and beast-like eyes. Both his hands and legs were clawed.
The fifth was a foxkin. He looked more handsome than the rest despite his fox-like features.

"They don’t look too bad," Kent said to himself as he started moving closer. From his scan of their aura, he found the strongest among them to be the foxkin, who was at the peak of the Root Ascension stage.
He knew it would be through him that he would enter the Dreadclaw Tribe.
After advancing and closing the distance to just two miles between himself and the five guards, he stopped and began looking for the right opportunity to strike.
Meanwhile, at the border of the Dreadclaw Tribe, the five beastkins stood guard, unaware of the danger approaching.
"In five days, we won’t have to stand guard here anymore," one of them, named Thokk, said. His friends nodded at his words.
"Indeed. The moment we handle those Bloodveins, they’ll become our slaves. I wonder if I’ll get a slave of my own," Lonki, the rabbitkin, said with a lustful expression.
"Relax. My uncle is a Root Sovereign, one of the main forces of the alliance. He said the chances of each of us getting a slave are very high," Karvar, one of the tiger demihumans, said.
"He even said we’ll get to choose."
"I just want one night with the priestess. That’s all I want," Zark, another Tiger demihuman, said with a smile.

"Don’t flatter yourself, Zark. The priestess can only be enjoyed by the tribe chief and perhaps the elders, or the Prince. Peasants like us can only go after the ordinary Bloodveins," Thokk said, making the rest laugh.
"What about you, Larkas? Do you have plans to get a slave of your own?" Zark asked.
"Isn’t that obvious? I plan on getting two, considering I’m stronger than all four of you. I believe they should share the spoils based on military contribution," Larkas answered.
"You bastard! We all want one—why should you have two?" Zark didn’t like the tone Larkas used. However, they all knew that if someone in authority heard Larkas’s words, they wouldn’t criticize him.
He had indeed made a valid point.

The strong ought to receive the best rewards, after all. The only downside was that he didn’t tell them it was the plan of the superiors. But they would find out soon enough, so it wasn’t like he was lying.
"Relax, you four. We must first survive the battle before thinking of our gains.

Though our alliance is large, we don’t trust the Soulshrouds. And while I’d love to say the Bloodveins are done for, they are the strongest for a reason—so we have to be prepared," Larkas said, and his friends nodded.
"Don’t worry. My uncle, the Root Sovereign, told me that both our tribes have recently acquired something that can aid us. I believe if we do our part, we’ll walk out victorious," Karvar said.
All five nodded. They had also heard rumors about that, so they planned to do their part and, hopefully, enjoy the benefits.
Kent, who was clearly hearing them speak, let out a deep sigh, but a frown was visible on his face.
They had openly said they would be taking slaves, and as someone who frowned on slavery, this made him want to kill every last one of them.
But he held himself back and chose to stick to the plan.

"If I kill them now, their disappearance will spark unease among the tribe. I can only kill them all during the battle to come in five days." He knew they had to die, so he would let them enjoy the next few days breathing the air of life.
After another three hours, the strongest among them, Larkas, excused himself and moved a couple of miles away to relieve himself.
Kent moved silently, using his superior Chaos and spiritual energy to evade their senses. A couple of meters away, Larkas came to a stop. But before he could unzip, his head came rolling off.
Kent quickly absorbed his memories, scanning through everything within a minute.
"Looks like he had a decent life. Too bad he chose the path of evil," he said, then crouched down and activated the [Perfect Disguise] skill Vexthra had given him.
It took a few minutes, but he replicated Larkas’s features to the last detail.

chapters.title: Chapter 530: Mission Assignment
paragraphs: Kent stayed at the peak of the mountain for the entire duration of the night. When day broke, he left for the mission assignment.
He met up with his friends first.
"How was your night, Larkas?" Lonki asked.
"Blissful," Kent had to answer, watching the expressions of his friends to see if perhaps Lovina had informed them of his sudden exit the previous night.
However, seeing they were unaware of his situation, he sighed in his heart. His performance of the Larkas persona was indeed impeccable.

Larkas had anxiety issues and a constant need to seek the approval of others. So Kent was living the persona well, making the two best friends not suspect a thing despite being with Larkas for close to 70 years already.
"I’ll see you guys later," Kent said to his two friends before running off.
A few minutes later, he appeared in a large section of land where close to 600 people stood, each holding or hanging a sword in its sheath.
They were swordsmen of the Dreadclaw tribe, and General Low, a catkin with sharper features, stood at the front facing everyone.
However, what made him different from the rest was his cultivation, which was at the peak of the Sovereign stage, and the fact that his sword aura and qi were at the profound stage.
Kent scanned him, aiming only for his status page.
⟦Name: Low Chanji⟧
⟦Cultivation: Peak Root Sovereign⟧
⟦Class: Swordsman (Sage)⟧
⟦Sword Qi: Profound (LvL 8)⟧
⟦Sword Intent: Profound (LvL 9)⟧
’I see. I guess he has the qualifications to lead 600-plus swordsmen,’ Kent thought as he walked and joined the line.
Larkas himself was a Sword Saint, so Kent wasn’t worried, considering his understanding of the sword was higher than Larkas’s.
Though he is a sword Grandmaster, Jest, his past incarnation was at the sword Saint stage, so he is sorted in that department.
After a while, the last swordsman joined the line. General Low walked forward and started addressing everyone.
"Listen up. I know by now you are all aware of the rumors going around—that we have joined forces with the Soulshroud Tribe to invade the Bloodvein Tribe. The rumors are indeed true.
We are now in an alliance with the Soulshroud to bring the Bloodvein to their knees.
In four days, we march toward the domain of the Bloodvein Tribe, and per our mission orders, we will be attacking first, considering most of the Bloodveins are swordsmen.

Our mission is simply to keep them busy so our tribe chief and the elders can engage the top brass of the Bloodvein Tribe. The moment they take them off the board, the other units will join us to destroy their army.
Know that because of the alliance, we will fight side by side with the warriors from the Soulshroud Tribe.
I will only say this once. Regardless of your personal issues with them, don’t let your anger get the best of you and attack them. They are our allies, so we must join forces to kill our enemies.
Once the battle is over, nobody will stop you if you still want to settle your differences. But during the battle, don’t attack them, for the punishment is death."
"Do I make myself clear?"
"Yes, General," everyone, including Kent, said. He had to play his part, and so far, he was doing an impeccable job.

"Good to hear that. To the last thing, Prince Ebert is asking for two swordsmen to join his unit. Naturally, I would ask you to duel it out; however, due to the urgent nature of the request, I brought a mage to help out.
All your names have been submitted, and he will use his methods to select the names based on how destined you are to become a guard of a Core Formation expert.
Know that if you survive the battle, you will be rewarded by the prince."
The sudden mention of becoming the prince’s guard was rather inviting. The prince was one of the few who could take on a full beast form.
He and his family were Pantherkin, so a majestic silver panther would appear when he took his true form. He is also one of their powerhouses.

In the past, he had shown his true form, but getting to be his guard meant you wouldn’t only be privy to some secrets, but you would also be on the frontline—and the first to pick from the loot if you survived.
’Tower, you already know what to do.’ Kent saw an opportunity, and he planned to seize it. He planned to get close to the Chief of the Dreadclaw Tribe.
Becoming a guard of the prince was the easiest way to get what he wanted. So he asked his overpowered tower to help, knowing this would be a walk in the park for the tower.
A man walked forward and waved his staff. From the wave, 703 orbs—matching the number of swordsmen—appeared in the air. Suddenly, they all started exploding until only two were left.
He waved his staff again, and the two orbs flew toward General Low, who caught them and squeezed. Two names appeared in his palm.
"Kalva and Larkas, step forward."
The sudden mention of the two names caused everyone to turn and look at the two smiling individuals as they walked forward.
"Lucky bastards." That was all anyone who wanted to become a guard could say. Kent and the other chosen swordsman stepped forward.
Kalva was a Lionkin.
"Follow me. The rest, go handle your affairs—we convene here in two days," General Low said as he led Kent and Kalva away. On the way, Kalva turned and smiled at Kent.
"I’m Kalva," he introduced himself.

"I’m Larkas. Nice meeting you," Kent replied, knowing their interaction would likely end there. His mission was now nearing completion. He had already made his first move, and the second—and final—was about to happen.

After walking for a few minutes, they entered a large house that was, without a doubt, the home of the tribe chief. General Low led them along a stone path until they came to a stop in front of a building.
Out front stood two individuals, each at the peak of the Root Sovereign stage. They were Batkin, with auras that rivaled most Core Formation experts in the human world.
"I’m here to see Prince Ebert. These are the two he asked for."

The Batkins smirked at Kent and Kalva before one of them went to call the prince. A few minutes later, he returned with the prince, who walked out with his arms wrapped around the waists of two Rabbitkin.
"A fox, huh? General Low, you sure know how to make my day."Prince Ebert said, smiling in Kent’s direction.
Kent immediately disliked the prince, so he branded his soul and planted a soul bomb in it.

Out front stood two individuals, each at the peak of the Root Sovereign stage.
They were Batkin, with auras that rivaled most Core Formation experts in the human world.
"I’m here to see Prince Ebert.
These are the two he asked for."
The Batkins smirked at Kent and Kalva before one of them went to call the prince.
A few minutes later, he returned with the prince, who walked out with his arms wrapped around the waists of two Rabbitkin.
"A fox, huh?
General Low, you sure know how to make my day."Prince Ebert said, smiling in Kent’s direction.
Kent immediately disliked the prince, so he branded his soul and planted a soul bomb in it.

chapters.title: Chapter 531: Soul Exploding Pendant
paragraphs: "I promised to get you two guards, so here they are," General Low said, pointing at Kent and Kalvas.
The prince was a much taller, thicker pantherkin who, by beast standards, was handsome. But by the look of his nature, one could already see his arrogance from a mile away.
"You two, on your knees," Prince Ebert said, and Kalvas immediately went down on his knees. Kent, on the other hand, stood there, staring at the prince with a calm expression.
"Didn’t you hear the order to kneel down?" one of the Batkin standing behind the prince said, pointing at Kent. However, despite directing his aura at him, Kent stood there, unmoving.
He locked gazes with the prince and then asked,

"I didn’t come here to kneel before you or anyone. I came because I was required to be your guard. Now, I don’t know if you’ll take offense, but I don’t see myself going down on my knees anytime soon."
It wasn’t that Kent was arrogant. No, he had Larkas’s memory, and he knew from that memory that Foxkin didn’t bow to anyone. It was their nature.
Forcing a Foxkin to their knees was akin to dragging their dignity through the mud. So they didn’t kneel—not even before the tribe chief.
Who knew what would have become of him if he had knelt when Prince Ebert commanded? He would probably have become a laughingstock to many.
"I guess you peasants didn’t exaggerate when you said it’s against your nature to bow. I wonder if you can keep that belief for long when I become the tribe chief," Prince Ebert said with a smirk.
’I am killing him first,’ Kent thought, knowing too well he would kill him first—and the two bats behind him.
Prince Ebert was a Level 8 Core Formation expert, unlike the priestess of the Bloodvein Tribe, who was at the peak and had already undergone three evolutions.
This meant that he couldn’t hold a candle to Velyra when it came to battle prowess.

"I don’t have much use for you two. The only thing required of you is to wear this pendant, and when the battle starts, find a way to sneak into the inner section of the Bloodvein forces and get closer to their priestess."
"Once you’re there, shatter the pendant and run away. If you come out alive, know that you will be able to pick three ripe ladies from the Bloodvein Tribe after we win the battle."
Prince Ebert threw two pendants to Kent and Kalvas, who caught them. Kent did a quick scan, and what he discovered only strengthened his determination to kill Prince Ebert.
’This bastard wants to use my soul to amplify this pendant just to weaken Velyra. It’s a suicide mission.’ Kent’s killing intent surfaced, but in soul form, so nobody noticed.
His soul was several times stronger than those around him.
"I will not fail you, my prince." Naturally, Kalvas had no idea what was happening, so he enthusiastically said this to the prince, who smiled—but with a mocking touch that only Kent noticed.
"I will also do my best not to fail you," Kent said, putting the pendant on his wrist. Watching this, the prince smiled in his heart.
⟪Name: Soul Exploding Pendant⟫
⟪Grade: Legendary⟫

→ Sacrifice your soul to unleash a powerful area-of-effect soul attack that can render those below Tier 10 comatose and those above to feel a pain so great they will lose control over their senses for ten seconds.
Kent didn’t say much, but he used his soul to destroy the pendant Kalvas was wearing and quickly ensured the number of people he branded included Kalvas.
"You can leave now. I expect you to find a way inside the domain of the Bloodveins before the battle begins, so start preparing."

"Thank you for this opportunity, my prince. I won’t fail you," Kalvas sucked up one last time, unaware he would die from this mission if Kent hadn’t destroyed the pendant. Not that he would live anyways.
Whether he made it inside the Bloodvein domain or not, he was marked for death, and Kent would ensure that.
"I know you wouldn’t fail me, because if you do, I will come knocking," the prince said before heading back inside with the two ladies still in his arms.
’He is dead for sure,’ Kent said to himself before walking away.
He didn’t go back home straight away. Instead, he went up a particular hill, sat down, and began meditating.
He didn’t want to go back to that horny Lovina, whom he had chosen to stay away from behind while he continued his mission. Naturally, the location he picked was just five miles away from the palace.

So when night came, he used the Rule Breaker to cancel his energy, making him invisible to all. This allowed him to sneak back into the mansion, but this time, he made his way toward the main palace where the tribe chief resided.
He came this evening because he knew a meeting was going on, and he couldn’t miss it. So, after closing in on the building, he climbed up to the stone roof and sat down.
His senses were locked on the prince, who was now conversing with the tribe chief and the three elders that every tribe had.
Like the elders of the Bloodvein Tribe, these three were at the peak and had already completed four evolutions.
’Tsk, they’re all at the 10th Tier in soul cultivation. Though my soul essence is limited, I can kill at least two of them and let Velyra and her people handle the rest.’
Kent quickly branded their souls without a single one of them noticing. He needed them linked to his soul in order to handle them when the time came.
After branding them, it was easy to hear everything they were saying.
"Ebert, didn’t you find the pawns to carry the pendants?" the tribe chief asked. He went by the name Rokar Dreadclaw, one of the powerful figures in the Dead Region.
He was a hulking figure over eight feet tall, with dark gray skin covered in rough, armored scales. His claws were enormous, and his eyes glowed a fierce red.
His black hair was wild, falling around his broad shoulders like a mane, and his teeth were sharp, capable of tearing through the toughest of hides.
"I did, Father," Ebert answered with a polite smile.
"Good. Now, I want you to have this." Tribe Chief Rokar retrieved a right-arm gauntlet radiating intense soul energy from his storage and handed it to Ebert.

chapters.title: Chapter 532: Their Secrets [Bonus]
paragraphs: "This is a Mystical-grade treasure, and judging by the aura, it has been refined using thousands of souls. It’s very dangerous if care is not taken."
Kent, who hadn’t refined a weapon before for some reason, could pick up on the nature of the gauntlet being handed to Prince Ebert.
Though he knew nothing of refining the soul, his deduction was spot on. The gauntlet was indeed refined using thousands of souls.
"Father, what is this?" Ebert asked his father.
"This is one of the two weapons the alliance has produced. Thanks to the Soulshroud tribe, we now have two powerful weapons forged using 4,000 souls.
It has the power to destroy the souls of those it strikes. I tested it inside the Chaos Region, and trust me, it’s as they said.
I have the left hand; you can have the right hand. Make sure you put it to good use."
"Okay, Father." Ebert stored away the gauntlet like it would be stolen by the elders any second. The elders sighed, knowing the good stuff wouldn’t be given to them.
"Father, with this, do we have a shot at defeating the Bloodvein tribe?" Ebert asked, and his father burst out laughing.

"Of course. They’ve already lost half the battle. We just have to show up in four days’ time and crush them completely," Tribe Chief Rokar spoke in a tone that suggested he was confident in their chances to win.
This made Ebert curious, and without even knowing he was being manipulated, he asked a question that made his father smile and tap him on the shoulder.
"I don’t understand, Father. How did we win half the battle when we haven’t fought yet?"
"Do you really think we’ve only just started plotting against the Bloodvein tribe? This plan has been in the works for years.

We knew from the start that the Bloodveins are powerful, so we started early, and thankfully, the plan bore fruit. So even if they somehow made us retreat, their race will come to an end in under a decade."
Ebert wanted to ask more, but his father stopped him.

"I know you want to know more, but know this—win or not, the Bloodvein tribe is done for. They won’t be able to live in their domain much longer anyway. So they will one day come begging, even if we choose not to attack them.

However, our chances of winning are very high. I learned recently that the Soulshroud tribe obtained a treasure that can easily bring them to their knees. So chin up—the priestess will be yours and other things you can’t even begin to imagine."
Ebert smiled and nodded toward his father.
"In that case, I will go prepare for when we march toward their domain."
His father nodded, and just like that, the plot thickened for Kent, who heard everything. But he didn’t leave—he stayed to see if he could overhear something.
However, after spending the entire night there, nothing new was said, so he left and went back to his meditation spot.
"Looks like this will not be as simple as I expected. They seem confident, and judging by how he spoke, the Bloodvein are already doomed.
This makes me wonder what they have done," Kent started to ponder.
He knew that for them to be this confident, whatever they did must have some serious implications that the Bloodvein tribe can’t handle, no matter how strong they are.
This made him wonder what that thing could be. He didn’t want to make any mistakes on this quest, so he most definitely wanted to know.
"Tower, what do you think?" Kent asked the tower, but this time, the tower wasn’t helpful. Though it did give him something:
⟪The mission parameters suggest the master should do this on his own. In that case, I cannot help you, but I can point you in the right direction: go back to the Bloodvein tribe and investigate.⟫
"I see. I guess I’d better wrap things up here first. However, I have another question." Kent sighed. "Based on my soul essence, how many Core Formation experts can I kill before losing 70% of it?
⟪You currently have 12,768,650 soul essence, meaning you can kill 5 Core Formation.⟫
"Perfect," Kent laughed, knowing his chances of evening the odds had just increased. However, what the tower said next shocked him.

⟪Your Progress Meter: 7,000,800 / 45,090,008. It shows the soul essence required to reach the 12th Tier. However, if you were to kill and absorb all five souls of the Core Formation experts, the progress would move to 15 million.

Now, I don’t know what you plan on doing, but if you go further and kill more from the Soulshroud tribe, you will be drawing closer to the endgame, which, in a way, will push you toward the 12th Tier.
But that is just by the way. The main gain here is that, after killing the Core Formation experts, you can choose to replenish your essence rather than use it to level up.
In this case, your soul essence will be restored, which you can use a second time.⟫ree
"Damn. I am that awesome, and I didn’t even know." Kent smiled, knowing he had indeed reached a level he didn’t even think was possible.
"Tell me, Tower, why are you telling me this, knowing full well it’s against the rules?" Kent may be naive sometimes, but he was not stupid. He could sense a conspiracy from a mile away.
He sensed the Tower wasn’t telling him all this for nothing.

⟪The endgame here, Master, is to get the Blood Heart Stone. And in order to do that, you have to show the Bloodvein tribe what you are capable of. I say this is the best move to get what you want the right way.⟫
"The Blood Heart Stone, huh. Very well, Tower, I will do just that." Kent stood up and went to see his two friends, not to chat, but to brand all the warriors marching from the Dreadclaw tribe.
He didn’t know why the Tower and the universe wanted him to get the Blood Heart Stone. However, since they wanted him to save the Bloodvein tribe, he would do that.
He made sure the majority of the warriors were branded, then went back to see the Prince one last time...

chapters.title: Chapter 533: Good News and Bad News [Bonus]
paragraphs: "My Prince, I came to inform you I will be leaving now to get started with my mission. I know this is early, but I want to get it done properly, so I can only move out now."
Kent said to Prince Ebert, who was seated with a beauty on his lap. He most certainly didn’t want to say it, but the guy was making him even angrier with this display.
"Very well. I will allow you to go. But you must take this. I will contact you when I arrive." He threw a communication token to Kent, who caught it
"You can also contact me through it if something pops up," Kent nodded and left speedily.
He knew if he stayed there a few more minutes, he would lunge at the guy and kill him.
After leaving, he went to see his two friends.

"Lonki, Karvar, I will be leaving early for the mission given to me by the prince. I don’t know if I will ever see you guys again, considering it’s a dangerous one, so I want to ask one last time: do you two really want to join this invasion? Like, do you have your heart in it and believe in it?"
Kent asked, and the two stared at him with strange expressions.
"Why ask this question, Larkas? Those Bloodfiends have stayed in charge for too long. Us taking over is only natural," Lonki answered with a smirk.
"I can already see my bed shaking with Redskin beauties lined on it," Karvar also said, with a lustful expression.
Kent examined them with his soul, and he could tell they meant everything they said, which caused him to sigh.
"In that case, I wish you two the best of fortune. May the Beast God smile on you two," Kent said, tapping them on the shoulder.
Perhaps because Larkas’s body helped him complete his mission, he didn’t want to kill his friends. However, from their response, they held no remorse for the Bloodvein race.
This could only mean they wouldn’t hesitate to work towards their dream.
In that case, Kent wouldn’t hold back and kill them when the time comes.
"Take care, Larkas. You are going into enemy territory," Lonki said, and Karvar nodded.
"I know, and I will be careful. See you two around." With that, Kent left and went straight to the border before finally leaving the domain of the Dreadclaws.
Kent didn’t want to draw attention, so he ran 20 miles before stopping. Even so, he waited ten minutes, ensuring he wasn’t followed.
When he was satisfied, he turned back to his real form and spread his wings, speeding toward the domain of the Bloodveins.
Meanwhile, back in the Dreadclaw Tribe, Lonki and Karvar continued talking until Lonki suddenly said something that raised Karvar’s brow.
"Is it just me, or is something different about Larkas?"
"What do you mean?" Karvar questioned.
"I mean, he never told us the mission he was going on. In the past, he would have. Also, the way he talked to us before he left—it felt more like he wasn’t him, yet he was him.
Not that it is important. What I am puzzled about is the fact that he tried to persuade us."
Karvar brushed his beard, holding a thoughtful expression. "You don’t think he knew something that could put our lives in danger, and so he asked that?"
"Nonsense. Larkas wouldn’t hold anything back if it concerned our lives." Lonki didn’t even want to entertain that idea.
"What if he is under a spell that prevents him from saying anything?"
"That makes sense, then. I can already see a pattern here, Karvar. Perhaps he indeed tried warning us." Lonki didn’t want to admit it, but Karvar’s reasoning made some sense.
"If that is the case, then perhaps we should rethink this whole war thing," Lonki suggested, and Karvar nodded.
"We can’t walk away, but we can stay alive. Knowing the Soulshroud Tribe will be our allies, I say we use the numbers to our advantage. Regardless of what happens, I want us to come out alive."
Karvar nodded again.
"That sneaky bastard. Despite being under a spell, he managed to warn us. We should give him a good beating when we see him again," the two friends nodded.

However, Kent’s desires and their reasoning didn’t align. In any case, they would make their move, and Kent would also make his. In the end, it would be between who wants to live and who has the will to live.

It took Kent five hours to reach the borders of the Bloodvein Tribe. When the five guards saw him this time, they didn’t attack. Instead, two escorted him back to the tribe, showing how much things had changed.
Kent didn’t immediately go to see the tribe chief or the elders. He first walked around the tribe with his two guards, who were assigned to never leave his side and attend to all his wants.
Kent spent seven whole hours examining the tribe but found nothing. However, since the tower had pointed him in the right direction, he didn’t stop and continued for another three hours.
Thankfully, when he was contemplating giving up, his senses picked up something. This made him move in that direction.
It was hidden deep in a cave that nobody would dare go near. But when he got there, he got the shock of his life.
"This is too sinister," Kent muttered, watching the most sinister thing he had seen so far in his time in the world of Sonox.
After examining it, he left to see the tribe chief and the elders. Naturally, Valyra was there too.
"My mission was a success. In three days, they will come, but don’t worry, they won’t get anywhere.
However, I have some good and some bad news. Which one do you want to hear first?"
Tribe Chief Malthar looked at the four inside with him and then sighed.
"The bad first," he said.
"The bad news is, every last Bloodvein will die in ten years."
"WHAT?"
