Us taking over is only natural," Lonki answered with a smirk.
"I can already see my bed shaking with Redskin beauties lined on it," Karvar also said, with a lustful expression.
Kent examined them with his soul, and he could tell they meant everything they said, which caused him to sigh.
"In that case, I wish you two the best of fortune.
May the Beast God smile on you two," Kent said, tapping them on the shoulder.
Perhaps because Larkas’s body helped him complete his mission, he didn’t want to kill his friends.
However, from their response, they held no remorse for the Bloodvein race.
This could only mean they wouldn’t hesitate to work towards their dream.
In that case, Kent wouldn’t hold back and kill them when the time comes.
"Take care, Larkas.
You are going into enemy territory," Lonki said, and Karvar nodded.
"I know, and I will be careful.
See you two around." With that, Kent left and went straight to the border before finally leaving the domain of the Dreadclaws.
Kent didn’t want to draw attention, so he ran 20 miles before stopping.
Even so, he waited ten minutes, ensuring he wasn’t followed.
When he was satisfied, he turned back to his real form and spread his wings, speeding toward the domain of the Bloodveins.
Meanwhile, back in the Dreadclaw Tribe, Lonki and Karvar continued talking until Lonki suddenly said something that raised Karvar’s brow.
"Is it just me, or is something different about Larkas?"
"What do you mean?" Karvar questioned.
"I mean, he never told us the mission he was going on.
In the past, he would have.
Also, the way he talked to us before he left—it felt more like he wasn’t him, yet he was him.
Not that it is important.
What I am puzzled about is the fact that he tried to persuade us."
Karvar brushed his beard, holding a thoughtful expression.
"You don’t think he knew something that could put our lives in danger, and so he asked that?"
"Nonsense.
Larkas wouldn’t hold anything back if it concerned our lives." Lonki didn’t even want to entertain that idea.
"What if he is under a spell that prevents him from saying anything?"
"That makes sense, then.
I can already see a pattern here, Karvar.
Perhaps he indeed tried warning us." Lonki didn’t want to admit it, but Karvar’s reasoning made some sense.
"If that is the case, then perhaps we should rethink this whole war thing," Lonki suggested, and Karvar nodded.
"We can’t walk away, but we can stay alive.
Knowing the Soulshroud Tribe will be our allies, I say we use the numbers to our advantage.
Regardless of what happens, I want us to come out alive."
Karvar nodded again.
"That sneaky bastard.
Despite being under a spell, he managed to warn us.
We should give him a good beating when we see him again," the two friends nodded.
However, Kent’s desires and their reasoning didn’t align.
In any case, they would make their move, and Kent would also make his.
In the end, it would be between who wants to live and who has the will to live.
It took Kent five hours to reach the borders of the Bloodvein Tribe.
When the five guards saw him this time, they didn’t attack.
Instead, two escorted him back to the tribe, showing how much things had changed.
Kent didn’t immediately go to see the tribe chief or the elders.
He first walked around the tribe with his two guards, who were assigned to never leave his side and attend to all his wants.
Kent spent seven whole hours examining the tribe but found nothing.
However, since the tower had pointed him in the right direction, he didn’t stop and continued for another three hours.
Thankfully, when he was contemplating giving up, his senses picked up something.
This made him move in that direction.
It was hidden deep in a cave that nobody would dare go near.
But when he got there, he got the shock of his life.
"This is too sinister," Kent muttered, watching the most sinister thing he had seen so far in his time in the world of Sonox.
After examining it, he left to see the tribe chief and the elders.
Naturally, Valyra was there too.
"My mission was a success.
In three days, they will come, but don’t worry, they won’t get anywhere.
However, I have some good and some bad news.
Which one do you want to hear first?"
Tribe Chief Malthar looked at the four inside with him and then sighed.
"The bad first," he said.
"The bad news is, every last Bloodvein will die in ten years."
"WHAT?"

chapters.title: Chapter 534: True Evil
paragraphs: Hearing Kent’s grim words clearly didn’t sit well with the leaders of the Bloodvein tribe. They clearly didn’t expect to be told they had ten years left to live.
"Clearly, you must be joking, Kent. Though the battle is coming, we don’t know the outcome, yet somehow you say we will be dying?" Velyra asked, not accepting Kent’s words.
"I didn’t know what else to say, but from my investigation, I found out your tribe will be wiped out in ten years—if you remain in this domain, that is."
"But how? And why can’t we live here after ten years?" Tribe Chief Malthar asked.
"That is because your land is poisoned, and, well, your bloodline has also been poisoned. I only found this out when I overheard the Tribe Chief and his elders talking about it.
It seems they’ve been planning this for a while now." Kent didn’t want to tell them his system told him.
An intense killing qi exuded from the Tribe Chief’s body upon hearing that their land and bloodline were poisoned—and that it had been so for a while now.
Also, the people they treated as friends were the perpetrators. These two things are just too much for them to come to terms with
"But why? Why would people we interact with every day do something like this? We share a good relationship with them, both in this region and outside during explorations.
So just why would they do something like that?" Velyra just couldn’t believe what she had heard. She most definitely could not believe her ears.

"Why else would someone do this if not to take your treasures and make you submit? I don’t know what you know about the outside world where I come from, but these things happen every day. Allies often conspire against each other for their own gain.
This is no different. The only question now is what you will do in response."
What Kent found inside the cave was a Tier 13 spell—something that shouldn’t be possible in this world, considering the limitations placed on it.
However, there indeed existed a Tier 13 spell that had seemingly been active for years.
After examining it, he discovered that it affected the Bloodvein bloodline and even the land. According to the tower’s deduction, they had less than a decade to live in their domain.

This, of course, made Kent wonder who had the means to cast such a powerful spell. He thought long and hard, but he just couldn’t come up with a logical explanation—aside from the fact that it coincided with what happened to the Life Magicians years ago.
"I have a question, though. It’s a long stretch, but do any of you know or have met someone outside this world who isn’t human, dragon, elf, dwarf, beastkin, or demon?"
"No, we’re unaware of anyone like that, considering we killed anyone who wasn’t part of the three major and four minor tribes."
"I see. In any case, the spell is a Tier 13 spell that can’t easily be destroyed. And even if we had the means to destroy it, we wouldn’t want to alert the caster."
"Are you implying the caster is outside this region?" Elder Ureth asked.
"I suspect so. There’s a similar situation in my world, and looking at your situation now, I believe the perpetrator is the same and not from this region."
"Then what should we do?" Velyra asked.

Kent smiled. "That will be the good news. I have two options, which I believe are the best for you. First, I will help you win the battle and even help you claim the lands belonging to the two major tribes.

This means you will kill the majority of them, which I don’t mind doing. However, the chances of you alerting the caster are very high, and I don’t know if your tribe will thrive naturally there when you move.
However, it’s my only option that comes for free, so what do you think?"
They didn’t immediately answer. This option really did sound reasonable; however, the chances of them liking it were low.
"You are right. Our tribe is of blood. We have an affinity for blood, and as such, this domain, which contains both Chaos and Blood Qi, is perfect for us.
Moving to a new domain is not something we can do. Of course, killing every last one of them is something we will do if we have the chance.
Since they can’t spare us, there is no need to spare them. We fight, even with evil."
"I say they are True Evil. But knowing the first option is a no-go, I’ll say the next option is also good, though it comes at a price." Kent’s smile made the Chief, elders, and Velyra gulp.
Those eyes were of a predator who wanted nothing more than to sink his fangs into the veins of his prey.
"Say I have the means to create a new domain where your kind could live in peace, free from danger. Basically, you would live the best life possible.
And the best part? The Mother of Killers is also there, training. So, what do you think?" Kent asked with a smile that said many things.
Name-dropping Neomi was just his way of spicing things up. This way, no matter how expensive the price was, they wouldn’t see it as a loss if they could be near their god.
"Are you being serious?" Velyra asked, the Chief and elders sharing the same questioning expression.
"Why would I lie about something like this?" Kent said with a thoughtful expression. "I just want to help. However, this help comes with a price."
"And the price is?" Chief Malthar asked, looking nervous.
"No need to look nervous. I just want the Blood Heart Stone in exchange for offering you a better accommodation. How does that sound?"
The five people in the room locked their murderous eyes on Kent when he mentioned the name of something that was supposed to be a secret.
They didn’t know how he knew that, but they most certainly didn’t want to take him for granted.
"Just who are you?" Velyra asked.
"Kent Madson..." Kent answered with a smile as he stood up. He knew they needed to think long and hard about his offer.

chapters.title: Chapter 535: Our Sister is a Shameless Goddess
paragraphs: Vexthra coming to the tower wasn’t just to see her sister and spend every day having sex with her husband. She had no plans to waste time.
Her major plan was to turn her sisters into powerhouses.
She is a god, so until Kent enters the god realm or finds himself in a unique world, she won’t be able to help him with anything combat-wise.
She is basically useless in that aspect, so as someone who had given him the quest to kill the God of Alchemy, she knew Kent would need all the help he could get.
This made her invest her strength in her sisters.
Unbeknownst to her, the simple human she gave this mega quest to was actually someone the universe fancied in all ways and forms.
Kent, who was meant to rise through the ranks and one day challenge the God of Alchemy, was actually badass from the start.
And this greatness now started to affect her sisters when Kent started bestowing True Names on them. She basically had her job cut in half for her.
So her coming was to prepare her sisters to reach the stage where, whenever their man was in danger, they would be able to help him.
That was why she never let any of them slack off when she started their training.

She first used the goddess’s powers and resources to move their spirit Roots from the Ruby stage to the Divine stage, which is only two grades away from reaching the Celestial grade—the peak of this universe.

This alone lifted their prowess from ordinary to a level they never thought possible. Even Elaine, who was basically clueless about combat, has now gained the power to protect herself from someone like her late master.
Vexthra didn’t hold back, and since her main plan was to ensure her man never lacked, she made sure the ladies she wanted in his life never lacked either.
After their upgrade, they tempered their bodies using some of the most valuable herbs in the universe. She really came prepared.
After tempering their bodies for nearly three months, she started them on a new regimen requiring them to climb to the 300th step in the Golden Titan Stairway.

Since she could use her goddess powers, she ensured they used the pressure to temper their bodies further. It was a difficult task for them, but she made sure none got stuck, especially those without True Names yet.
The first to reach the 300th step was Lady Vari, who, for the past few months, had fully committed to the training Vexthra designed for her.
Her cultivation was reset to the Peak of the Sovereign stage, but she wasn’t angry. In fact, at her current cultivation stage, she felt more powerful than before.
In the Assassin profession, there are different ranks, just like there are ranks in swordsmanship or spearmanship. Assassins also have ranks.
They start from Rank 1, which is akin to a Master Swordsman. Then there’s Rank 2, which is a Sword Grandmaster.
In the assassin path, they call it the Shadow Grandmaster.
Lady Vari is a Shadow Sage, which makes her Rank 4. Vexthra wants her to become Rank 5—a Shadow King. This would make her one of the best and deadliest in the world when it comes to assassination.
To help her gain great control over the shadows, Vexthra lowered her cultivation base. Now, she would have to study the shadows and rise from there.

Thankfully, Kent ensured her disciple’s safety, so she wasn’t worried about her. This allowed her to throw herself into the training so intensely that, when Vexthra started polluting her mind, she couldn’t resist.
And it wasn’t just her. Elaine was the same, and now she just wants Kent to come back and spread their legs.
She knew the two wouldn’t miraculously become her sisters, so she did her best to ensure they walked the path themselves.
This way, when Kent comes back, they would get curious themselves and perhaps want to get in his pants after hearing all there is to hear about him.
The ladies really put a lot into their training.
The first to reach the 300th step was Lady Vari, who was awarded the Body Transcendence Pill.

Thanks to that, and the fact that she was already at the Silver Body stage after the herbal bath, she stepped into the Gold Body stage, making not only her body refined but also her beauty shoot up by leaps and bounds.

She became so hot that if Kent were to see her in just her pants and tank top—considering Vexthra basically made them wear clothes that don’t really do much to cover their bodies—his dragon rod would probably raise its head.
The lady is beautiful by all standards, but her body form and shape have changed after becoming a gold body cultivator.
Nara was the second to reach the 300th step. She also received the Body Transcendence Pill, which enabled her to break through to the Gold Body stage.

Like Lady Vari, she had also become a damsel to die for. And while her cultivation base is only at the Peak of the Transcendent stage, she has a True Name, so she was basically a beauty even before becoming a Gold Body cultivator.
But after she reached the 300th level, her form developed to the point that even her sisters gulped when looking at her.
Neomi was third, also gaining the same reward. Mara and Lady Lani were the fourth to reach the 300th step, then Camilla followed. Selene and Ingrid reached at the same time.
Elsa and Val also reached the 300th step at the same time, followed by Lilian and Unity. Alina and Elaine came last. However, this all happened within 30 days—something even Vexthra never expected.
Still, she was impressed watching every last one of them reach this level in their cultivation.
"How are you ladies feeling?" Vexthra asked, hovering above them. She is a goddess, so the pressure wasn’t having any effect on her.
"I feel like I can punch a hole into a mountain," Unity answered, flexing her muscles—muscles that would make any man gulp if they saw her shape.
"Good. You’ll all need this energy for when our man returns."
"Big sister..." The ladies—every last one of them—blushed upon hearing her say that. Not that it was the first time she said something like it.
’Our big sister is a shameless goddess.’ That was what Unity had said to her the first time she made such a comment. Naturally, they all laughed, and she even puffed her chest, not denying the claim.

chapters.title: Chapter 536: Their First Time with Kent
paragraphs: "Big sister, when can we continue climbing?" Lilian asked, watching the thousands of steps left to climb.

"The current you doesn’t have the means to continue. However, I will ensure you start climbing soon enough. For now, my next move is to enrich your yin qi to the point that, even with your lower cultivation base, you can show some effect when you have sex with Kent."
Vexthra didn’t hold anything back, so even Lady Vari and Elaine knew about Kent’s dual cultivation and the other benefits they would give him and receive in return.
They never really cared much, considering what they had received was enough to make them open their legs for him.
They were innocent in that department. However, if they stayed around Vexthra for a while, they wouldn’t be for long.
"Big sister, how do we do that?" Mara asked, and her sister nodded. They all want to enrich their yin qi.
"I have many ways, but mostly, we already have a method inside the Harem Tower. I have prepared a technique for each and every one of you that will allow you to cultivate it.
We still have some time before Kent returns, so we will use that time for the next phase of your cultivation. When that is done, you can all return to climbing."
"Thank you, big sister. With what we’ve gained now, I wonder if Kent can handle all of us." Selene, of course, had her mind wander into the shameless, lustful department.
"Trust me, Kent is a beast. Even when he wasn’t this strong, he was able to make me moan for hours—and I am a goddess." The ladies laughed.
Well, Lady Vari and Elaine blushed.

"Big sister, tell us about your first time with him," Unity asked, getting more involved in Vexthra’s life than her sisters. She basically wanted to know more about being a goddess, considering she was a dormant goddess herself.
"My first time with Kent was wild. I was clueless about love and affection back then, considering my divinity is basically hatred and resentment.
Kent was just a mortal who didn’t have any qualities I desired, aside from his rather unusual connection to my divinity that even impressed me for the first time in millions of years.
But that was just it. He basically didn’t have anything I wanted. However, this lowly mortal that any goddess would squash like a bug made a move on me, and I couldn’t resist."
"Clearly, you are exaggerating," Lady Vari said, but Vexthra smiled and shook her head.
"I wasn’t exaggerating. Kent made his move on me, and while my brain wanted me to grab his neck and squeeze the life out of him, my tainted heart refused to listen.
In fact, when he touched me, I felt like a little girl given candy. He basically rendered me useless to my own thinking and started arousing a desire I never knew was there all these years.
When he kissed me and touched my breasts and butt, I basically melted in his hands. Then he claimed my virginity, which became one of the most blissful moments of my life.
Could you believe, even as a mortal, he went on for hours with me—basically tossing me around on my own bed?" Most of her sisters didn’t need to imagine. They had already been through that.
"Looks like he was a beast from the start," Elsa commented.
"Trust me, he is a beast in bed, and I love that about him. He never leaves us unsatisfied." Vexthra smiled and then turned to Unity.
"You were the second lady he had sex with. How was your experience?" Unity smiled.

paragraphs: "Zaila will be coming out today," Camilla said, sitting in the love garden with her sisters as they spent the afternoon together.
"Indeed. Too bad Kent won’t be here to welcome her. However, we are here, so we should make her feel welcomed," Vexthra answered, and the ladies nodded.
"Then how should we do that?" Mara asked.
"Very simple—we throw her a party here inside the harem tower. This way, she won’t freak out when she finds out this is a no-clothing space," Vexthra answered, and her sisters could only smile.
"Not that she is new to this. Kent already told me she and he have made progress in their relationship and even promised to rock her world when she comes out.

At this rate, she’ll be getting the good stuff before Lani and Nara." Vexthra didn’t want to tease the two friends, but to make the environment more lively, she did—and as expected, she made them blush.
"Then we should start early. I don’t want her party to be any less entertaining."
"Gaia, dear, why don’t you come here?" Vexthra called out, and the Cosmic loli appeared wearing a suit like a butler. The ladies always cracked up when they saw her in such clothing.

"You called me, my lady." Naturally, Gaia was the biggest and perhaps the most shameless of them all. She asked the question with a straight face and demeanour befitting a butler, making the ladies crack up.
"We want to eat into our man’s account," Vexthra said, and Gaia smiled.
"What belongs to Master belongs to you all. You can buy anything you want, and I’ll put it on his tab," Gaia said, knowing moments like this only come once. She would get her share anyway.

"Nice one, Gaia. I keep liking you every single minute." Vexthra smiled and then told her the plan. "We want a big cake made with both strawberry and vanilla. It should have the writing: ’Welcome Home Zaila, We Love You.’
Aside from that, we need champagne and some of the top-shelf stuff, if you know what I’m talking about." Gaia nodded.
"I got you, my lady."

"Thank you, Gaia." The cosmic loli left to prepare what was required of her. Meanwhile, the ladies freshened up, and in simple clothes, they went back to the body tower, where the Nightmare Chamber was located.
On the door was a countdown, showing that she would be coming out in 10 minutes.
Mara held Camilla’s hand as they waited for her disciple, whom she thought she had lost 20-plus years ago. Now, she is just waiting for her to return healthy, like she should be.
Zaila had never recovered from her trauma of being kidnapped and used as a blood bank for over twenty years by the late Sect Master of the Divine Palace sect.
If Kent hadn’t intervened when he did, she would have formed a heart demon long ago, which would have been hard on her.

As the minutes counted down, the ladies grew nervous. They knew the Nightmare Chamber was the cure, so if that didn’t work, then there was no other way but for Dori to wipe her memory—something that would deprive her of her time with Nara.
"She is coming out." The moment the timer reached zero, the door to the Nightmare Chamber opened, and Zaila stepped out.
However, the moment she did, a painful scream escaped her mouth as she dropped to the ground and held her head.
"Zaila!" Camilla was the first to reach her, holding her in her arms as tears flowed from her eyes. Her sisters, except Vexthra, surrounded her.
The goddess stood back, looking at something that made her brow raise. It was like she knew something was up, and truthfully, she was right...
"Everyone, step back." Vexthra waved her hand, and her sisters were pulled away from Zaila, flung three miles back, leaving Zaila alone on the ground.
"Big sister, what is go—" Selene wasn’t even done speaking when a powerful energy burst out of Zaila’s body, causing her scream to grow louder.
Vexthra vanished and reappeared beside her, placing a hand on her shoulder—not to ease her pain, but to ensure she didn’t pass out.
Dori appeared in the air above them.
"Goddess, don’t let her go. She is on the last step, so make sure she remains conscious," Dori said before she began drawing symbols in the air.
Far from them, Gaia and Akira also appeared, watching this with smiles on their faces.
"I guess the plan worked," Gaia said.

"Indeed. That sneaky Dori really knows how to stir up trouble. But this is good for her. Becoming a mind cultivator would make her someone her sisters can rely on when the time comes," Akira answered.

Dori wrote thousands of symbols and made them move into Zaila’s body. The moment they did, the air came to a complete stop. Then, despite being miles away, the ladies felt their senses pulled into a different realm.
The scene inside the tower changed, bringing a new scene of a river, very large, housing thousands of beautiful, colorful fish.
There were sea unicorns, seahorses, octopuses, whales, sharks—thousands of them. They came in different shapes and colors, making the river elegant and nurturing.
"Where are we?" Lilian asked, looking around.
"Welcome to my realm, sisters. I have been waiting for you." Suddenly, a voice they all recognized spoke, causing them to turn to their left.
When they did, they saw Zaila walking toward them. She was wearing only white pants and a bra, and her thin white nightwear flowed behind her like a cape.
She looked beautiful, more than she did on the outside. Her hair was hazy red, flowing down her back. Her body was also well-developed, growing in all the right places.
"Is it just me, or has Zaila become even more beautiful?" Camilla asked, looking at her disciple, who now appeared confident, radiant, and genuinely happy.
She looked nothing like her broken self before entering the Nightmare Chamber.
"That is because that is not Zaila—at least not the real her," Vexthra replied, and the ladies turned to her.
"If that is not her, then who is she?" Alina asked. To answer this, Vexthra looked at Zaila, and the two smiled.
"She is not the real Zaila, because this is a Primordial Spirit—a true Primordial Spirit."

chapters.title: Chapter 538: Zaila’s Primordial Spirit
paragraphs: "A primordial spirit?"
The ladies became confused by the beauty standing before them. They turned to Vexthra, but her smile made them turn to Zaila.
"Who are you really?" Selene asked.
"I am Zaila’s mind and soul. In other words, I am her soul body. However, since I can talk and make decisions on my own, I transcended the name ’soul body’ and became a Primordial Spirit.

In this form, I am basically Zaila, considering that if her physical body dies, provided I am not affected, she can reform her body again. Basically, I am the dream of every immortal, god, supreme, or celestial."
"Shameless much." Even Selene could see her shamelessness from a mile away. However, what she said did sound cool.
"So is your name also Zaila?" Alina asked.
"Yes. But we can workshop that later. Of course, you can see me as your fellow sister, considering we will be having the same man soon."

"That’s enough, Zaila." Suddenly, the real Zaila appeared inside the realm her sisters had been pulled into. It was actually her soul space, created from her mind, so technically, it could be called Mind Space.
Zaila stood beside her Primordial Spirit, and immediately, the disparity in looks could be seen. The Primordial Spirit was basically a goddess compared to Zaila.
"Zaila, what is happening?" Camilla asked, looking between her disciple and her Primordial Spirit.
"Master, her name is Zaila—the one who helped me get through my depression and trauma," Zaila answered with a cute little smile.
"But how? I thought the Nightmare Chamber was supposed to help you," Camilla asked again, but Zaila just smiled.
"Indeed, the chamber helped me. But along the way, Zaila appeared, first as a baby, and during the 2,000 years I spent inside the chamber, she grew up with me and helped me through a lot of issues.
Basically, I don’t know how it happened, but she is my soul now, so yay." Zaila didn’t want to get into things now, but the ladies wouldn’t allow her.
"You were supposed to be inside the chamber for 23 years and a few months. Where are the 2,000 years coming from?" This time, Vexthra asked.
"I will only tell Kent," Zaila and her Primordial Spirit said, sticking out their tongues.
"This brat," Vexthra chuckled, knowing the truth would come out soon enough. But she seemed very happy for some reason.
And she should be. For someone to have a Primordial Spirit meant they had understood themselves and truly taken a deep dive into their soul, coming to terms with their true nature.
That is the first step in birthing a Primordial Spirit from a soul body.
So this meant Zaila hadn’t only overcome her trauma, but she had come to terms with it and chosen to accept that part of her, making it a part of who she is and who she would be from now on.
It sounded vague and easy, but even Vexthra still couldn’t form a Primordial Spirit after millions of years. This shows just how impressive Zaila is for having one.
However, Vexthra is happy because, knowing someone who now has a primordial spirit, who is even her sister, she knows there is hope for her and perhaps hope for her sisters.

"Sisters, you don’t have to worry. Zaila is my soul, and since she took the part of me I like to hide, we are the same person, but she can be unruly sometimes. She is my mind and soul; I’ve become a better me thanks to her.
You can’t have me without her, and she can be without me." Zaila smiled.

"Plus, she found a way to help you all awaken your own Primordial Spirits. Of course, I can’t guarantee success for all, but if you want to have a shot at defeating me in combat, then you must try your best."
"Brat, know when to brag. I am your master and a Root Ascension stage expert—what makes you think you can defeat me?" Camilla bragged, watching her disciple.

"That’s because she is also a Root Ascension stage expert. But while that is not too impressive, her Primordial Spirit is a Spirit Lord. Even Kent wouldn’t be able to defeat her if they worked together," Vexthra said.
"WHAT?!"
Zaila and her Primordial Spirit burst out laughing, holding their stomach...
"No need to look shocked, sisters. I lived in seclusion for 2,000-plus years, and during that time, I trained tirelessly, and my Primordial Spirit rose as high as the Heavenly Ascension stage.
She dropped to the Spirit Lord stage because she transferred her cultivation base to me. But even so, I don’t need her to defeat you all—even if you come at me together."
"Now you’re just asking for some beating." Neomi drew her weapon. However, Zaila just waved her hand, and her spear burst into dust.
"What?" The ladies were blown away again.

"This is my realm, ladies, and as someone whose mind has already reached the Spirit Lord stage—that is, Tier 18—I am basically a god here." The Primordial Spirit used sign language to translate the 18 for them, mocking the ladies.
"This is awesome," Unity, the overly supportive sister, said with a smile, walking toward the Primordial Spirit. When she got close, the Primordial Spirit squinted her eyes and smiled.
"You have dormant Primordial Spirits, too."
"Wait, spirits as in more than one?" Vexthra asked again, shocked this time too.
"Yes. She has two, to be exact." This time, the ladies turned and looked at Unity.
"Just what is happening?" Elsa asked, but the next second, the Primordial Spirit spoke.
"Now that I am paying close attention to you all, I can’t help but wonder—how are you, you, you, you, and you also having dormant Primordial Spirits?"
She pointed at Selene, Neomi, Elsa, Lilian, and Ingrid. The ladies looked puzzled, hearing her say that.
"That is because they have True Names," Vexthra answered, connecting the dots now that she had five variables to play with. However, upon hearing her answer, the Primordial Spirit became shocked.
"Wait, there are five people with True Names here? Just what kind of freaky family have we stepped into, Zaila?" she shouted, causing Zaila and the ladies to laugh.
"His name is Kent..." Zaila said, "Kent Madson. My man."
The ladies raised their eyebrows, hearing her bold words.
"Our man," they said in unison

"This is my realm, ladies, and as someone whose mind has already reached the Spirit Lord stage—that is, Tier 18—I am basically a god here." The Primordial Spirit used sign language to translate the 18 for them, mocking the ladies.
"This is awesome," Unity, the overly supportive sister, said with a smile, walking toward the Primordial Spirit.
When she got close, the Primordial Spirit squinted her eyes and smiled.
"You have dormant Primordial Spirits, too."
"Wait, spirits as in more than one?" Vexthra asked again, shocked this time too.
"Yes.
She has two, to be exact." This time, the ladies turned and looked at Unity.
"Just what is happening?" Elsa asked, but the next second, the Primordial Spirit spoke.
"Now that I am paying close attention to you all, I can’t help but wonder—how are you, you, you, you, and you also having dormant Primordial Spirits?"
She pointed at Selene, Neomi, Elsa, Lilian, and Ingrid.
The ladies looked puzzled, hearing her say that.
"That is because they have True Names," Vexthra answered, connecting the dots now that she had five variables to play with.
However, upon hearing her answer, the Primordial Spirit became shocked.
"Wait, there are five people with True Names here?
Just what kind of freaky family have we stepped into, Zaila?" she shouted, causing Zaila and the ladies to laugh.
"His name is Kent..." Zaila said, "Kent Madson.
My man."
The ladies raised their eyebrows, hearing her bold words.
"Our man," they said in unison

chapters.title: Chapter 539: True Names [Bonus]
paragraphs: "Wait a moment. All five of you have True Names... how is that possible?" Zaila’s Primordial Spirit asked, acting like an entity of its own.
This begs the question: just what is she?
The fact that she looked shocked means she clearly has her own reasoning, which suggests she is more than an entity formed from Zaila’s soul.
If that was the case, then the question should be: What is a Primordial Spirit, and what do they stand for?

They clearly have a mind of their own and can reason independently, even exhibiting all the signs of a person who has their own free will. This means there is a lot to unpack from the concept of Primordial Spirits.
First, however, the question must be answered.
"They have True Names, which were given to them by Kent," Vexthra answered. She knew something profound was happening here, and as the most intelligent among her sisters, she ought to know.
"There are five of them, and they received their True Names from a person. That is a first." In front of everyone, the Primordial Spirit waved her hand, and a book appeared—a rather large book.
"Does any of you know what this is?" she asked, making the book hover before their eyes. They all looked at it, but only Vexthra knew the answer.
"It is a manual containing spells from the Ancient Library. How do you have the Serpent Manual?" Vexthra asked after she answered.
The Serpent Manual is one of the oldest books in existence. It contains some of the original spells created by the first ever mind cultivator to appear in the universe, the Serpent Queen.

It was said that she created the infamous AquaLife Manual, a powerful technique that allows those who master it to harness the ability to summon powerful sea beasts with just a swing of their weapons.

She also created a powerful skill that, when used, allows the user to summon beasts hidden within the Dead Sea—said to hold creatures that escaped the destruction of the Primordial Era—to aid in combat.

All these skills and techniques are left in the Serpent manual, kept in the Ancient Library. Nobody, not even the immortals, can brag that they have ever seen its cover, yet here it was, hovering before Zaila’s Primordial Spirit.

"You ask where I got this book from. What if I were to tell you it belongs to me? Would you believe me?" The ladies turned to Vexthra, who seemed to be the only one with the brainpower to comprehend what was happening.
"If you are the owner of this book, then are you telling me you are the reincarnation of the Serpent Queen?" Vexthra asked, but the Primordial Spirit shook her head.
"I don’t know. I am just Zaila’s soul that has awakened in a spirit form. As to whether I am the Serpent Queen, that should be asked of Zaila. However, she also doesn’t know.
Still, I believe you already know the answer, and thanks to these five ladies, I now have the understanding I needed."
"Don’t tell me you think they are the reincarnations of their True Names," Vexthra said, raising her eyebrow.

"Then, how do you explain them having dormant Primordial Spirits? You have a True Name, but it’s not the one they have—meaning their True Names are the profound ones." She flipped the book open to a page.
"According to the records here, True Names aren’t something that can literally transform someone. However, can any of you tell me I’m lying?
When your True Name was awakened, you gained a bloodline, a unique cultivation path, skills and techniques that aren’t from this era, and even your physical appearance changed.
Tell me I’m lying."
The ladies looked at each other, but they couldn’t deny it. This meant what she said was indeed spot on, and they began to connect the dots.
"If that is the case, then does it mean our True Names are lives we once lived?" Elsa asked, and the Primordial Spirit nodded.
"I’m not one hundred percent sure, but there’s a high chance that’s the case. If so, then you five are monsters that must be feared."
"You’re exaggerating, lady. Zaila hasn’t awakened her True Name yet, but she basically has the means to solo us without even your help. How are we the monsters here?" Selene asked with a smirk.

"You still don’t get it, do you? The current you is already monstrous. You can fight those in realms above you, and judging by your forms and aura, I’d say you are nearing the first limit in your evolution path.
That’s something that can’t be achieved easily. However, even if that weren’t enough, you have a bloodline to enhance your prowess as you grow.

Then there’s the case where you have to awaken your Primordial Spirit. So tell me—if my theory is correct and I am indeed the reincarnation of the Serpent Queen, known as the Mother of Mind Cultivators, what kind of monster would I become?
More importantly, if you ladies are already under this impression, what would become of you when you awaken your True names?"
The ladies took a deep breath.
"Suddenly, I feel like we are much more impressive," Neomi joked, but Vexthra shook her head.

"The question on my mind now is: what kind of existence are we tied to? All of this is possible because of him. So, what kind of person is Kent?" she wondered, and her sisters couldn’t help but smile.
"He is our man, destined to dominate the universe one day. For now, we have to ensure he doesn’t carry all the burdens by himself," Unity said, and her sisters nodded.
"So are you two like the two-body problem? Which of you gets to sleep with Kent?" Selene, of course, changed the topic, asking the obvious.
The ladies glared at her, but they all wanted to know.
"Zaila and I are the same. I am her soul, so whatever she feels, I feel the same. We are not separate beings. I am just her soul that gained intelligence."
The ladies laughed.
"Does this mean we all can have Primordial Spirits the moment we get our True Names?" Val suddenly asked.
"Yes. I will coordinate with the one who created the Nightmare Chamber and turn it into a training space where you can awaken your Primordial Spirits."
"Great. At this rate, Kent will have freaks following him around." The ladies laughed. They left the mind space and went back to the garden to celebrate Zaila’s return.

chapters.title: Chapter 540: Become My Servant [Bonus]
paragraphs: A day had passed since Kent dropped the bomb on the Bloodveins. Not that they didn’t see it coming. Kent took them to the location of the spell, and from what they saw, they knew he wasn’t lying to them.
It would be tough to destroy it. And even if they did, the chances of things not escalating were unknown, meaning the spell could not be destroyed.
However, Kent gave them a solution, and while they would love to say he was robbing them, the offer wasn’t something they could ignore.
The fact that they would have a good place to live and even be closer to their god was something they couldn’t deny was enticing.
The only downside was that they would be giving away their precious Blood Heart Stone.
However, Kent wasn’t an unreasonable person. He knew they were going through a lot, so he proposed they put a pin in their discussion until after the battle.ree
This way, they would have no worries when making their decision.
So, after they came to that conclusion, Kent left with Velyra and helped her advance her chaos qi comprehension until she touched the wall, making her the third to achieve that.
"Thank you, Kent," she said with a smile.
"No need to thank me. My wives would pull my ear off if they knew I didn’t help a beauty in need." She smiled, making Velyra blush.
"Don’t flatter me, Kent. I know you’re just trying to make me feel good by calling me a beauty." Velyra turned away, not wanting to show her flustered expression.
"Oh please, do you look at yourself in the mirror? You are a beauty beyond measure." Naturally, she was insecure about her skin color being red.
Compared to Kent’s, she felt like she would stand out like a sore thumb when around those not sharing the same color as her.
Not that she was wrong. She would indeed stand out—but then, what about that? She would basically be unique in her own way. And Kent wasn’t one to make a lady sad, so he had to work his magic.

"Trust me, you being a different skin color will make many become jealous of you. I know this because your people don’t have variations like us humans, who have some with long ears, short legs, and stuff.
So, embrace your beauty and don’t let your head down. You are beautiful, and you should embrace that beauty and be proud."
"Really?" Velyra asked, turning toward him.
"Indeed. I don’t lie," Kent smiled.

"If you don’t lie, then tell me if you truly have the means to save my people. They are the only ones I have, and while I would love to move away to the other domains, that will cause our bloodline to decline.
So, can you really help us? I don’t mind giving you the Blood Heart Stone now if you can promise me." Kent was taken aback hearing her words.
’Looks like I touched her heart,’ Kent said to himself.

"I know you can tell if I’m lying, so tell me—am I lying?" Kent sighed and said, "I really do have a way to save your race and give them a good life. And I wasn’t lying about the fact that your god is where I will take you."
Velyra studied him for a few seconds before planting her face in his chest and starting to sob. Kent didn’t know why it had gotten to that, but he did his best to console her.
"Just relax for now. I will save your people, and then we can continue from there," Kent said, wiping her tears.
"Okay," Velyra nodded, a little embarrassed.
"Now, can you point me in the direction where the lady is imprisoned?" Kent asked, and Velyra nodded, taking him to the prison entrance.
"I will be back soon." She nodded, and Kent walked inside.
Deep inside the cave, the hunter, who was fortunate enough to be healed by the Tribe Chief, was seated with her right leg bound by a thick chain.
Her body was still aching, but she would live. Naturally, her soul was also wounded, considering all her undead were killed, and she wouldn’t be able to raise them from the dead anymore.
Basically, she would want to die now, but the universe and the tower had other plans. To them, life had just begun when she met Kent.
"Looks like you never anticipated being a pawn in the schemes of the Hand and the Oracles."
The hunter, who was regretting her decision to come after Kent, suddenly heard a familiar voice, causing her to stand and turn to her right.
"It’s you," she muttered, a little afraid of Kent.
"In the flesh. Why, did you miss me?" Kent asked with a cheeky smile, staring at her angered expression.
"I bet you’re in deep trouble now. Why, you never stopped to consider that you’re just a pawn being used by the Hand." Kent couldn’t help laughing.
"What do you want?" the annoyed hunter asked, knowing she wasn’t really in the form to become aggressive.
"I have the means to kill you now, considering you came to kill me. However, I have a different idea."
"And that is?"
"Become my servant."
"What if I said no?" the hunter asked.

"Very simple, really. I will turn around and leave. But before leaving, I’ll point out that a battle will happen soon. Right after, the people living in this domain will migrate from here because their land is dying.
Naturally, you will be left here, in which case you’ll die in ten years after the land withers."
"Why do you want me to become your servant? I am your enemy—you should kill me instead." The hunter didn’t understand why Kent wanted her to be his servant. It just didn’t make sense.

"Trust me, I have no idea, too. However, my sugarmommy wants me to make you my servant, so I must listen. Now, do you want to? And before you think it, I don’t like slavery, so you will have your free will."
The hunter thought hard about the offer, but in the end, she accepted it. She hated Kent, but now, she hates the hand and the oracles even more.
So seeing a chance present itself, she took it, even if that chance meant becoming a servant to the most hateful brat she had ever met in her 450 years of existence.
⟪Congratulations. You have received a new servant. Name: Yi Lai⟫
⟪Trust Meter: 22%⟫
⟪Do you want to bestow the Dragon Necromancy class to her?⟫
Kent shook his head. The gift for taking her as his servant was a unique class called Dragon Necromancy. Basically, she can only have dragon undeads in her undead legion.
Kent knew this was something the tower and the universe came together and cooked up, but he was impressed by the unique nature of this class.
"Here you go, Yi Lai. This is my first gift to you," Kent said, opening his palm. A skull-shaped orb flew out and entered her forehead.
She fell back and passed out. Kent waved his hand, and her body vanished into the tower, appearing inside the Servant Tower.
With that settled, he left the underground prison and started preparing for the invasion.

chapters.title: Chapter 541: The Invasion (1) [Bonus]
paragraphs: Just like that, the days went by, and before long, the day of the invasion came.

Kent hadn’t slept for the past three days since he was stacking attacks using the Fractured Void skill. That particular skill he learned during his time in the Gaze Enlightenment was one that he held in high regard.
It allows him to load attacks into the Void, and then, at his convenience, he can unleash them. Initially, he could only stack up attacks for 24 hours.
However, he spent 100,000 skill points to upgrade it from Mythic to Immortal grade. This allowed him to stack attacks for two whole weeks in advance.
For the past three days, Kent had been stacking attacks, only stopping when his energy was depleted. But three days was a long time for someone to stack attacks.
In the end, he had stacked the second form of the Annihilation Sword Technique 5,000 times—meaning he could open the void and rain down attacks on the army like it was a typical Tuesday.
But that wasn’t the only skill he stacked. He used the [Elemental Lord] skill to stack thousands of different forms of flame beasts, with the smallest being 3 meters in height.
That skill allows him to unleash an attack by manipulating his elements. He used his Blue Void Flame this time to ensure the skill was utilized perfectly.
He also used the first form of the Nine Calamities Sword Strike to stack more attacks.
Kent didn’t want to waste time on this mission, so he planned on getting it done quickly. Eliminating half of the major threats would easily weaken them.
As for the rest of the army, he pitied them. He knew the moment he weakened the alliance force, the Bloodvein army would slaughter the rest.
"This is enough. I better get going now," Kent said, jumping down from a 200-meter-tall mountain. He landed softly on the ground where Velyra was waiting for him.
Kent raised his eyebrows when he saw her.
"You look..."
"Different," she said, making Kent nod. Velyra was out of her baggy gown, now clad in dark armor with a sword strapped to her back.

Her armor was an elegant mix of danger and finesse, especially with her skull-shaped shoulder pads. She looked truly different, and while Kent didn’t want to make it obvious, looking at her shape in those leather trousers made him want to admire her even more.
"I am a warrior, Kent. It’s just that when there’s no battle to fight, I prefer to live a peaceful life as a priestess."
"I see. In any case, I think you look good in the armor," Kent said, not hiding his admiration.
"Thank you. Now, let’s go. They’re waiting for us." They quickly left the training ground and headed to the meeting hall, which also served as the throne room.
"Kent, this is General Xant. He will be leading the warriors." The Tribe Chief, Malthar, introduced a thick, tall man whose features screamed hammer wielder.
He was at peak Core Formation with four evolutions under his belt, so he was capable of leading. Kent nodded in his direction before speaking.
"I used the communication token given to me by Prince Ebert. According to him, they are five hours out, meaning we have less than that to get into position.
Not that it’ll be needed much. From what I gathered, they have some secrets up their sleeve that are giving them confidence.
This means my main objective here is to make them reveal that secret even before the battle starts."
"And how do you intend to do that?" General Xant asked.
"Simple. I will command them to reveal it," Kent answered with a smile that made General Xant turn to look at the Tribe Chief. However, seeing that he wasn’t saying anything, he turned back to Kent.
"Let’s say you manage to make them reveal their secret. What then would you do?" General Xant asked.
"Again, very simple. I’ve already made preparations to handle five Core Formation experts from the enemy side and a few Sovereigns.
Now, I don’t know about the Soulshroud Tribe’s side, but I’m prepared to easily kill at least two elders of the Dreadclaw Tribe, their prince, his guards, and the leaders of their units.
The Soulshroud Tribe might prove stubborn because, from the information I gathered, they’re the masterminds behind this invasion.
This means the secret is with them. So after I handle the people I named, I’ll take their chief out of the equation. You can handle the rest."
"If you can really do what you said, then I believe we can handle the rest, even if the minor tribes join them. My only issue now is whether or not you can live up to your claims."
It wasn’t that he didn’t trust Kent; it was more that he didn’t want to have false hope. If Kent failed them, they would be in deep trouble.
"Don’t worry, General. I wasn’t sent here to put your life in danger. I will do my part, and hopefully, you can do your part too."
The general and the elders nodded.
"If all goes well, the battle will be over in under an hour, so let’s all prepare to celebrate afterwards." The elders laughed at his words.
"Priestess, I will require your assistance, so you will move with me. In that case, let’s meet on the battlefront." Kent stood up and left with Velyra.
"Can we bet on him, Chief?" General Xant asked.
"Our priestess trusts him, so we have to trust our priestess. Also, he is the envoy of the Mother of Killers, so let’s wait and see what magic he can make."
The general nodded and also left. The warriors were already at the border waiting for the enemy.

Kent and Velyra flew toward the battlefield where the 7,000 Bloodvein warriors were waiting. When they arrived, Kent found a tree and sat down, displaying a calm, nonchalant demeanor—unlike the Bloodveins, who looked nervous.
His nonchalant display made the warriors look at him with puzzled expressions. However, Kent didn’t even bother to change his posture.
Thus, a few hours later, the enemy arrived with an army five times the size of the Bloodveins. Instinctively, the Bloodveins began to panic.

Kent hadn’t slept for the past three days since he was stacking attacks using the Fractured Void skill.
That particular skill he learned during his time in the Gaze Enlightenment was one that he held in high regard.
It allows him to load attacks into the Void, and then, at his convenience, he can unleash them.
Initially, he could only stack up attacks for 24 hours.
However, he spent 100,000 skill points to upgrade it from Mythic to Immortal grade.
This allowed him to stack attacks for two whole weeks in advance.
For the past three days, Kent had been stacking attacks, only stopping when his energy was depleted.
But three days was a long time for someone to stack attacks.

He used the [Elemental Lord] skill to stack thousands of different forms of flame beasts, with the smallest being 3 meters in height.
That skill allows him to unleash an attack by manipulating his elements.
He used his Blue Void Flame this time to ensure the skill was utilized perfectly.
He also used the first form of the Nine Calamities Sword Strike to stack more attacks.
Kent didn’t want to waste time on this mission, so he planned on getting it done quickly.

chapters.title: Chapter 542: The Invasion (2) [Bonus]
paragraphs: The alliance army numbered over thirty thousand, while the Bloodvein army was slightly above seven thousand.
Naturally, their instinctive fear kicked in, so they started to panic.
However, Kent just sat calmly in the air, watching the incredibly large army march toward them, their evil intent visible in their eyes.

"Looks like every last one of them is committed to this battle," Kent said to himself with a sigh. "What a pity. I would have been slightly merciful. But looking at your intent, it’s best I put you down."

Thus, Kent continued to watch as the army approached and stopped a kilometer from them. The moment they halted, the tribe chiefs and elders, alongside their generals from the Dreadclaw and Soulshroud tribes, stepped forward.
On the Bloodvein side, Tribe Chief Malthar and the elders also stepped forward. Kent, who was seated on a branch, saw Velyra preparing to move forward, so he gave her the go-ahead.
"You can go. I will be right behind you." Velyra nodded and vanished, appearing beside her father. They moved a few meters forward and stopped, maintaining a distance of 900 meters between them.
Though that didn’t really do much, all still heard their voices.
"Tribe Chief Malthar, we gave you enough time to hand over what we demanded, but it seems you chose death," Tribe Chief Rokar of the Dreadclaw tribe said, looking smugly at the Bloodveins.
"Who are you kidding, Rokar? I know you’re rotten, but I never expected you to be rotten to the core. How can you let these soul animals pull you into their scheme?
Did that little brain of yours do any thinking to realize this won’t end well for you?"
Kent, who was up in the tree, mouthed the word "Damn" after hearing Tribe Chief Malthar’s words.
The fight hadn’t started yet, but he had already scored a damn. His words were both harsh and a reality check for the Dreadclaw tribe, but it seemed they didn’t really want to listen.
"Whether we are mere weapons in this invasion or not, at the end of the day, you will be the one crying," Tribe Chief Rokar said.
Tribe Chief Malthar shook his head and locked eyes with Tribe Chief Calthar, the chief of the Soulshroud tribe.
"I never pegged you for being a schemer, Calthar."
Tribe Chief Calthar smirked. "Your end has come, Malthar. I don’t have to tell you how happy I am about that."

The Soulshroud Tribe’s people have translucent, pale skin that glows faintly in the dark, giving them an ethereal, ghost-like appearance. Their eyes are black, with many possessing no pupils or irises at all.
They all have this ghostlike appearance, making them appear very dangerous. Kent raised his brow when he sensed something from the side of the Soulshroud army.

"As expected of a soul tribe, they have things to protect their souls from even a Tier 11 soul attack." Kent sensed that the two elders, despite being at Tier 10, had soul items protecting them from even attacks from him.
A young man, who was undoubtedly the prince, also had the same item protecting him.
"Not that it mattered. They will die, and that is final," Kent smirked.
As for Tribe Chief Calthar, his soul was Tier 11, so Kent knew he had found the danger—or perhaps the first danger-that must be eliminated if the Bloodvein wanted any chance of winning.
Chief Malthar looked at the Alliance army as if sizing them up. He then shifted his attention back to the tribe chiefs of the two major clans.
"Tell me, what did they offer you two to go as far as helping them cast a Tier 13 spell that is eroding both my domain and bloodline? What could they have possibly given you?"
This time, the two tribe chiefs frowned upon hearing what Chief Malthar said.
"You think we wouldn’t know, huh? We know of your plans and what this means for my people. Naturally, I was shocked to learn that people we called neighbors could be this cruel.
However, it doesn’t matter, because after today, you two will be dead, and your people will have no leaders to guide or protect them.
And knowing the dangerous nature of this region, you two have doomed your people."
"Oh? And what gave you the confidence to say that? In ten years, you all would be dead unless you submit to us?" Tribe Chief Calthar said.
"You are dead meat, Malthar," Tribe Chief Rokar added.
"What if I say no to that? Would you two perhaps straighten up and leave?" Kent suddenly appeared in the air, looking smugly at the two tribe chiefs.
"And you are?" they asked.

"You can just call me a concerned human who doesn’t like minding his own business. Now, I’m going to ask again: what if I said no to your arrogance? Are you going to retreat and never return here again?"
"Never!" both tribe chiefs shouted, glaring coldly at the foreigner who had appeared.
Kent smiled and turned his head, locking eyes with Prince Ebert.
"You are Ebert, right?" he asked.
"I don’t answer to lowly humans like you," Prince Ebert said, pointing his left hand at Kent. He had killed quite a few unfortunate humans who had found themselves in the Dead Region.
So, to him, he had just found another human to torture. If only he knew death was smiling at his stupidity.
Kent shook his head, hearing Prince Ebert’s words.
"In that case, why don’t you obey this?" Kent flashed an evil smile that made the princes tremble in their hearts.
"Drop dead." Kent snapped his fingers, and like a mango falling from a branch, the prince dropped dead. One moment he was standing—then the next, he collapsed lifelessly.
The faces of everyone turned pale at the sight. However, before anyone could react, Kent pointed at two Batkins.
"You can join your master in the afterlife." He snapped his fingers again, causing the two Peak Sovereigns to drop dead without any resistance.
The sudden death of three people from the Dreadclaw tribe sent a wave of panic through the alliance army.
They didn’t know how it happened, but looking at the three bodies on the ground, it became painfully clear—they were in deep trouble.
All eyes turned to Kent, but when they saw his smile, their hearts trembled.
"Who are you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 543: The Invasion (3) [Bonus]
paragraphs: "I already told you who I am. You just chose not to listen. In any case, don’t blame me for being cruel, but I think we all know cruelty went out the window when you helped cast a Tier 13 spell that is slowly killing your own neighbors."
Kent’s gaze turned cold.
"I know humans can be cruel, but I never expected a small group such as yourselves to be this evil." He then turned and looked at two elders from the Dreadclaw clan.
"You two can drop dead too." With a snap of his fingers, the two elders could only clench their chests before dropping to their deaths.
"It’s only fair I share the death among the tribe." Kent turned to one elder from the Soulshroud tribe and their army general, the only two not wearing a Tier 11 soul protection artifact.
"Death is calling you two." Their tribe chief tried to defend them, but Kent had long planted the soul bomb, so it was useless.
He didn’t stay back when he told Velyra to go join her father for nothing. Those few seconds were spent planting soul bombs.
"Alliance, charge and kill them all!" Tribe Chief Rokar, who had lost a son and two elders, became furious and ordered his tribe warriors to charge forward.
However, before General Xant of the Bloodvein tribe could give an order to his soldiers, Kent raised his hand and snapped his fingers.
His eyes shone, and like the coming of the apocalypse, the void shattered and thousands of sword arcs rained down, decimating the ranks of the army that charged forward.
"No need to be in a rush. I have more where that came from." The alliance army came to a sudden stop, panic and fear setting in.

"You’d better take out your secret weapon that was meant to guarantee your victory, or else the next wave of attacks will reduce your ranks to half," Kent said, looking smugly at the two tribe chiefs.
He really expected them to do that. However, to his shock, they didn’t.
"In that case, don’t blame me."
Kent snapped his fingers again, and this time, the attacks that came were multiplied using the [Thousand Blade Refraction] skill.
This caused his hundred attacks to multiply into thousands. When the attack was released, Kent felt a large chunk of his energy drain.
The two tribe chiefs tried to defend, but they could only do so much. By the time all the attacks landed, close to fifteen thousand soldiers had died.
"This is..." Even the Bloodvein tribe was shaken, watching the devastation unfold before their eyes. They never expected a single person to be this destructive.
If only they knew this was Kent being merciful.
He could have killed all of them, considering the three days he spent weren’t wasted. He had been planning well, and all the attacks he stacked were imbued with Chaos Qi.
This meant even the Peak Sovereigns were but little flowers in front of his attacks. They had little resistance against it, and knowing Kent, he had made sure there were no mistakes.
"Tribe Chief Malthar, I’ll leave that brute to you. Be careful, though—he has a powerful soul weapon." Kent blinked and appeared a few meters from Tribe Chief Calthar.
"Why don’t you show me what you’re hiding?" Kent kicked forward, landing a powerful punch on the tribe chief that sent him flying.
At the same time, Tribe Chief Malthar also attacked, clashing with Tribe Chief Rokar, who was seething with rage.
"Bloodvein army, slaughter them all!" General Xant commanded, raising his weapon. "For the Mother of Killers!"
"For the Mother of Killers!"
They charged forward and clashed with the army from the alliance, whose ranks had been decimated and whose formations were completely broken.
Taking advantage of that, they stormed into the weakened ranks and began slaughtering them.
Elder Ureth clashed with an elder from the Soulshroud tribe who was a weapon refiner. The enemy took out ten weapons and started controlling them to attack.
However, thanks to Kent’s opening, the brute elder was on fire as he charged at the weapons, sending them flying. He knew his job was to kill that elder, and he focused entirely on doing just that.

Elder Ferra also clashed with another weapon refiner who used daggers instead. However, upon closer inspection, those daggers had been refined with thousands of souls, making them more dangerous than even a Peak Sovereign.
Elder Zarka, on the other hand, was clashing with Elder Vak from the Dreadclaw tribe. He was the last remaining elder, considering Kent had already killed the other two.
Meanwhile, Velyra was locked in combat with the prince of the Soulshroud tribe. He was also a Core Formation expert who had completed three evolutions.
Their battle prowess was matched, and considering his weapon was a mystical-grade soul sword, he was packing severe attacks.
However, Velyra wasn’t worried. She had more control over Chaos Qi than the prince, so she knew she could handle him.
Tribe Chief Rokar had already transformed into his full beast form, taking the shape of a 12-meter-tall panther with silver fur.

All members of the royal bloodline of the Dreadclaw clan are silver panthers, so he had taken that form. And thanks to him wielding his full strength, Tribe Chief Malthar found himself facing a mountain.

However, he wasn’t the leader of the Bloodvein tribe for nothing. His combat power was something that could not be ignored. He was essentially an overpowered warrior who wielded both blood and chaos energy.
His close combat abilities are impeccable.
Kent had always wondered why Malthar had three eyes instead of two like everyone else. Today, the answer has become clear.
The third eye allowed him to see a few seconds into the future. So, despite the overwhelming strength of his opponent, he always seemed to be one step ahead of Tribe Chief Rokar.
Though he couldn’t use it continuously, using it occasionally was proving to be a tremendous advantage.
General Xant, on the other hand, was leading his army to decimate the ranks of the alliance forces, causing some even to begin fleeing.
He used just a single attack to kill the General from the Dreadclaw army. It was a mistake on that general’s part for freezing when he should have been decisive.
This gave General Xant the chance to charge toward even those fleeing.
Knowing that the cause of their land’s decay was this very alliance, the Bloodvein warriors weren’t letting them escape so easily.
With their leaders being held back, it was only a matter of time before the alliance army was completely leaderless.

He used just a single attack to kill the General from the Dreadclaw army.
It was a mistake on that general’s part for freezing when he should have been decisive.
This gave General Xant the chance to charge toward even those fleeing.
Knowing that the cause of their land’s decay was this very alliance, the Bloodvein warriors weren’t letting them escape so easily.
With their leaders being held back, it was only a matter of time before the alliance army was completely leaderless.

chapters.title: Chapter 544 - 10,000 Soul Flag [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent and Tribe Chief Calthar clashed, creating a shockwave strong enough to overwhelm those at the Transcendent level and below.

Their attacks weren’t simple at all. Kent was using his bare fists, as the tribe chief was doing the same. However, that didn’t mean the tribe chief was having it easy, despite undergoing five complete evolutions.
The moment one undergoes even a single evolution, their prowess rises to a stage that an ordinary peak Core Formation cultivator can’t handle.

However, Kent, who was only at the third level of the Root Ascension stage, was overwhelming him in physical combat. The reason behind this was that he was both a dragon and someone who had broken a limit on himself.
Breaking a limit is not something one can easily do. There are gods who haven’t even broken three limits yet. However, Kent had already broken one and was on track to break the second.
That alone was enough to place him at a level the tribe chief, despite undergoing five core evolutions, couldn’t comprehend.
"Just who are you, and what are you made of?" After getting punched in his translucent face, he spat out dark blood and asked.
"I’m just a concerned friend who can’t bear to see this person in danger. Just like how you helped cast such a nasty spell on those you called neighbors, I am helping them slaughter you scums"
"Do you know what you’re playing with? I don’t know where you came from, but messing with something you know nothing about won’t end well for you."
"Don’t worry. The fact that the person behind you hasn’t appeared yet means they can’t appear now. At most, I have one month to run from here and be gone before they show up."
Kent raised his hand, causing hundreds of doom shards to burst from the ground, blasting into the defense of Tribe Chief Calthar.
"And what makes you think the Bloodvein Tribe won’t be obliterated after you’re gone? Even if they take our domain, they’ll just be sheep waiting to be slaughtered."
"But you’ll be dead, so why worry about that?" The void cracked open exactly one kilometer away, letting out a powerful sword attack.
It was the Void Cleave attack, and using the 1km distance, the attack landed hard on the defense, sending the tribe chief flying.
Kent appeared behind him and landed a powerful kick that sent him flying farther. The tribe soldiers who saw this just couldn’t believe their eyes.
However, Kent wasn’t paying attention to them, since he knew the tribe chief wasn’t that physically strong. However, his soul was even more robust than his.
Thankfully, Kent was immune to soul attacks, so it wasn’t like all the soul attacks coming his way could do anything to him.
Tribe Chief Calthar wasn’t having the best time either.
He was being pushed into a corner because his soul attacks weren’t working, and his physical prowess wasn’t much to speak of. Naturally, the outcome of the battle was already determined.
However, that didn’t last long. Suddenly, a three-meter-wide flag appeared in the air and unleashed a powerful aura that pushed Kent back, sending him flying toward the ground.
"A soul flag." Kent immediately recognized it and frowned. He instinctively created a soul wall around himself and the tribe chief, preventing the soul energy coming from the flag from spreading out.
He then called out to Velyra.
"Velyra, move your battle back now!" He wasn’t even done speaking when a large skull emerged from the flag and let out a powerful howl, assaulting everyone’s ears.
Thankfully, the soul wall blocked most of the sound, so aside from a few nose bleeds, nobody died.
Kent narrowed his eyes at the skull, which turned and looked directly at him.
"This is a 10,000-soul flag we received from our benefactor. Do you now understand what is happening here? You’ve caused the doom of everyone.
They could have survived this if they had just handed over that damn Blood Heart Stone and that bitch. Now, they’ll become meat for my Skull."
Tribe Chief Calthar raised his head and laughed, his voice echoing through the air, drawing everyone’s attention toward him.
When their eyes landed on the skull, whose eyes were burning red and erratic, they all gulped and instinctively stepped back.
Kent, however, stood frozen, staring at the soul flag with a curious gaze. It felt familiar, not in the sense that he had once owned it, but more in how the skull had been created.
For a moment, he felt like he could do it—like he had done this thousands of times before. That only made him question where he knew it from.
’Jest is a swordsman. There’s no way he could do this. Which means... this is from my own past self. But that’s not important right now. I just have to crush this man’s dreams and aspirations first.’
"Very impressive of you to have something this dangerous. Though that skull can be comparable to a Tier 12 soul cultivator, I’m not afraid of it simply because soul attacks don’t work on me.
And you don’t have enough soul essence to unleash its true power.
That is why I can easily do this."

Kent moved, and he was in front of the skull the next second. Before the tribe chief could do anything, he walked into the skull and, like the unruly bastard he was, released his lightning, fire, and soul energy.
Instead of howling, the skull now screamed as a powerful energy exploded inside it, shattering it in thousands of ways.
Before Tribe Chief Calthar could send it back inside to heal, Kent released another soul attack, completely destroying it.
The soul flag hovering in the air turned from deep red to pure white, signaling that the 10,000 souls used in creating the skull had perished.
"What have you done?" Tribe Chief Calthar asked, faltering in his steps. However, Kent didn’t answer. Instead, he blinked and appeared before him, snatching something from around his neck.
With a chuckle, Kent distanced himself before putting the item away.
Tribe Chief Calthar looked around his neck and realized his soul defense artifact had been taken. "You damn bastard!" His fury exploded, and he unleashed his soul essence into a devastating attack.
However, when it struck Kent, he just stood there smiling.
"Like I said, soul attacks don’t work on me. Now, be ready to die." His sword appeared in his hand, and with a quick swing, it was back in the sheath the next second.
However, up ahead, the tribe chief, who couldn’t easily be killed, lost his head, which hit the ground with a powerful thud.
Just like that, he had died, not knowing how it happened.

chapters.title: Chapter 545: Let Them Go [Bonus]
paragraphs: The moment Tribe Chief Calthar dropped dead, the alliance was broken.
"The chief is dead, run."

Without any hesitation, the soldiers still alive decided to run for their dear lives. The fact that they lost even before the battle began was clear as day to them, so they did not need a second opinion from anyone to tell them they were fucked.
Kent turned and looked in the direction where Tribe Chief Malthar was facing the tribe chief of the Dreadclaw tribe.
"Looks like they indeed are the strongest. I’d better make them even stronger now so they can help me in the future," Kent said, watching as the silver panther was now bathed in red.
Kent couldn’t help shaking his head.
He turned toward the direction of Elder Farra and saw that the old woman had her whip around the neck of her opponent. With a quick pull, his head came off, landing on the floor with a thud.
Then something unique happened.

The whip jumped into the severed neck, and all the blood from the body of her opponent was sucked into the whip. Kent immediately appraised the whip, and what he saw made him question where she got the weapon.
⟦Name: Blood Eater Whip⟧
⟦Grade: Legendary⟧
⟦Quality: SS Rank⟧
⟦Abilities: 2 Active | 3 Passive⟧

⟦Description: An ordinary whip that can be nurtured using the blood of those it slays. The more blood it drinks, the more powerful it becomes. Feeding it the blood of those stronger can evolve both the grade and quality.⟧
"I think Sylara is going to like this lady." With a smile, Kent turned to Elder Ureth, who had also ended his battle, but his body was littered with wounds—some shallow, some deep.
He was a brute who faced off against a weapon refiner who could use his mind to control the weapon and maintain his distance. It was only natural that he struggled to defeat him.

But the endgame justifies the means, so he won and was now absorbing the blood of the one he killed. Elder Zarka was also the same, considering that the enemy was already running when they ended their battles.
They were not needed, and in battle, it is best if the strongest do not rush into everything immediately. Nobody knew where a surprise was hiding or when it would appear, so they stayed back.
General Xant and Velyra were doing all the killing. She had already ended her battle in under five minutes, so she was currently slaughtering the Root Sovereigns who held no candle to her.
In fact, the Bloodvein were showing great prowess that made Kent wonder if they really needed his help.
However, remembering he ended most of the Core Formation experts and even removed the danger from the board, he knew they were impressive, but not on the level of his legion.
After a while, Tribe Chief Malthar managed to bring down his opponent, who turned back to his demi-human form and looked at Tribe Chief Malthar with a fearful gaze.

"Don’t do this, Malthar. We’ve known each other for close to a thousand years. Don’t do this," Tribe Chief Rokar cried out, but looking into the three red eyes watching him, he knew his cry wasn’t doing anything.
"It’s because we’ve known each other for so long that I won’t be slaughtering your entire tribe. However, you will die today." Tribe Chief Malthar raised his axe and looked coldly at him.
"You will regret this, Malthar. In a week, you will know who you’ve offended." In his desperate cry, he gave the tribe chief a timeframe.
"See you on the other side, Rokar." With that, his head came off clean.
"I will take the body, thank you," Kent appeared in the air above and said to Tribe Chief Malthar.
"Go ahead." He didn’t even bother to ask what he wanted it for. Kent sent the body and head into his Necro Forge.
He then turned to the rest of the Core Formation dead bodies, but they had been drained, so he let them be.
"What are you going to do? Will you chase after them?" Kent asked, watching the thousands of alliance soldiers running.
"No. We’ll let them go," Tribe Chief Malthar said. "We have already killed the main culprits, and it’s not like we can take over their domain.
Also, we have lost ours, and per his last words, the one responsible will be coming in a week’s time. That is already a reason to prepare fast and leave."
"Does that mean you have accepted my offer?" Kent asked.
"Yes. However, if it turns out to be a lie, then pardon my words, but we will not hesitate to use every means to bring you down."
Kent smiled, hearing him. He didn’t want to tell them, but if he were allowed to bring his legion, the Bloodvein tribe wouldn’t have lifted even a single finger.
But they can have their moment now, and perhaps, if it makes them feel better, they can brag and say they could bring him down.
After the last alliance soldier left, the elders, General Xant, and Velyra moved toward Kent and the tribe chief.
"As promised, victory is yours," Kent said.
"Thank you, Kent. You really have helped us greatly," General Xant said, now seeing Kent as someone he could put his bet on. Naturally, the elders also held the same expressions now.
"I just did what I was told to do. No need to thank me," Kent said with a small smile.
"Does that mean you will be leaving soon?" General Xant asked, but Kent didn’t immediately answer. He turned to Tribe Chief Malthar.
"Let’s go back first."
Kent, the elders, General Xant, and Velyra nodded as they flew toward the tribe.
Meanwhile, the soldiers in the Bloodvein army were cheering and celebrating their victory over the alliance. Every single one of them didn’t know if they would come out alive.
However, now that they were the winners, they couldn’t help but celebrate their win.
Kent and the elders entered the throne room for one last discussion, considering they had a major migration to make in the next few days.
"Before we begin, tell us more about where you want to take us."
